# Docker Manager phase 3 (live) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Live data in the Docker Manager: lists that update from Engine events, CPU and memory sparklines, host gauges for CPU, RAM and Docker's disk usage, a follow log for a container, a stack and an external compose project, and a terminal into any container on any registered host (local, TCP, TLS, mTLS, SSH).

**Architecture:** A new package `internal/dockerwatch` runs one events watcher per host while somebody needs it (reconnect with backoff, resync, a list-poll fallback when `/events` is refused), samples stats only for the containers the UI shows (3 s, rings of 60) and for the rail gauges (10 s), caches `/system/df`, bounds streaming Engine connections per host, and follows container and project logs (new project containers are attached from the watcher's `start` events). `internal/server` exposes it as one SSE stream per desktop client with replaceable subscriptions, three log-follow SSE routes, a disk-usage route and a terminal WebSocket that reuses the protocol and serve loop of the existing container terminal over the host's own transport. The desktop app gets a stream client, log and terminal panels (xterm), SVG sparklines and gauges, and turns its 5 s poll into a 60 s safety poll while the stream is live.

**Tech Stack:** Go (raw `net/http` to the Engine API through `dockerutil`, hijacked exec stream, `github.com/gorilla/websocket`), Server-Sent Events, vanilla JS desktop modules, xterm.js 6 with the fit addon (vendored), SVG, design tokens in CSS, Node VM tests, go-rod browser tests.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-docker-manager-design.md` (phase 3; aligned with this plan's decisions in the same commit). Earlier plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-docker-manager-phase1-foundation.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-docker-manager-phase2-stacks.md`. Out of scope here (phase 4): image update check, notifications, registry credentials, images/volumes/networks actions, cleanup, adopt; (phase 5) the `docker_stacks` agent tool, AI help, templates.

## How to execute

- **Worktree:** `.worktrees/docker-manager-p3` on a new branch `docker-manager-p3` from local `main`. Other sessions commit to `main` in the main checkout; land the branch by rebase plus `git merge --ff-only`, or with the app's `sync_with_base_branch`.
- **Order:** Part A → Part B → Part C. Part D (UI) codes against the API contract with a fake API and needs none of A–C, so it may run in parallel with them (its own worktree/branch, merged before the final sweep); run its browser tests again after the merge. Inside a part, tasks run in order.
- **Base:** the code was drafted on `a80113379`. Edit blocks quote exact old text; where `main` moved and an old text no longer matches, re-read the file and apply the same change (report it as a deviation).
- **GitNexus:** before editing an existing function, run the impact step the task lists. The index is stale and often does not resolve Go functions or the desktop scripts (`reference_gitnexus_index_gaps`); then the listed `git grep` is the caller check. `--repo` takes the absolute path `C:\Users\Andi\Documents\repo\AuraGo`. Run `detect-changes` before each commit; for new files "No symbols mapped" is expected.
- **Go cache:** `GOCACHE=D:\dev-cache\go-build`, `GOTMPDIR=D:\tmp\go-build` (backslash form). If a build fails with "not enough space on the disk", trim `D:\dev-cache\go-build` entries older than 3 days (fall back to 1 day) and clear `D:\tmp\go-build` before retrying. Run `internal/dockerwatch`, `internal/dockerstacks` and `internal/server` tests in one process at a time.
- **Lean testing (user preference):** the tests in this plan plus one test per bug fixed on the way. One combined review per batch of tasks; Critical and Important findings only.
- **Preserved behaviour:** `/containers`, `/api/containers` (incl. its terminal and logs), the SSE `container_update` poll, `/events`, the `docker` agent tool, Invasion and every phase 1/2 Docker Manager route keep working as before. The only changes to existing code: `dockerutil.Client` keeps its dial function (A1); `dockerstacks` notifies an observer on state changes (A6); the existing terminal's serve loop moved into a variant with options, the old function calls it with none (B7); `engineFailure` and `removeAllowed` are split into a classifier and a writer, and a shared protection check (C1, C4); the container `logs` route gains `follow=1` (C3); `terminal` is routed (C4); the UI's one-shot log view is replaced by the follow panel and external projects open a pane (D3–D8).
- **Live acceptance (after Part C):** run the gated live tests of Tasks A7 and B6 (`AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1`) against local Docker Desktop (if it is running) and, with the user's OK, against aurago-test. They create throw-away containers named `aurago-dw-live-*` from the pinned runner image (`dockerstacks.RunnerImage`; pull it first if the engine lacks it and remove it afterwards when it was not there before) and remove only those; existing containers, apps and data are never touched (`feedback_test_server_scope`). They confirm what no fake can: the real `/events` line format and that its headers are flushed at once, the stats JSON on cgroup v1/v2 and `one-shot`, `tail=N&since=T` and `tail=0&follow=1`, an exec round trip over the host transport. Then `go test -race ./internal/dockerwatch/ ./internal/dockerhost/ ./internal/dockerstacks/` and the Docker Manager server tests under `-race` on aurago-test (recipe in `reference_aurago_test_server`: ship the committed package dirs, `GOTOOLCHAIN` per `go.mod`, `CGO_ENABLED=1`, a dead `DOCKER_HOST`).
- **How the drafts were checked:** each part was implemented in its own scratch worktree and checked there; the code blocks are copies of the code that passed, rendered by scripts, not retyped. Part A (on `a80113379`): one commit per task, `go vet` and `go test` of `dockerutil`, `dockerhost`, `dockerstacks` and `dockerwatch` per commit, a replay of every block that reproduced all 8 commits byte for byte, 60 repeated runs of the watch tests. Part B (on `a80113379` with a stub of Part A's surface, then checked again on Part A's real code): one commit per task, a replay of every block RED → GREEN byte for byte, the existing terminal tests unchanged. Part C (on Part A + Part B): a replay of every task RED → GREEN, the whole tree equal to the verified one, the full `internal/server` package with only the known failure. Part D (on `a80113379`): per task the Node test and the Go guards, `npm run check:ui`, from D8 on four browser tests in headless Chrome, a replay byte for byte, a screenshot review in a dark and a light theme. Not run while planning: the race detector (no gcc on the planning machine) and anything against a real Engine.

## Decisions taken while planning

1. **No Docker SDK;** streaming requests (events, log follow, exec) use a client without a total timeout, bounded by their context.
2. **Remote terminal:** the hijacked `POST /exec/{id}/start` is dialled through the host's own transport (`dockerutil.Client.Dial`) with the negotiated API version, so TLS, mTLS and SSH hosts work. Same WebSocket protocol and serve loop as `/api/containers/{id}/terminal`; the new route adds a 1 MiB frame limit and a 30 s ping (75 s pong deadline). Shell: bash when present, else sh, as login shells.
3. **One events watcher per host**, only while a stream client or a project log follower needs it; it stops 30 s after the last user. Reconnect with backoff 1–30 s and a `resync` after a reconnect. `paused` (the host answers, `/events` does not: three HTTP-error connects in a row or three stream ends within 60 s) polls the container list every 10 s and retries events every 60 s; a host that does not answer is `unreachable` with the classified reason.
4. **Stats** only for the container ids the UI shows (≤ 50 per host per client), every 3 s, at most 4 calls in flight per host, `one-shot` on API ≥ 1.41 with CPU from our previous sample, 60 points per container. Container CPU is a percent of one core (as `docker stats`); host CPU a percent of the whole host.
5. **Host gauges** sample every running container (≤ 100, then `partial`) every 10 s while a client has them open; Info (NCPU, MemTotal) cached 5 min.
6. **Disk usage** only on request, cached 5 min per host, `refresh=1` re-reads when older than 60 s; the gauge shows Docker's usage in bytes.
7. **Stream budget:** 16 streaming Engine connections per host (events watcher, followed container logs, terminals); a single follow or terminal without a slot is 429 `too_many_streams`, a project follower reports the services it could not follow.
8. **One SSE stream per desktop client** (`GET /stream`, `hello` with a 128-bit `stream_id`), subscriptions replaced with `PUT /stream/subscriptions` (unknown hosts listed in `rejected`, never a failed request), at most 32 open streams, a client that falls 512 messages behind is sent `dropped` and closed. Operation state changes of `dockerstacks` reach the clients of the operation's host as `operation` messages.
9. **Logs:** raw lines (ANSI stripped in the UI), 16 KiB per line, batched every 100 ms or 200 lines; defaults `tail` 200 for a container, 100 per container of a stack or project; reconnect with `tail=5000&since=<newest line>` (inclusive; the UI drops repeats). Stack and project logs exist only as streams.
10. **Terminal refusals** are answered as JSON before the WebSocket check (a browser hides the body of a refused handshake, so the app repeats the request as a plain GET to read the reason): 403 `read_only`, 403 `forbidden_origin`, 404, 409 `container_not_running` / `helper_container` / `container_protected_confirmation_required` (`?confirm=protected`), 429 `too_many_streams`, then 400 `websocket_required`. A plain GET never creates an exec.
11. **`docker.readonly`** allows the stream, subscriptions, log follow and disk usage, and refuses the terminal.
12. **UI:** stats patch cells in place (no table re-render from the stream); every key inside the terminal goes to xterm, `Ctrl+]` or the toolbar button leaves it; the rail gauges show for a single selected host.

Each part lists its own deviations from the shared contract at its top.

## Open points for the user (decided as written unless you say otherwise)

- **Disk gauge** shows Docker's own usage (images, containers, volumes, build cache) in bytes, not a percentage of the disk: the Engine API reports no file-system size.
- **Cost on large or remote hosts:** the gauges cost one stats call per running container (up to 100) every 10 s while open; a watched SSH host costs up to five SSH logins (events feed plus 4 parallel stats calls), and every followed container log or terminal on an SSH host is its own SSH connection (the phase 1 transport opens one SSH client per Engine connection). The 16-slot budget bounds the streams.
- **A stack with more services than free slots** shows which services are not followed.
- **ANSI colours** in logs are stripped, not rendered.
- **A crash-looping container** in a followed stack or project produces a detached/attached notice pair per restart (at most one per second).
- **A stack created by hand on the host** is unknown to the stack log route until the stack list is refreshed (30 s scan cache).
- **The terminal diagnosis GET** runs the same checks as the handshake (incl. the protection lookup of the local host) and takes and frees a stream slot; it never starts an exec.
- **A proxy that holds back the headers of `/events`** until the first event would show a quiet host as `unreachable` (timeout) every 20 s; the live test confirms the Engine behaviour.
- **Limits of the UI's diagnosis:** a refused WebSocket handshake for a forbidden origin is explained as "needs a WebSocket connection" (a same-origin GET carries no `Origin`); a refused `/stream` (32 clients, Docker disabled) shows "Live updates paused" without the reason while the 5 s poll keeps the lists fresh; the diagnosis GET of a failed follow can hold a follower for up to 8 s.
- **Translations:** Greek, Hindi, Japanese and Chinese strings had no native review, as in phases 1 and 2.
- **Follow-ups not in this plan:** split `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs` (2237 lines); an NVDA and keyboard-only pass of the log and terminal panels.

## Part A: live data backend (`dockerutil` accessors, `dockerhost` live calls, `internal/dockerwatch`, `dockerstacks` observer)

### Part A notes

**What this part builds.** The Go side of the Docker Manager's live data, below the HTTP layer:

- three accessors on `dockerutil.Client` (its own dial function, the negotiated API version, a client without a total timeout);
- three Engine calls in `dockerhost` (the events feed, one container stats sample, the disk usage);
- the new package `internal/dockerwatch`: the hub that fans live data out to stream clients, one events watcher per host (reconnect, resync, list-poll fallback), the stats sampler with its rings and the host gauges, the disk-usage cache and the per-host stream budget;
- `dockerstacks.Service.Observe`, the hook the server uses to forward operation state changes.

Names, types and JSON shapes are the contract's (`CONTRACT.md`: "Part A surface", "Events watcher behaviour", "Stats behaviour", "Stream messages"); every deviation is listed below. No route, no SSE writing, no log follower and no terminal is in this part.

**Prerequisites.** Phase 2 landed (`a80113379`: `dockerhost`, `dockerstacks`, the stacks routes). Go 1.27. Parts B, C and D are not needed. Part B adds `logs*.go` to `internal/dockerwatch` and `engine_logs_exec.go` to `internal/dockerhost` and uses `Hub.WatchHost`, `Hub.Acquire`, `Event`, `Client.Dial` and `Client.APIVersion` from here; Part C wires the hub into `internal/server`.

**How the code was verified.** Every task was written and run in a scratch worktree (detached at `a80113379`) as one commit per task. The code in this part is the content of those commits, rendered by a script, not retyped; a second script re-applied every create, edit and delete block of this part to the parent state of its task and compared the result with the commit, file by file, byte for byte (all 8 tasks matched). For each of the 8 commits `go vet` and `go test` of `internal/dockerutil`, `internal/dockerhost`, `internal/dockerstacks` and `internal/dockerwatch` pass, checked commit by commit. The "Expected" outputs below are the real outputs of those runs (timings vary), the failing runs are real too (each task's tests on top of the previous commit). Besides: `go build ./...`; `go test ./internal/invasion -run 'Docker|TLS'`, `go test ./internal/server -run 'DockerManager|Containers|ContainerTerminal'` and `go test ./internal/tools -run Docker` pass; the `internal/dockerwatch` tests passed 60 repetitions (`-count=30 -cpu 1,4`) after one race in the test fake (the events feed was registered after the response was flushed) had been fixed. **Not run:** the Go race detector (no gcc on the planning machine; run `go test -race ./internal/dockerwatch/ ./internal/dockerstacks/` on a Linux box, see `reference_aurago_test_server`) and the live test (compiled and skipped; no Docker was started).

**What only the live test can confirm** (Task A7): that a real Engine's `/events` line format and `/containers/{id}/stats` sample match the fixtures (the fixtures follow the Engine's documented JSON and a Docker 27 sample; cgroup v1 and v2 memory keys are covered by fixtures only), that the Engine (and any socket proxy in front of it) flushes the response headers of `/events` before the first event (the watcher counts the feed as established when the headers arrive; a proxy that holds them back would show a quiet host as `unreachable` with reason `timeout` every `ConnectTimeout`), that `one-shot=true` answers at once on API 1.41+, that a stopped container answers the all-zero sample the sampler treats as gone, and that `/system/df` totals are what `docker system df` shows.

New guide: `internal/dockerwatch/AGENTS.md`.

**Deviations from the contract** (names and JSON shapes are unchanged unless said; each deviation is forced by the Engine or the codebase, or protects data):

1. **`dockerhost.StreamEventsOpen`** is added next to `StreamEvents` (which has the contract's signature and calls it). It takes one more callback, `opened func()`, run when the Engine has accepted the request and before the first event: the point where the watcher flips `connecting` to `live`. The Engine flushes the headers of `/events` at once, so this is the moment the feed is established, not the first event.
2. **CPU of an idle container is 0, not -1.** The contract says "`-1` unless both deltas are > 0". `docker stats` shows 0.00 % for a container that used no CPU, and an unknown (-1) value would draw a gap in the UI for every idle container. Implemented: -1 when there is no previous sample (one-shot, first sample), when the system delta is not positive, when the counter went backwards, or (below API 1.41) when `precpu_stats` is not filled; 0 when the system clock ticked and the container used nothing. The value is the percent of **one core** (a container that fills two cores reads 200), as `docker stats` prints it; `host_stats.cpu` is the percent of the **whole host**.
3. **Operation state names:** the contract's list says `waiting_health`; the code's constant (and the journal value) is `health_wait` (`dockerstacks.StateHealthWait`). `Observe` reports the real value.
4. **Extra errors, all matchable with `errors.Is`:** `ErrTooManyHosts` (more than `MaxSubscribedHosts` hosts in one list of a subscription), `ErrInvalidSubscription` (a syntactically bad host or container id; every error of `Client.Set` matches it, also `ErrTooManyIDs` and `ErrTooManyHosts`), `ErrClientClosed`, `ErrHubClosed`. Part C maps every `Set` error that matches `ErrInvalidSubscription` to 400 `bad_request` with the error text (it already names the limit).
5. **`Client.Set` checks the shape of ids and nothing else:** host ids must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`, container ids are 12 to 64 hex characters (case-insensitive) and are reduced to their first 12, lowercase. A container *name* is refused. The hub does **not** know whether a host exists (the contract's "unknown hosts are rejected per entry" is Part C's job: ask the registry before calling `Set`); a host the registry forgets later shows up as `host_status` `unreachable` with the extra reason `host_not_found` (`ReasonHostNotFound`).
6. **`Options.ConnectTimeout`** (default 20 s) is added: how long the watcher waits for the Engine to answer `GET /events` (the streaming client has no total timeout, so a hung proxy would otherwise block it forever). Such an attempt is `unreachable` with reason `timeout`.
7. **`paused` means "the host answers, `/events` does not".** The contract says "after 3 failed connects in a row ... the host goes paused". Implemented: three connects *answered with an HTTP error* in a row (a socket proxy without `EVENTS=1`, an old Engine) or three stream ends within 60 s. A connect that gets no answer at all (dial, TLS, timeout, SSH login) is `unreachable` with the classified reason and is retried with the backoff indefinitely: polling the container list of a host that does not answer would not work either. In `paused` the poll turns the state into `unreachable` when the list call itself gets no answer and back into `paused` when it does.
8. **The events watcher holds one stream slot while it runs, softly:** if the host's 16 slots are used up it runs without one (at most one connection over the budget) instead of starving.
9. **A stats id that answered `stats_gone` is sampled again** when a client asks for it again or when the host's watcher reports `start`, `restart` or `unpause` for it (the contract only says it is dropped). A stopped container answers 200 with an all-zero sample, not 404/409, so that sample (zero `read`, zero memory, zero CPU counter) counts as gone too.
10. **The first reading of the gauges** is followed after 2 s (or `HostInterval` if shorter) by a second one, because the first has no CPU deltas yet; `cpu` is -1 in a reading where no container's CPU is known.
11. **`Message.Data` types** are concrete and exported so the server only has to `json.Marshal` them: `HostStatus`, `Event`, `Resync`, `StatsMsg`, `StatsHistoryMsg`, `StatsGoneMsg`, `HostStats`, `Dropped`; the message names are the constants `MsgHostStatus`, `MsgEvent`, `MsgResync`, `MsgStats`, `MsgStatsHistory`, `MsgStatsGone`, `MsgHostStats`, `MsgOperation`, `MsgDropped`. `hello`, the heartbeat and the `operation` payload (`{"host":..., "operation":...}`) are Part C's; it sends `operation` with `Hub.Publish(host, Message{Event: dockerwatch.MsgOperation, Data: ...})`.

**What the contract left open, as implemented** (parts B, C and D should know):

- A client receives messages in the order they were produced; a dropped client reads the `dropped` message in place of its oldest unread message and then finds the channel closed. `Client.Close` is idempotent and also what the server must call when the SSE request ends. `Hub.Close` closes every client.
- On `Set`, a host newly added to `Hosts` gets the host's current `host_status` first (a fresh watcher starts as `connecting`); a container newly added to `Stats` gets its `stats_history` first when a ring exists, and the sampler takes a sample at once instead of waiting for its next 3 s tick.
- `Hub.Publish` and the `Observe` callback may be called with the operation's locks held: both are non-blocking.
- `WatchHost` keeps the host's watcher alive (it counts as a user) and receives the normalised events (`Event.Type` container, image, volume or network) plus `Event{Type: "resync", Action: "reconnect"|"poll"}`; the callback runs on the watcher goroutine without a lock held and must not block or call back into the hub.
- `DiskUsage` returns `dockerhost.DiskUsage` (its JSON tags are the contract's); a failed reading keeps the old cache and returns the Engine error unchanged.
- Names that Part B and Part C must not redeclare in package `dockerwatch` (reuse them instead): `shortID`, `sleepCtx`, `reasonOf`, `labelProject`, `labelService`, `containerActions`, `normalizeEvent`, `listDigest`, `cpuPercent`, `pointOf`, `ring`, `supportsOneShot`, `watcher`, `statsState`, `dfEntry`, `hostRT`, plus the exported ones; in the test files `fakeEngine`, `fakeHosts`, `testClock`, `testEnv`, `newTestEnv`, `next`, `waitFor`, `waitUntil`, `isStatus`, `eventLine`, `webID`, `risingStats`, `statsBody`. In package `dockerhost` (new file `engine_live.go`) the unexported names are `liveGet`, `liveRawEvent`, `liveCPUStats`, `liveRawStats`, `ctxOr`, `nonNegative`, `eventLineMax`, `dfBodyMax`, `eventFilters`; `liveGet` (GET on the streaming client, non-2xx becomes a `*StatusError`) is reusable by Part B's log follow.

**Open points for the user** (decided as written unless the user says otherwise):

- A remote host reached over **SSH** costs up to five SSH logins while it is being watched (the events feed plus up to 4 parallel stats calls, each on its own pooled connection that is reused while it is busy and reaped after a minute idle). This is the existing "one SSH client per Engine connection" behaviour of phase 1; the login guard of the registry still applies.
- **Container CPU is a percent of one core** (as `docker stats`), host CPU a percent of the whole host. The UI should scale a container sparkline by its own maximum, not by 100.
- A host with many containers costs one stats call per running container (up to 100) every 10 s while a client has its gauges open.

### Task A1: `dockerutil.Client.Dial`, `APIVersion` and `StreamingHTTPClient`

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/dockerutil/client.go`
- Modify: `internal/dockerutil/AGENTS.md`
- Test: `internal/dockerutil/client_access_test.go`

The live features need three things the client already has but does not expose. A hijacked exec stream (Part B) must reach the Engine the way pooled requests do, through the client's own dial function, which is what makes it work on TLS, mutual TLS and SSH hosts: `Client.Dial`. It must also address the API version the version transport negotiated: `Client.APIVersion` (without the `v`, "1.45"; it probes once like a request would). Streams (events, log follow) need the same transport without the client-wide request timeout: `Client.StreamingHTTPClient`. `NewClient` and `NewClientWithDialer` keep every existing behaviour: the dial closure that the transport used is now also stored in the `Client`, and the "has no dial function" error of a nil dial function is kept (it is also what `Dial` returns).

```go
func TestClientDialUsesTheClientsOwnTransport(t *testing.T) {
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		fmt.Fprint(w, "pong")
	}))
	defer server.Close()
	addr := server.Listener.Addr().String()

	var dials atomic.Int32
	dialed := NewClientWithDialer("custom", func(ctx context.Context) (net.Conn, error) {
		dials.Add(1)
		return (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext(ctx, "tcp", addr)
	}, 0, 0)
	defer dialed.CloseIdleConnections()
	plain := NewClient("tcp://"+addr, time.Second)
	defer plain.CloseIdleConnections()

	for name, c := range map[string]*Client{"dialer": dialed, "endpoint": plain} {
		conn, err := c.Dial(context.Background())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: Dial: %v", name, err)
		}
		if _, err := io.WriteString(conn, "GET /ping HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: docker\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: write: %v", name, err)
		}
		status, err := bufio.NewReader(conn).ReadString('\n')
		conn.Close()
		if err != nil || status != "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n" {
			t.Fatalf("%s: first line = %q, %v, want an HTTP 200 answer over the raw connection", name, status, err)
		}
	}
	if dials.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the caller's dial function ran %d times, want once (for Dial)", dials.Load())
	}
}

func TestClientDialWithoutDialFunctionFailsInsteadOfPanicking(t *testing.T) {
	client := NewClientWithDialer("none", nil, time.Second, 0)
	defer client.CloseIdleConnections()
	if conn, err := client.Dial(context.Background()); err == nil {
		conn.Close()
		t.Fatal("Dial succeeded without a dial function")
	}
	var missing *Client
	if _, err := missing.Dial(context.Background()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Dial on a nil client succeeded")
	}
}

func TestClientAPIVersionReturnsTheNegotiatedVersionAndProbesOnce(t *testing.T) {
	var probes atomic.Int32
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path == "/version" {
			probes.Add(1)
			fmt.Fprint(w, `{"ApiVersion":"1.41","MinAPIVersion":"1.24"}`)
			return
		}
		fmt.Fprint(w, `{}`)
	}))
	defer server.Close()
	client := NewClient("tcp://"+server.Listener.Addr().String(), 2*time.Second)
	defer client.CloseIdleConnections()

	version, err := client.APIVersion(context.Background())
	if err != nil || version != "1.41" {
		t.Fatalf("APIVersion = %q, %v, want 1.41 without the v prefix", version, err)
	}
	if code, err := client.DoJSON(context.Background(), http.MethodGet, "containers/json", nil, nil); err != nil || code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("DoJSON = %d, %v", code, err)
	}
	if again, _ := client.APIVersion(context.Background()); again != "1.41" || probes.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("APIVersion = %q after %d probes, want the cached 1.41 after one probe", again, probes.Load())
	}
}

func TestClientAPIVersionReportsAFailedProbe(t *testing.T) {
	client := NewClientWithDialer("down", func(ctx context.Context) (net.Conn, error) {

func TestStreamingHTTPClientHasNoTotalTimeoutAndSharesTheTransport(t *testing.T) {
	server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path == "/version" {
			fmt.Fprint(w, `{"ApiVersion":"1.45","MinAPIVersion":"1.24"}`)
			return
		}
		fmt.Fprint(w, "first ")
		w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
		time.Sleep(150 * time.Millisecond)
		fmt.Fprint(w, "second")
	}))
	defer server.Close()
	client := NewClient("tcp://"+server.Listener.Addr().String(), 50*time.Millisecond)
	defer client.CloseIdleConnections()

	streaming := client.StreamingHTTPClient()
	if streaming.Timeout != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Timeout = %v, want none", streaming.Timeout)
	}
	if streaming.Transport != client.HTTPClient().Transport {
		t.Fatal("the streaming client must reuse the Docker transport")
	}
	if client.HTTPClient().Timeout != 50*time.Millisecond {
		t.Fatalf("the shared client's timeout changed to %v", client.HTTPClient().Timeout)
	}

	read := func(hc *http.Client) (string, error) {
		req, _ := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, Endpoint("events"), nil)
		resp, err := hc.Do(req)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return string(body), err
	}
	if body, err := read(client.HTTPClient()); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("the 50ms client read %q without an error, want its total timeout to cut the slow body", body)
	}
	if body, err := read(streaming); err != nil || body != "first second" {
		t.Fatalf("streaming read = %q, %v, want the whole slow body", body, err)
	}
	var missing *Client
	if missing.StreamingHTTPClient() != nil {
		t.Fatal("StreamingHTTPClient on a nil client should be nil")
	}
}
```

```go
// CloseIdleConnections releases pooled connections without interrupting
// requests that are already using this client.
```

new_string:

```go
// StreamingHTTPClient returns a client on the same transport (and so the same
// version negotiation and dial function) without a total timeout, for
// requests that stay open as long as their context lives: the events feed and
// followed logs. The caller bounds every request with its context.
func (c *Client) StreamingHTTPClient() *http.Client {
	if c == nil || c.httpClient == nil {
		return nil
	}
	client := *c.httpClient
	client.Timeout = 0
	return &client
}

// Dial opens a raw connection to the Engine with the client's own transport:
// the endpoint dialer of NewClient (unix socket, named pipe, TCP) or the
// caller's dial function of NewClientWithDialer (TLS, mutual TLS, SSH). The
// caller owns the connection and closes it. Raw upgraded streams (exec attach)
// use it so they reach the same Engine the pooled requests do.
func (c *Client) Dial(ctx context.Context) (net.Conn, error) {
	if c == nil || c.dial == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("docker client has no dial function")
	}
	return c.dial(ctx)
}

// APIVersion returns the Engine API version the client's version transport
// negotiated, without the "v" ("1.45"). It probes GET /version once when the
// client has not negotiated yet, and again after a stale-version signal.
func (c *Client) APIVersion(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	if c == nil || c.httpClient == nil {
		return "", errors.New("docker client is not initialised")
	}
	transport, ok := c.httpClient.Transport.(*VersionTransport)
	if !ok {
		return "", errors.New("docker client has no version transport")
	}
	origin, _ := url.Parse("http://docker")
	version, err := transport.versionFor(ctx, origin)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return strings.TrimPrefix(version, "v"), nil
}

// CloseIdleConnections releases pooled connections without interrupting
// requests that are already using this client.
```

### Task A2: `dockerhost` live calls: `StreamEvents`, `ContainerStats`, `SystemDF`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerhost/engine_live.go`
- Modify: `internal/dockerhost/AGENTS.md`
- Test: `internal/dockerhost/engine_live_test.go`

The three Engine calls the hub builds on, all through `*dockerutil.Client`:

- `StreamEvents` follows `GET /events` (filter `{"type":["container","image","volume","network"]}`, `since` as `seconds.nanoseconds` when asked for) on the streaming client and hands each decoded line to a callback. A line is at most 1 MiB. It ends with the context's error, the callback's error, or an `io.EOF`-wrapped error when the connection drops; a non-2xx answer is a `*StatusError`. `StreamEventsOpen` (deviation 1) adds a callback for the moment the request was accepted.
- `ContainerStats` reads one `stats?stream=false[&one-shot=true]` sample into `RawStats`: cumulative CPU, network and block counters, memory usage and the cache to subtract (`total_inactive_file`, else `inactive_file` (cgroup v2), else `cache`), `online_cpus` (else the length of `percpu_usage`), `pids_stats.current`. The `read` time is the zero time for the all-zero sample the Engine answers for a container that is not running.
- `SystemDF` reads `GET /system/df` and totals it like `docker system df`: image size is `LayersSize` (unique layers) and reclaimable is what images without a container hold beyond the layers in use, container size is the writable layers (stopped ones are reclaimable), volumes use `UsageData` (unreferenced ones are reclaimable), build cache counts records that are not shared (idle ones are reclaimable); the Engine's "not computed" -1 counts as 0. It reads on the streaming client because the call can take a while on a large host; the caller's context bounds it.

```go
package dockerhost

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func mustParseQuery(t *testing.T, raw string) url.Values {
	t.Helper()
	values, err := url.ParseQuery(raw)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("query %q: %v", raw, err)
	}
	return values
}

// writeEventLines sends each line on its own chunk, like the Engine's /events.
func writeEventLines(w http.ResponseWriter, lines ...string) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	flusher := w.(http.Flusher)
	flusher.Flush()
	for _, line := range lines {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, line+"\n")
		flusher.Flush()
	}
}

const (
	eventStart = `{"Type":"container","Action":"start","Actor":{"ID":"aaaaaaaaaaaa1111","Attributes":{"name":"shop-web-1","image":"nginx:1.27","com.docker.compose.project":"shop"}},"scope":"local","time":1730102400,"timeNano":1730102400123456789}`
	eventDie   = `{"Type":"container","Action":"die","Actor":{"ID":"aaaaaaaaaaaa1111","Attributes":{"name":"shop-web-1","exitCode":"137"}},"scope":"local","time":1730102401,"timeNano":1730102401000000000}`
	eventImage = `{"Type":"image","Action":"pull","Actor":{"ID":"nginx:1.27","Attributes":{"name":"nginx"}},"scope":"local","time":1730102402}`
)

func TestStreamEventsDecodesChunkedLinesAndSendsTheTypeFilter(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	var query string
	fe.on(http.MethodGet, "/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		query = r.URL.RawQuery
		writeEventLines(w, eventStart, "", eventDie, eventImage)
	})

	var got []EngineEvent
	opened := 0
	err := StreamEventsOpen(context.Background(), fe.client(t), time.Time{}, func() { opened++ }, func(ev EngineEvent) error {
		if opened != 1 {
			t.Errorf("event delivered before the open callback (opened = %d)", opened)
		}
		got = append(got, ev)
		return nil
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want an io.EOF-wrapped error when the stream ends", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d events, want 3 (the blank line is skipped): %+v", len(got), got)
	}
	start := got[0]
	if start.Type != "container" || start.Action != "start" || start.ID != "aaaaaaaaaaaa1111" ||
		start.Attributes["name"] != "shop-web-1" || start.Attributes["com.docker.compose.project"] != "shop" ||
		start.Time.UnixNano() != 1730102400123456789 {
		t.Fatalf("start = %+v", start)
	}
	if got[1].Action != "die" || got[1].Attributes["exitCode"] != "137" {
		t.Fatalf("die = %+v", got[1])
	}
	if got[2].Type != "image" || got[2].Time.Unix() != 1730102402 {
		t.Fatalf("image event = %+v, want the seconds field as the fallback time", got[2])
	}

	values := mustParseQuery(t, query)
	var filters map[string][]string
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(values.Get("filters")), &filters); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("filters %q: %v", values.Get("filters"), err)
	}
	if strings.Join(filters["type"], ",") != "container,image,volume,network" {
		t.Fatalf("filters = %v, want the four resource types", filters)
	}
	if values.Has("since") {
		t.Fatalf("query %q has since although none was asked for", query)
	}
}

func TestStreamEventsSendsSinceAndStopsWhenTheCallbackFails(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	var query string
	fe.on(http.MethodGet, "/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		query = r.URL.RawQuery
		writeEventLines(w, eventStart, eventDie)
	})
	stop := errors.New("enough")
	calls := 0
	since := time.Unix(1730102000, 5000)
	err := StreamEvents(context.Background(), fe.client(t), since, func(EngineEvent) error {
		calls++
		return stop
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, stop) || calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v after %d calls, want the callback's error after the first event", err, calls)
	}
	if got := mustParseQuery(t, query).Get("since"); got != "1730102000.000005000" {
		t.Fatalf("since = %q, want unix seconds with nanoseconds", got)
	}
}

func TestStreamEventsEndsWithTheContext(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	fe.on(http.MethodGet, "/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		writeEventLines(w, eventStart)
		<-r.Context().Done()
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	defer cancel()
	c := fe.client(t)
	got := make(chan string, 1)
	go func() {
		err := StreamEvents(ctx, c, time.Time{}, func(EngineEvent) error {
			cancel()
			return nil
		})
		got <- fmt.Sprint(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled))
	}()
	select {
	case canceled := <-got:
		if canceled != "true" {
			t.Fatalf("StreamEvents did not return the context error")
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("StreamEvents kept running after its context ended")
	}
}

func TestStreamEventsReportsAnEngineErrorWithItsStatus(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	fe.json(http.MethodGet, "/events", http.StatusForbidden, `{"message":"events are not allowed by the socket proxy"}`)
	err := StreamEvents(context.Background(), fe.client(t), time.Time{}, func(EngineEvent) error { return nil })
	if StatusOf(err) != http.StatusForbidden || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not allowed") {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v (status %d), want a *StatusError 403 with the Engine message", err, StatusOf(err))
	}
	if ClassifyError(err) != CodeAuth {
		t.Fatalf("ClassifyError = %q, want auth for a 403", ClassifyError(err))
	}
}

func TestStreamEventsRejectsAnOversizedLine(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	fe.on(http.MethodGet, "/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		writeEventLines(w, `{"Type":"container","Action":"start","Actor":{"ID":"x","Attributes":{"big":"`+strings.Repeat("a", 2<<20)+`"}}}`)
	})
	err := StreamEvents(context.Background(), fe.client(t), time.Time{}, func(EngineEvent) error { return nil })
	if err == nil || errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want a line-too-long error that is not a clean end", err)
	}
}

// A cgroup v2 sample (Docker 27 on a current kernel): inactive_file is the cache.
const statsV2 = `{"read":"2026-10-28T08:00:03.250000000Z","preread":"2026-10-28T08:00:00.250000000Z",
"pids_stats":{"current":7},
"blkio_stats":{"io_service_bytes_recursive":[{"major":8,"minor":0,"op":"read","value":4096},{"major":8,"minor":0,"op":"write","value":8192},{"major":8,"minor":16,"op":"Read","value":1000},{"major":8,"minor":16,"op":"Total","value":999999}]},
"cpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":2000000000,"usage_in_kernelmode":500000000,"usage_in_usermode":1500000000},"system_cpu_usage":40000000000,"online_cpus":4},
"precpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":1900000000},"system_cpu_usage":39000000000,"online_cpus":4},
"memory_stats":{"usage":104857600,"stats":{"anon":50000000,"file":40000000,"inactive_file":20971520,"active_file":19000000},"limit":2147483648},
"name":"/web","id":"aaaaaaaaaaaa1111",
"networks":{"eth0":{"rx_bytes":1000,"tx_bytes":2000},"eth1":{"rx_bytes":10,"tx_bytes":20}}}`

// A cgroup v1 sample: total_inactive_file wins over cache; no online_cpus (old Engines).
const statsV1 = `{"read":"2026-10-28T08:00:03.000000000Z",
"pids_stats":{"current":3},
"cpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":500,"percpu_usage":[100,100,150,150]},"system_cpu_usage":4000},
"precpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":400,"percpu_usage":[100,100,100,100]},"system_cpu_usage":3000},
"memory_stats":{"usage":52428800,"stats":{"cache":30000000,"total_cache":30000000,"inactive_file":1,"total_inactive_file":10485760},"limit":1073741824}}`

// Old v1 kernels without inactive_file: the cache counter is the fallback.
const statsV1CacheOnly = `{"read":"2026-10-28T08:00:03Z","memory_stats":{"usage":1000,"stats":{"cache":300},"limit":2000},"cpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":1}},"precpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":0}}}`

func TestContainerStatsDecodesCgroupV2AndSendsOneShot(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	var queries []string
	fe.on(http.MethodGet, "/containers/web/stats", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		queries = append(queries, r.URL.RawQuery)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, statsV2)
	})
	c := fe.client(t)

	s, err := ContainerStats(context.Background(), c, "web", true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ContainerStats: %v", err)
	}
	want := RawStats{
		Read: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 8, 0, 3, 250000000, time.UTC), CPUTotal: 2000000000, SystemCPU: 40000000000, OnlineCPUs: 4,
		PreCPUTotal: 1900000000, PreSystem: 39000000000, MemUsage: 104857600, MemCache: 20971520, MemLimit: 2147483648,
		NetRx: 1010, NetTx: 2020, BlkRead: 5096, BlkWrite: 8192, Pids: 7,
	}
	if !s.Read.Equal(want.Read) {
		t.Fatalf("Read = %v, want %v", s.Read, want.Read)
	}
	s.Read = want.Read
	if s != want {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v\nwant   %+v", s, want)
	}

	if _, err := ContainerStats(context.Background(), c, "web", false); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ContainerStats: %v", err)
	}
	if len(queries) != 2 || queries[0] != "one-shot=true&stream=false" || queries[1] != "stream=false" {
		t.Fatalf("queries = %q, want one-shot only when asked for", queries)
	}
}

func TestContainerStatsCacheRulesOfCgroupV1(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	for name, body := range map[string]string{"v1": statsV1, "old": statsV1CacheOnly} {
		fe.json(http.MethodGet, "/containers/"+name+"/stats", http.StatusOK, body)
	}
	c := fe.client(t)

	v1, err := ContainerStats(context.Background(), c, "v1", false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v1.MemCache != 10485760 || v1.MemUsage != 52428800 || v1.MemLimit != 1073741824 {
		t.Fatalf("v1 memory = usage %d cache %d limit %d, want total_inactive_file as the cache", v1.MemUsage, v1.MemCache, v1.MemLimit)
	}
	if v1.OnlineCPUs != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("OnlineCPUs = %d, want the length of percpu_usage when online_cpus is missing", v1.OnlineCPUs)
	}
	if v1.CPUTotal != 500 || v1.PreCPUTotal != 400 || v1.SystemCPU != 4000 || v1.PreSystem != 3000 || v1.Pids != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("v1 cpu = %+v", v1)
	}

	old, err := ContainerStats(context.Background(), c, "old", false)
	if err != nil || old.MemCache != 300 {
		t.Fatalf("old = %+v, %v, want the cache counter when no inactive_file is reported", old, err)
	}
}

func TestContainerStatsErrors(t *testing.T) {
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

**Create `internal/dockerhost/engine_live.go`**

```go
package dockerhost

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// The live Engine calls of the Docker Manager: the events feed, one stats
// sample of a container and the disk usage. Streaming reads use the client
// without a total timeout (Client.StreamingHTTPClient); the caller's context
// bounds them.

// eventLineMax bounds one line of the events feed; real events are a few
// hundred bytes, the limit only protects against a broken or hostile endpoint.
const eventLineMax = 1 << 20

// dfBodyMax bounds the /system/df answer.
const dfBodyMax = 32 << 20

// eventFilters limits the feed to the resource types the Docker Manager shows.
const eventFilters = `{"type":["container","image","volume","network"]}`

// EngineEvent is one entry of the Engine's events feed.
type EngineEvent struct {
	Type       string            // container | image | volume | network
	Action     string            // e.g. start, die, "health_status: healthy" (raw)
	ID         string            // Actor.ID
	Attributes map[string]string // Actor.Attributes; values are not masked and never go to the UI raw
	Time       time.Time         // from timeNano, else from time
}

type liveRawEvent struct {
	Type     string `json:"Type"`
	Action   string `json:"Action"`
	TimeSec  int64  `json:"time"`
	TimeNano int64  `json:"timeNano"`
	Actor    struct {
		ID         string            `json:"ID"`
		Attributes map[string]string `json:"Attributes"`
	} `json:"Actor"`
}

// liveGet sends a GET on the streaming client and turns a non-2xx answer into
// a *StatusError. The caller closes the body of a successful response.
func liveGet(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, path string) (*http.Response, error) {
	hc := c.StreamingHTTPClient()
	if hc == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("docker client is not initialised")
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, dockerutil.Endpoint(path), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("create Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	resp, err := hc.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(dockerutil.EngineErrorMessage(dockerutil.ReadErrorBody(resp.Body)), 512)
		return nil, &StatusError{Status: resp.StatusCode, Err: fmt.Errorf("Docker API returned %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, message)}
	}
	return resp, nil
}

// StreamEvents follows GET /events (types container, image, volume, network;
// events since the given time when it is not zero) and calls fn for each
// decoded event. It returns when ctx ends (ctx.Err()), when fn returns an
// error (that error), or when the stream ends (an error wrapping io.EOF; the
// Engine never ends the feed on its own, so this means a dropped connection).
func StreamEvents(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, since time.Time, fn func(EngineEvent) error) error {
	return StreamEventsOpen(ctx, c, since, nil, fn)
}

// StreamEventsOpen is StreamEvents with a callback that runs once, as soon as
// the Engine has accepted the request and before the first event: the point
// where the feed counts as established. opened may be nil.
func StreamEventsOpen(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, since time.Time, opened func(), fn func(EngineEvent) error) error {
	query := url.Values{"filters": {eventFilters}}
	if !since.IsZero() {
		query.Set("since", fmt.Sprintf("%d.%09d", since.Unix(), since.Nanosecond()))
	}
	resp, err := liveGet(ctx, c, "events?"+query.Encode())
	if err != nil {
		return ctxOr(ctx, err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if opened != nil {
		opened()
	}
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), eventLineMax)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := scanner.Bytes()
		if len(strings.TrimSpace(string(line))) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		var raw liveRawEvent
		if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &raw); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("decode Docker event: %w", err)
		}
		ev := EngineEvent{Type: raw.Type, Action: raw.Action, ID: raw.Actor.ID, Attributes: raw.Actor.Attributes}
		switch {
		case raw.TimeNano > 0:
			ev.Time = time.Unix(0, raw.TimeNano).UTC()
		case raw.TimeSec > 0:
			ev.Time = time.Unix(raw.TimeSec, 0).UTC()
		}
		if err := fn(ev); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return ctxOr(ctx, fmt.Errorf("read Docker events: %w", err))
	}
	return ctxOr(ctx, fmt.Errorf("Docker events stream ended: %w", io.EOF))
}

// ctxOr prefers the context's error over the transport error it caused.
func ctxOr(ctx context.Context, err error) error {
	if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
		return ctxErr
	}
	return err
}

// RawStats is the decoded subset of one GET /containers/{id}/stats sample.
// The counters are cumulative; callers derive rates and percentages.
type RawStats struct {
	Read              time.Time // zero for a container that is not running
	CPUTotal          uint64    // cpu_stats.cpu_usage.total_usage
	SystemCPU         uint64    // cpu_stats.system_cpu_usage
	OnlineCPUs        int       // cpu_stats.online_cpus, else len(percpu_usage)
	PreCPUTotal       uint64    // precpu_stats.cpu_usage.total_usage
	PreSystem         uint64    // precpu_stats.system_cpu_usage
	MemUsage          uint64    // memory_stats.usage
	MemCache          uint64    // total_inactive_file or inactive_file, else cache
	MemLimit          uint64    // memory_stats.limit
	NetRx, NetTx      uint64    // summed over the networks
	BlkRead, BlkWrite uint64    // blkio read and write bytes, summed over devices
	Pids              uint64
}

type liveCPUStats struct {
	CPUUsage struct {
		Total  uint64   `json:"total_usage"`
		PerCPU []uint64 `json:"percpu_usage"`
	} `json:"cpu_usage"`
	System uint64 `json:"system_cpu_usage"`
	Online uint32 `json:"online_cpus"`
}

type liveRawStats struct {
	Read string `json:"read"`
	Pids struct {
		Current uint64 `json:"current"`
	} `json:"pids_stats"`
	Blkio struct {
		IOServiceBytes []struct {
			Op    string `json:"op"`
			Value uint64 `json:"value"`
		} `json:"io_service_bytes_recursive"`
	} `json:"blkio_stats"`
	CPU    liveCPUStats `json:"cpu_stats"`
	PreCPU liveCPUStats `json:"precpu_stats"`
	Memory struct {
		Usage uint64            `json:"usage"`
		Limit uint64            `json:"limit"`
		Stats map[string]uint64 `json:"stats"`
	} `json:"memory_stats"`
	Networks map[string]struct {
		Rx uint64 `json:"rx_bytes"`
		Tx uint64 `json:"tx_bytes"`
	} `json:"networks"`
}

// ContainerStats reads one stats sample (stream=false). oneShot adds
// one-shot=true, which the Engine honours from API 1.41: it answers at once
// instead of waiting a second to fill precpu_stats, and leaves precpu_stats
// empty. A container that is not running answers with an all-zero sample
// (Read is the zero time).
func ContainerStats(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, id string, oneShot bool) (RawStats, error) {
	if err := validateContainerRef(id); err != nil {
		return RawStats{}, err
	}
	path := "containers/" + url.PathEscape(id) + "/stats?stream=false"
	if oneShot {
		path = "containers/" + url.PathEscape(id) + "/stats?one-shot=true&stream=false"
	}
	var raw liveRawStats
	if err := engineJSON(ctx, c, http.MethodGet, path, &raw); err != nil {
		return RawStats{}, err
	}
	out := RawStats{
		CPUTotal:    raw.CPU.CPUUsage.Total,
		SystemCPU:   raw.CPU.System,
		OnlineCPUs:  int(raw.CPU.Online),
		PreCPUTotal: raw.PreCPU.CPUUsage.Total,
		PreSystem:   raw.PreCPU.System,
		MemUsage:    raw.Memory.Usage,
		MemLimit:    raw.Memory.Limit,
		Pids:        raw.Pids.Current,
	}
	if out.OnlineCPUs == 0 {
		out.OnlineCPUs = len(raw.CPU.CPUUsage.PerCPU)
	}
	if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, raw.Read); err == nil && t.Year() > 1 {
		out.Read = t.UTC()
	}
	// Page cache that the kernel can drop at once does not count as use, like
	// `docker stats`: cgroup v1 reports total_inactive_file, cgroup v2
	// inactive_file, very old kernels only cache.
	for _, key := range []string{"total_inactive_file", "inactive_file", "cache"} {
		if v, ok := raw.Memory.Stats[key]; ok {
			out.MemCache = v
			break
		}
	}
	for _, n := range raw.Networks {
		out.NetRx += n.Rx
		out.NetTx += n.Tx
	}
	for _, e := range raw.Blkio.IOServiceBytes {
		switch strings.ToLower(e.Op) {
		case "read":
			out.BlkRead += e.Value
		case "write":
			out.BlkWrite += e.Value
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// DiskUsageGroup is the usage of one kind of Docker data.
type DiskUsageGroup struct {
	Count       int   `json:"count"`
	Active      int   `json:"active"`
	Size        int64 `json:"size"`
	Reclaimable int64 `json:"reclaimable"`
}

// DiskUsage is Docker's own disk use in bytes (the Engine API reports no size
// for the file system itself).
type DiskUsage struct {
	Images     DiskUsageGroup `json:"images"`
	Containers DiskUsageGroup `json:"containers"`
	Volumes    DiskUsageGroup `json:"volumes"`
	BuildCache DiskUsageGroup `json:"build_cache"`
	Total      int64          `json:"total"` // sum of the four Size values
}

// nonNegative maps the Engine's "not computed" value -1 to 0.
func nonNegative(n int64) int64 {
	if n < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return n
}

// SystemDF reads GET /system/df and totals it the way `docker system df`
// does: image size is the size of the unique layers, container size the
// writable layers, volume size the reported usage, build cache without shared
// records. Reclaimable is what unused images, stopped containers, unreferenced
// volumes and idle build cache hold. The call can take a while on a large host.
func SystemDF(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client) (DiskUsage, error) {
	resp, err := liveGet(ctx, c, "system/df")
	if err != nil {
		return DiskUsage{}, ctxOr(ctx, err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var raw struct {
		LayersSize int64 `json:"LayersSize"`
		Images     []struct {
			Size       int64 `json:"Size"`
			SharedSize int64 `json:"SharedSize"`
			Containers int64 `json:"Containers"`
		} `json:"Images"`
		Containers []struct {
			State  string `json:"State"`
			SizeRw int64  `json:"SizeRw"`
		} `json:"Containers"`
		Volumes []struct {
			UsageData *struct {
				RefCount int64 `json:"RefCount"`
				Size     int64 `json:"Size"`
			} `json:"UsageData"`
		} `json:"Volumes"`
		BuildCache []struct {
			InUse  bool  `json:"InUse"`
			Shared bool  `json:"Shared"`
			Size   int64 `json:"Size"`
		} `json:"BuildCache"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, dfBodyMax)).Decode(&raw); err != nil {
		return DiskUsage{}, ctxOr(ctx, fmt.Errorf("decode Docker disk usage: %w", err))
	}

	var out DiskUsage
	used := int64(0)
	out.Images.Count = len(raw.Images)
	for _, img := range raw.Images {
		if img.Containers > 0 {
			out.Images.Active++
			if img.Size >= 0 && img.SharedSize >= 0 {
				used += img.Size - img.SharedSize
			}
		}
	}
	out.Images.Size = nonNegative(raw.LayersSize)
	out.Images.Reclaimable = nonNegative(out.Images.Size - used)

	out.Containers.Count = len(raw.Containers)
	for _, ctr := range raw.Containers {
		size := nonNegative(ctr.SizeRw)
		out.Containers.Size += size
		if strings.EqualFold(ctr.State, "running") {
			out.Containers.Active++
		} else {
			out.Containers.Reclaimable += size
		}
	}

	out.Volumes.Count = len(raw.Volumes)
	for _, vol := range raw.Volumes {
		if vol.UsageData == nil {
			continue
		}
		size := nonNegative(vol.UsageData.Size)
		out.Volumes.Size += size
		switch {
		case vol.UsageData.RefCount > 0:
			out.Volumes.Active++
		case vol.UsageData.RefCount == 0:
			out.Volumes.Reclaimable += size
		}
	}

	out.BuildCache.Count = len(raw.BuildCache)
	for _, rec := range raw.BuildCache {
		if rec.InUse {
			out.BuildCache.Active++
		}
		if rec.Shared {
			continue
		}
		size := nonNegative(rec.Size)
		out.BuildCache.Size += size
		if !rec.InUse {
			out.BuildCache.Reclaimable += size
		}
	}

	out.Total = out.Images.Size + out.Containers.Size + out.Volumes.Size + out.BuildCache.Size
	return out, nil
}
```

### Task A3: `internal/dockerwatch` hub: stream clients, subscriptions, `Publish`, `WatchHost`, `Acquire`, disk-usage cache

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerwatch/types.go`, `hub.go`, `client.go`, `budget.go`, `df.go`, `seams.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerwatch/fakeengine_test.go`, `internal/dockerwatch/hub_test.go`

The core of the package. `Hub` owns the stream clients and one `hostRT` per host that something needs (an events watcher, `WatchHost` callbacks, a stats loop, a gauge loop). One mutex, `Hub.mu`, guards the clients, their subscriptions and the host runtimes; messages are pushed into the clients' buffered channels while it is held (a push never blocks), so a client sees messages in the order they were produced. `Client.push` is where a full buffer turns into the `dropped` notice and a closed client. `Client.Set` validates a whole `Subscription` (limits, id shapes, ids reduced to 12 characters), swaps it in and reconciles every host it touched. `Acquire` is the per-host budget of 16 streaming connections. `DiskUsage` caches `dockerhost.SystemDF` per host (5 min; a forced refresh only when the cache is older than 60 s; one Engine call at a time per host).

`seams.go` holds do-nothing stand-ins for the two parts the next tasks add (`watcher`, `statsState` and the functions that start them), so that this task compiles and passes on its own; task A4 removes the watcher half of the file and task A5 deletes it. The fake Engine of the tests (`fakeengine_test.go`) already serves what tasks A4 and A5 need: `/version`, `/info`, `/containers/json`, `/system/df`, an `/events` feed that the test writes to and drops, and per-container stats generators.

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log/slog"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
	"aurago/internal/testutil"
)

var reStatsPath = regexp.MustCompile(`^/v1\.\d+/containers/([^/]+)/stats$`)

// fakeEngine is an httptest Docker Engine with the routes the hub uses:
// /version, /info, /containers/json, /events (a feed the test controls),
// /containers/{id}/stats and /system/df.
type fakeEngine struct {
	server *httptest.Server

	mu         sync.Mutex
	api        string // reported ApiVersion
	containers string // body of /containers/json
	info       string
	df         string
	infoCalls  int
	listCalls  int
	dfCalls    int

	eventsStatus int  // non-zero: /events answers this status
	eventsHang   bool // /events never answers
	eventsEnd    bool // /events answers 200 and ends the stream at once
	eventConns   int
	feeds        []*eventFeed

	stats        map[string]func(call int) (int, string)
	statsCalls   map[string]int
	statsQueries []string
	statsDelay   time.Duration
	inflight     int
	maxInflight  int
}

type eventFeed struct {
	lines chan string
	drop  chan struct{}
}

func newFakeEngine(t *testing.T) *fakeEngine {
	t.Helper()
	fe := &fakeEngine{
		api:        "1.45",
		containers: "[]",
		info:       `{"Name":"nas","NCPU":4,"MemTotal":8589934592}`,
		df:         `{"LayersSize":0,"Images":null,"Containers":null,"Volumes":null,"BuildCache":null}`,
		stats:      map[string]func(int) (int, string){},
		statsCalls: map[string]int{},
	}
	fe.server = testutil.NewHTTPServer(t, http.HandlerFunc(fe.serve))
	t.Cleanup(fe.server.Close)
	return fe
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) client(t *testing.T) *dockerutil.Client {
	t.Helper()
	c := dockerutil.NewClient("tcp://127.0.0.1:"+strconv.Itoa(fe.server.Listener.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port), 5*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(c.CloseIdleConnections)
	return c
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	path := r.URL.Path
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/version"):
		fe.mu.Lock()
		api := fe.api
		fe.mu.Unlock()
		fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"Version":"27.3.1","ApiVersion":%q,"MinAPIVersion":"1.24"}`, api)
	case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/info"):
		fe.mu.Lock()
		fe.infoCalls++
		body := fe.info
		fe.mu.Unlock()
		fmt.Fprint(w, body)
	case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/containers/json"):
		fe.mu.Lock()
		fe.listCalls++
		body := fe.containers
		fe.mu.Unlock()
		fmt.Fprint(w, body)
	case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/system/df"):
		fe.mu.Lock()
		fe.dfCalls++
		body := fe.df
		fe.mu.Unlock()
		fmt.Fprint(w, body)
	case strings.HasSuffix(path, "/events"):
		fe.serveEvents(w, r)
	case reStatsPath.MatchString(path):
		fe.serveStats(w, r, reStatsPath.FindStringSubmatch(path)[1])
	default:
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
		fmt.Fprint(w, `{"message":"page not found"}`)
	}
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) serveEvents(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	fe.eventConns++
	status, hang, end := fe.eventsStatus, fe.eventsHang, fe.eventsEnd
	fe.mu.Unlock()
	switch {
	case hang:
		<-r.Context().Done()
		return
	case status != 0:
		w.WriteHeader(status)
		fmt.Fprint(w, `{"message":"events are not available"}`)
		return
	}
	// The feed is registered before the client can see the answer, so a test
	// that has seen the stream open can always write to it.
	feed := &eventFeed{lines: make(chan string, 64), drop: make(chan struct{})}
	if !end {
		fe.mu.Lock()
		fe.feeds = append(fe.feeds, feed)
		fe.mu.Unlock()
	}
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	flusher := w.(http.Flusher)
	flusher.Flush()
	if end {
		return
	}
	for {
		select {
		case line := <-feed.lines:
			io.WriteString(w, line+"\n")
			flusher.Flush()
		case <-feed.drop:
			return
		case <-r.Context().Done():
			return
		}
	}
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) serveStats(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	fe.statsCalls[id]++
	call := fe.statsCalls[id]
	fe.statsQueries = append(fe.statsQueries, r.URL.RawQuery)
	gen := fe.stats[id]
	delay := fe.statsDelay
	fe.inflight++
	fe.maxInflight = max(fe.maxInflight, fe.inflight)
	fe.mu.Unlock()
	defer func() {
		fe.mu.Lock()
		fe.inflight--
		fe.mu.Unlock()
	}()
	if delay > 0 {
		time.Sleep(delay)
	}
	if gen == nil {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
		fmt.Fprint(w, `{"message":"No such container"}`)
		return
	}
	status, body := gen(call)
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	fmt.Fprint(w, body)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) set(f func(fe *fakeEngine)) {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	f(fe)
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) conns() int {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return fe.eventConns
}

func (fe *fakeEngine) calls(id string) int {
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	return fe.statsCalls[id]
}

// send writes a line on the newest open events feed.
func (fe *fakeEngine) send(t *testing.T, lines ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	if len(fe.feeds) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no events feed is open")
	}
	feed := fe.feeds[len(fe.feeds)-1]
	for _, line := range lines {
		feed.lines <- line
	}
}

// dropFeed ends the newest events connection from the server side.
func (fe *fakeEngine) dropFeed(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	fe.mu.Lock()
	defer fe.mu.Unlock()
	if len(fe.feeds) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no events feed is open")
	}
	close(fe.feeds[len(fe.feeds)-1].drop)
}

// fakeHosts satisfies Hosts over fake engines.
type fakeHosts struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	clients map[string]*dockerutil.Client
	down    map[string]bool
}

func newFakeHosts() *fakeHosts {
	return &fakeHosts{clients: map[string]*dockerutil.Client{}, down: map[string]bool{}}
}

func (f *fakeHosts) add(t *testing.T, id string, fe *fakeEngine) {
	t.Helper()
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.clients[id] = fe.client(t)
}

func (f *fakeHosts) setDown(id string, down bool) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.down[id] = down
}

func (f *fakeHosts) Host(_ context.Context, id string) (dockerhost.Host, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	if _, ok := f.clients[id]; !ok {
		return dockerhost.Host{}, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return dockerhost.Host{ID: id, Name: id}, nil
}

func (f *fakeHosts) Client(_ context.Context, id string) (*dockerutil.Client, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	if f.down[id] {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused")
	}
	c, ok := f.clients[id]
	if !ok {
		return nil, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return c, nil
}

// testClock is a manually advanced clock for Options.Now.
type testClock struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	t  time.Time
}

func newTestClock() *testClock {
	return &testClock{t: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 8, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)}
}

func (c *testClock) Now() time.Time {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.t
}

func (c *testClock) Advance(d time.Duration) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	c.t = c.t.Add(d)
}

// testEnv is a hub over one fake host "h1" with short timings.
type testEnv struct {
	hub   *Hub
	hosts *fakeHosts
	fe    *fakeEngine
	clock *testClock
}

func newTestEnv(t *testing.T, tune func(*Options)) *testEnv {
	t.Helper()
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	hosts := newFakeHosts()
	hosts.add(t, "h1", fe)
	clock := newTestClock()
	opts := Options{
		Now:            clock.Now,
		StatsInterval:  15 * time.Millisecond,
		HostInterval:   40 * time.Millisecond,
		PollInterval:   15 * time.Millisecond,
		RetryPaused:    250 * time.Millisecond,
		IdleStop:       60 * time.Millisecond,
		ConnectTimeout: 2 * time.Second,
		Backoff:        []time.Duration{5 * time.Millisecond, 10 * time.Millisecond},
		Logger:         slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
	}
	if tune != nil {
		tune(&opts)
	}
	hub := New(hosts, opts)
	t.Cleanup(hub.Close)
	return &testEnv{hub: hub, hosts: hosts, fe: fe, clock: clock}
}

// attach opens a client and subscribes it.
func (e *testEnv) attach(t *testing.T, sub Subscription) *Client {
	t.Helper()
	c, err := e.hub.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Attach: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(c.Close)
	if _, err := c.Set(sub); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Set: %v", err)
	}
	return c
}

// next waits for the next message of a client.
func next(t *testing.T, c *Client, timeout time.Duration) Message {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case m, ok := <-c.Messages():
		if !ok {
			t.Fatal("the client's stream is closed")
		}
		return m
	case <-time.After(timeout):
		t.Fatal("timed out waiting for a message")
		return Message{}
	}
}

// waitFor reads messages until pick returns true for one; the others are skipped.
func waitFor(t *testing.T, c *Client, what string, pick func(Message) bool) Message {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.After(5 * time.Second)
	for {
		select {
		case m, ok := <-c.Messages():
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("the stream closed while waiting for %s", what)
			}
			if pick(m) {
				return m
			}
		case <-deadline:
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
	}
}

func isStatus(state string) func(Message) bool {
	return func(m Message) bool {
		s, ok := m.Data.(HostStatus)
		return m.Event == MsgHostStatus && ok && s.State == state
	}
}

func waitUntil(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if cond() {
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(3 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
}
```

**Create `internal/dockerwatch/hub_test.go`**

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

func TestAttachGivesRandomIDsAndStopsAtTheClientLimit(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	reID := regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{32}$`)
	var clients []*Client
	for i := 0; i < MaxClients; i++ {
		c, err := env.hub.Attach()
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Attach %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		if !reID.MatchString(c.ID()) {
			t.Fatalf("ID = %q, want 32 lowercase hex characters", c.ID())
		}
		if found, ok := env.hub.Client(c.ID()); !ok || found != c {
			t.Fatalf("Client(%q) = %v, %v", c.ID(), found, ok)
		}
		clients = append(clients, c)
	}
	if _, err := env.hub.Attach(); !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyClients) {
		t.Fatalf("Attach #%d = %v, want ErrTooManyClients", MaxClients+1, err)
	}
	clients[0].Close()
	clients[0].Close() // idempotent
	if _, ok := env.hub.Client(clients[0].ID()); ok {
		t.Fatal("a closed client is still found")
	}
	if _, open := <-clients[0].Messages(); open {
		t.Fatal("a closed client's stream is still open")
	}
	if _, err := env.hub.Attach(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Attach after a Close: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestSetChecksTheLimitsAndNormalisesIDs(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	c, err := env.hub.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer c.Close()

	long := strings.Repeat("AbC123", 10) + "abcd" // 64 characters, mixed case
	accepted, err := c.Set(Subscription{
		Hosts:     []string{"h1", "h1"},
		Stats:     map[string][]string{"h1": {long, long[:12], "0123456789ab"}},
		HostStats: []string{"h1"},
	})
	if err != nil || accepted != (Accepted{Hosts: 1, Stats: 2, HostStats: 1}) {
		t.Fatalf("Set = %+v, %v, want 1 host, 2 distinct 12-char ids, 1 gauge host", accepted, err)
	}
	env.hub.mu.Lock()
	got := c.sub.Stats["h1"]
	env.hub.mu.Unlock()
	if fmt.Sprint(got) != "[0123456789ab abc123abc123]" {
		t.Fatalf("stored ids = %v, want the lowercase 12-character prefixes, sorted", got)
	}

	ids := make([]string, MaxStatsIDs+1)
	for i := range ids {
		ids[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%012x", i+1)
	}
	hosts := make([]string, MaxSubscribedHosts+1)
	for i := range hosts {
		hosts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("h_%d", i)
	}
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		sub  Subscription
		want error
	}{
		"too many ids":    {Subscription{Stats: map[string][]string{"h1": ids}}, ErrTooManyIDs},
		"too many hosts":  {Subscription{Hosts: hosts}, ErrTooManyHosts},
		"too many gauges": {Subscription{HostStats: hosts}, ErrTooManyHosts},
		"bad id":          {Subscription{Stats: map[string][]string{"h1": {"web"}}}, ErrInvalidSubscription},
		"bad host":        {Subscription{Hosts: []string{"../x"}}, ErrInvalidSubscription},
	} {
		if _, err := c.Set(tc.sub); !errors.Is(err, tc.want) || !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidSubscription) {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, want %v (and ErrInvalidSubscription)", name, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := c.Set(Subscription{Stats: map[string][]string{"h1": ids[:MaxStatsIDs]}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("exactly %d ids per host must be accepted: %v", MaxStatsIDs, err)
	}
	// A refused Set changes nothing: the last good subscription is still in force.
	env.hub.mu.Lock()
	kept := len(c.sub.Stats["h1"])
	env.hub.mu.Unlock()
	if kept != MaxStatsIDs {
		t.Fatalf("the subscription holds %d ids after refused calls, want %d", kept, MaxStatsIDs)
	}
}

func TestPublishReachesOnlyClientsOfTheHost(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	a := env.attach(t, Subscription{Hosts: []string{"h1"}})
	b := env.attach(t, Subscription{})
	env.hub.Publish("h1", Message{Event: MsgOperation, Data: "op-1"})
	env.hub.Publish("other", Message{Event: MsgOperation, Data: "op-2"})

	m := waitFor(t, a, "the operation message", func(m Message) bool { return m.Event == MsgOperation })
	if m.Data != "op-1" {
		t.Fatalf("operation = %v, want op-1", m.Data)
	}
	select {
	case m := <-b.Messages():
		t.Fatalf("a client without the host received %+v", m)
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Millisecond):
	}
}

func TestSlowClientIsSentDroppedAndClosed(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	slow := env.attach(t, Subscription{Hosts: []string{"h1"}})
	for i := 0; i < ClientBuffer+10; i++ {
		env.hub.Publish("h1", Message{Event: MsgOperation, Data: i})
	}
	var last Message
	n := 0
	for m := range slow.Messages() { // the channel is closed after the notice
		last = m
		n++
	}
	if last.Event != MsgDropped || last.Data != (Dropped{Reason: "slow_client"}) {
		t.Fatalf("last message = %+v, want dropped/slow_client", last)
	}
	if n > ClientBuffer {
		t.Fatalf("read %d messages, want at most the buffer of %d", n, ClientBuffer)
	}
	waitUntil(t, "the dropped client to be removed", func() bool {
		_, ok := env.hub.Client(slow.ID())
		return !ok
	})
	if _, err := slow.Set(Subscription{}); !errors.Is(err, ErrClientClosed) {
		t.Fatalf("Set on a dropped client = %v, want ErrClientClosed", err)
	}
}

func TestAcquireStopsAtTheStreamBudgetPerHost(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	var releases []func()
	for i := 0; i < MaxStreamsPerHost; i++ {
		release, err := env.hub.Acquire("h1")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Acquire %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		releases = append(releases, release)
	}
	if _, err := env.hub.Acquire("h1"); !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyStreams) {
		t.Fatalf("Acquire #%d = %v, want ErrTooManyStreams", MaxStreamsPerHost+1, err)
	}
	if release, err := env.hub.Acquire("h2"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("another host has its own budget: %v", err)
	} else {
		release()
	}
	releases[0]()
	releases[0]() // a second call must not free a second slot
	again, err := env.hub.Acquire("h1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Acquire after a release: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := env.hub.Acquire("h1"); !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyStreams) {
		t.Fatalf("a double release freed two slots: %v", err)
	}
	again()
}

func TestDiskUsageIsCachedForFiveMinutesAndRefreshedAfterOneMinute(t *testing.T) {
	env := newTestEnv(t, nil)
	env.fe.set(func(fe *fakeEngine) {
		fe.df = `{"LayersSize":1000,"Images":[{"Size":1000,"SharedSize":0,"Containers":1}],"Containers":null,"Volumes":null,"BuildCache":null}`
	})
	ctx := context.Background()
	read := func(refresh bool) (dockerhost.DiskUsage, time.Time, bool) {
		t.Helper()
		usage, at, cached, err := env.hub.DiskUsage(ctx, "h1", refresh)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("DiskUsage: %v", err)
		}
		return usage, at, cached
	}
	calls := func() int {
		env.fe.mu.Lock()
		defer env.fe.mu.Unlock()
		return env.fe.dfCalls
	}

	usage, firstAt, cached := read(false)
	if cached || usage.Total != 1000 || usage.Images.Size != 1000 || calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("first read: usage %+v cached %v calls %d, want a fresh reading", usage, cached, calls())
	}
	env.clock.Advance(30 * time.Second)
	if _, at, cached := read(false); !cached || !at.Equal(firstAt) || calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("second read: cached %v at %v calls %d, want the cached reading", cached, at, calls())
	}
	if _, _, cached := read(true); !cached || calls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("refresh after 30 s: cached %v calls %d, want the cache (younger than 60 s)", cached, calls())
	}
	env.clock.Advance(40 * time.Second)
	if _, at, cached := read(true); cached || !at.After(firstAt) || calls() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("refresh after 70 s: cached %v calls %d, want a new reading", cached, calls())
	}
	env.clock.Advance(4 * time.Minute)
	if _, _, cached := read(false); !cached || calls() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("read after 4 min: cached %v calls %d, want the cache", cached, calls())
	}
	env.clock.Advance(2 * time.Minute)
	if _, _, cached := read(false); cached || calls() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("read after 6 min: cached %v calls %d, want a new reading (cache older than 5 min)", cached, calls())
	}

	env.fe.set(func(fe *fakeEngine) { fe.df = `not json` })
	env.clock.Advance(2 * time.Minute)
	if _, _, _, err := env.hub.DiskUsage(ctx, "h1", true); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("DiskUsage hid an Engine failure")
	}
	if _, _, _, err := env.hub.DiskUsage(ctx, "nope", false); !errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown host: err = %v, want ErrHostNotFound", err)
	}
}
```
