### Task A7: Gated live test against a real Docker Engine

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerwatch/live_test.go`

`TestLiveWatch` runs the live data against a real Engine. It is gated by `AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1` (endpoint from `AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE_ENDPOINT`, default `dockerutil.DefaultHost()`) and needs the pinned runner image to be on the engine already (it pulls nothing; it skips with the `docker pull` command otherwise). It creates one throw-away container of the runner image named `aurago-dw-live-<hex>` (entrypoint `sleep`, command `60`, no network) while a hub client watches the host, and checks: the host goes `live`; the `start` event arrives with the container's name and short id; two stats points arrive and the last has CPU >= -1 and memory > 0; a `host_stats` reading has running containers, memory, NCPU and MemTotal; a `kill` produces a `die` event with exit code 137 and then `stats_gone`; `DiskUsage(refresh)` returns a fresh reading with at least the runner image. Cleanup removes only its own container. Here the test is only compiled; it is run in the live acceptance (below).

- [ ] **Step 1: Create the test**

**Create `internal/dockerwatch/live_test.go`**

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"encoding/hex"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// The live test runs the live data against a real Docker Engine: a throw-away
// container of the pinned runner image (sleep 60) is created, started, killed
// and removed while a hub client watches host "live". It checks that the events
// arrive through the hub, that a stats point and a host gauge reading carry
// real numbers, that the container is reported gone after it dies, and that
// the disk usage can be read. It is gated by environment variables:
//
//	AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1                   switch the test on
//	AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE_ENDPOINT=<host>     Engine endpoint (default: dockerutil.DefaultHost())
//
// The runner image must already be on the engine (run the dockerstacks live
// test or `docker pull docker:29.9.2-cli` once); the test pulls nothing. It
// creates and removes only its own container, named aurago-dw-live-<hex>.
//
//	AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1 go test ./internal/dockerwatch/ -run TestLiveWatch -v -count=1 -timeout 5m

// liveHosts serves one host, "live", from a real engine client.
type liveHosts struct{ client *dockerutil.Client }

func (l liveHosts) Host(_ context.Context, id string) (dockerhost.Host, error) {
	if id != "live" {
		return dockerhost.Host{}, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return dockerhost.Host{ID: "live", Name: "live", Kind: dockerhost.KindLocal}, nil
}

func (l liveHosts) Client(_ context.Context, id string) (*dockerutil.Client, error) {
	if id != "live" {
		return nil, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound
	}
	return l.client, nil
}

func TestLiveWatch(t *testing.T) {
	if os.Getenv("AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE") != "1" {
		t.Skip("set AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1 to run against a real Docker Engine")
	}
	endpoint := os.Getenv("AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE_ENDPOINT")
	if endpoint == "" {
		endpoint = dockerutil.DefaultHost()
	}
	client := dockerutil.NewClient(endpoint, 30*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(client.CloseIdleConnections)
	ctx := context.Background()

	image := ""
	for _, ref := range []string{dockerstacks.RunnerImage, dockerstacks.RunnerLocalTag} {
		if code, err := client.DoJSON(ctx, http.MethodGet, "images/"+url.PathEscape(ref)+"/json", nil, nil); err == nil {
			image = ref
			break
		} else if code == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("cannot reach the engine at %s: %v", endpoint, err)
		}
	}
	if image == "" {
		t.Skipf("the runner image %s is not on the engine; pull it once (docker pull %s)", dockerstacks.RunnerImage, dockerstacks.RunnerImageTag)
	}

	hub := New(liveHosts{client: client}, Options{
		StatsInterval: time.Second,
		HostInterval:  2 * time.Second,
		Logger:        slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelDebug})),
	})
	t.Cleanup(hub.Close)
	cl, err := hub.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(cl.Close)

	var suffix [4]byte
	_, _ = rand.Read(suffix[:])
	name := "aurago-dw-live-" + hex.EncodeToString(suffix[:])

	// Watch the host before the container exists, so its create and start are seen.
	if _, err := cl.Set(Subscription{Hosts: []string{"live"}, HostStats: []string{"live"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	waitLive(t, cl, "host_status live", func(m Message) bool {
		s, ok := m.Data.(HostStatus)
		return m.Event == MsgHostStatus && ok && s.State == StateLive
	})

	var created struct {
		ID string `json:"Id"`
	}
	body := map[string]any{
		"Image":      image,
		"Entrypoint": []string{"sleep"},
		"Cmd":        []string{"60"},
		"Labels":     map[string]string{"aurago.docker-watch-live": "1"},
		"HostConfig": map[string]any{"NetworkMode": "none"},
	}
	if _, err := client.DoJSON(ctx, http.MethodPost, "containers/create?name="+name, body, &created); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = dockerhost.RemoveContainer(context.Background(), client, created.ID, true)
	})
	short := created.ID[:12]

	if _, err := cl.Set(Subscription{Hosts: []string{"live"}, Stats: map[string][]string{"live": {short}}, HostStats: []string{"live"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := dockerhost.ContainerAction(ctx, client, created.ID, "start"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
	}
	ev := waitLive(t, cl, "the start event", func(m Message) bool {
		e, ok := m.Data.(Event)
		return m.Event == MsgEvent && ok && e.Type == "container" && e.Action == "start" && e.ID == created.ID
	}).Data.(Event)
	if ev.Name != name || ev.ShortID != short || ev.T == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("start event = %+v, want name %s and short id %s", ev, name, short)
	}

	// Two stats points: the first CPU is unknown (-1), later ones are readings.
	var point StatsPoint
	for seen := 0; seen < 2; seen++ {
		point = waitLive(t, cl, "a stats point", func(m Message) bool { return m.Event == MsgStats }).Data.(StatsMsg).Point
	}
	if point.CPU < -1 || point.Mem == 0 || point.T == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stats point = %+v, want cpu >= -1 and memory > 0", point)
	}
	hs := waitLive(t, cl, "a host reading with CPU and memory", func(m Message) bool {
		h, ok := m.Data.(HostStats)
		return m.Event == MsgHostStats && ok && h.Running >= 1 && h.MemUsed > 0
	}).Data.(HostStats)
	if hs.MemTotal == 0 || hs.NCPU == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("host stats = %+v, want the host's memory and CPU count", hs)
	}

	if err := dockerhost.ContainerAction(ctx, client, created.ID, "kill"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("kill: %v", err)
	}
	die := waitLive(t, cl, "the die event", func(m Message) bool {
		e, ok := m.Data.(Event)
		return m.Event == MsgEvent && ok && e.Action == "die" && e.ID == created.ID
	}).Data.(Event)
	if die.ExitCode == nil || *die.ExitCode != 137 {
		t.Fatalf("die event = %+v, want exit code 137 after a kill", die)
	}
	waitLive(t, cl, "stats_gone after the container died", func(m Message) bool {
		g, ok := m.Data.(StatsGoneMsg)
		return m.Event == MsgStatsGone && ok && g.ID == short
	})

	usage, at, cached, err := hub.DiskUsage(ctx, "live", true)
	if err != nil || cached || at.IsZero() || usage.Total < 0 || usage.Images.Count == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DiskUsage = %+v at %v cached %v err %v, want a fresh reading with at least the runner image", usage, at, cached, err)
	}
	t.Logf("disk usage: %+v", usage)
}

// waitLive reads the client's messages until pick accepts one (30 s at most).
func waitLive(t *testing.T, cl *Client, what string, pick func(Message) bool) Message {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.After(30 * time.Second)
	for {
		select {
		case m, ok := <-cl.Messages():
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("the stream closed while waiting for %s", what)
			}
			if pick(m) {
				return m
			}
		case <-deadline:
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
	}
}
```

**Create `internal/dockerwatch/AGENTS.md`**

````markdown
# Docker Manager live data

## Purpose and ownership

`internal/dockerwatch` is the Docker Manager's live data: one Engine events watcher per host, the stats sampler with its rings and the host gauges, the disk-usage cache, the per-host budget of streaming Engine connections, and the `Hub` that fans all of it out to the open `/api/docker-manager/stream` clients. The HTTP side (SSE writing, routes, the `dockerstacks` operation bridge, the terminal) lives in `internal/server`, the desktop app in `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager*.js`; hosts and Engine clients are `../dockerhost/AGENTS.md`, the design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-docker-manager-design.md`. The package's own code imports `dockerhost` and `dockerutil` only (the live test also `dockerstacks`); nothing in `tools`, `dockerhost`, `dockerutil` or `dockerstacks` may import it.

## Local contracts

- **Hub and clients** (`hub.go`, `client.go`). `New(hosts, Options)` runs nothing until a client subscribes or `WatchHost` is called. `Attach` opens a stream client (at most `MaxClients` = 32, then `ErrTooManyClients`; its id is 32 lowercase hex characters from `crypto/rand`); `Messages()` is a channel of 512 (`ClientBuffer`) that is closed on `Close`. A client that falls 512 messages behind is sent `dropped` (in place of its oldest unread message) and closed; the UI reconnects. `Set` replaces the client's whole subscription (`Hosts`, `Stats` host -> ids, `HostStats`) after checking all of it: at most `MaxSubscribedHosts` = 20 hosts per list (`ErrTooManyHosts`), `MaxStatsIDs` = 50 container ids per host (`ErrTooManyIDs`), ids are 12 to 64 hex characters and are reduced to their first 12, host ids match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`; every error matches `ErrInvalidSubscription` and a refused `Set` changes nothing. The hub does not know whether a host exists (the server checks that first); a host the registry has forgotten shows as `unreachable` with reason `host_not_found`.
- **Locking.** `Hub.mu` guards the clients, their subscriptions and all host runtimes; messages are pushed into the clients' buffered channels while it is held (a push never blocks), so a client sees messages in the order they were produced (`stats_history` before the live `stats` that follow it). Order of locks: `Hub.mu`, then `Client.mu`. `budgetMu`, `dfMu` and a df entry's gate are leaves and are never held while taking `Hub.mu`. `WatchHost` callbacks run on the watcher goroutine without any lock and must not block or call back into the hub. `Publish` never blocks; the `dockerstacks` observer may call it with the operation's locks held.
- **Events watcher** (`watcher.go`, `eventmap.go`). One per host while a client has the host in `Hosts` or a `WatchHost` callback exists; it stops `IdleStop` (30 s) after the last user, and a client that arrives sooner finds it running and is sent its current `host_status`. It holds one stream slot while it runs (it runs without one when the budget is used up). States: `connecting` until the Engine accepts `GET /events`, `live`, `unreachable` (no answer; `reason` is `dockerhost.ClassifyError`) and `paused` (the host answers but `/events` does not: three refused connects in a row, or three stream ends within a minute): the container list is polled every `PollInterval`, a `resync` (reason `poll`) is sent whenever the digest of (id, state, status, health) changes, and the feed is retried every `RetryPaused`. A feed established again after any interruption sends `resync` (reason `reconnect`). Reconnect delays are `Backoff` (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 s; the last repeats), a request the Engine never answers ends after `ConnectTimeout`. Container events forwarded: create start restart die stop kill pause unpause destroy rename oom update and `health_status: <x>` (action `health_status`, field `health`); everything else is dropped, image, volume and network events pass as they are. Only name, compose project and service, exit code and health are copied from the Engine's attributes; label values never reach a client.
- **Stats** (`stats.go`). Containers are sampled only when a client asks for their id: every `StatsInterval` (3 s), at most 4 Engine calls in flight per host (both sampling loops together), `stream=false` plus `one-shot=true` from API 1.41 (CPU from our own previous sample; the first sample is `-1`), plain `stream=false` below (CPU from `precpu_stats`). CPU is the container's percent of one core (the share of the system's CPU time times online CPUs); `-1` means unknown (no previous sample, system delta not positive, counter went backwards); a container that used no CPU reads 0. Memory is usage minus the cache (`RawStats.MemCache`). A ring holds 60 points; a client that starts asking for a container with a ring first receives `stats_history` (oldest first). A 404/409 answer or an all-zero sample (the Engine's answer for a stopped container) sends `stats_gone` once, frees the ring and stops sampling that id until a client asks again or a `start`/`restart`/`unpause` event for it arrives. A ring nobody sampled for 5 minutes is freed, and the loop ends when nothing is left.
- **Host gauges** (`gauges.go`). For a host with a `HostStats` subscriber: every `HostInterval` (10 s) the running containers are listed and up to `MaxHostSample` (100) of them sampled (`partial: true` above that); one that also has a stats ring with a point at most `HostInterval` old is not sampled again. `cpu` is the sum of the known container CPU values divided by the host's CPU count (`-1` while none is known; the second cycle follows after 2 s so the first reading is not a gap), `mem_used` the sum of memory, `mem_total` and `ncpu` come from `dockerhost.Info`, cached 5 minutes.
- **Disk usage** (`df.go`). `DiskUsage(ctx, host, refresh)` serves a cached `SystemDF` reading for 5 minutes; `refresh` re-reads only when the cache is older than 60 seconds; concurrent callers share one Engine call; a failed reading keeps the cache and returns the error. The Engine API reports no size of the file system, so the figure is Docker's own usage in bytes.
- **Stream budget** (`budget.go`). `Acquire(host)` takes one of `MaxStreamsPerHost` = 16 slots (events watcher, followed container logs, terminals) or fails with `ErrTooManyStreams`; the returned release can be called more than once.
- Engine and transport errors are returned unchanged; the server classifies them with `dockerhost.ClassifyError`. Message names are the `Msg*` constants and the JSON of the message types is the contract with the UI (`types.go`): change them together with `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-live.js`.

## Work guidance

- Tests use the fake Engine in `fakeengine_test.go` (an `httptest` server with `/version`, `/info`, `/containers/json`, `/system/df`, per-container stats generators and an `/events` feed the test writes to and drops), `newTestEnv` (a hub over host `h1` with intervals of a few milliseconds and an injected clock) and the `waitFor`/`waitUntil` helpers; none needs Docker. Keep waits short and drive time with `Options.Now`; sleeps over a few tens of milliseconds are a smell. `live_test.go` runs a throw-away container against a real Engine and is gated by `AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1`.
- New producers send through `Hub.publishLocked`/`Client.push` while holding `Hub.mu`; anything that calls into an Engine does so without it. A new background loop is started from `reconcileLocked` (with `h.wg.Add(1)`), stops with `h.ctx`, and clears its own flag under `Hub.mu` when it ends.

## Verification

```
go test ./internal/dockerwatch/... ./internal/dockerstacks/... ./internal/dockerhost/... ./internal/dockerutil/... -count=1
AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1 go test ./internal/dockerwatch/ -run TestLiveWatch -v -count=1 -timeout 5m
```

Run `go test -race ./internal/dockerwatch/` on a Linux box (no gcc on the planning machine; see `reference_aurago_test_server`).

## Child DOX Index

None.
````

## Part B: log follow, exec and the Docker Manager terminal (`internal/dockerhost`, `internal/dockerwatch`, `internal/server`)

### Part B notes

**What this part builds.** The server-side engine behind the Logs and Terminal tabs, without any route:

1. `internal/dockerhost/engine_logs_exec.go`: `FollowLogs` (a container's log as `LogLine`s, TTY and multiplexed, 16 KiB cap per line) and the exec calls `ExecCreate`, `ExecStart` (a hijacked `POST /exec/{id}/start` dialled through `Client.Dial` with the version `Client.APIVersion` negotiated), `ExecResize`, `ExecStartDetached`.
2. `internal/dockerwatch/logs*.go`: `Hub.FollowContainer` and `Hub.FollowProject` (history merged by timestamp, batches of 200 lines or 100 ms, project selection by compose labels and working dir, attach on `start` events, re-list after a watcher resync, stream-slot budget with `not_followed` notices).
3. `internal/server/docker_manager_terminal.go`: the second backend of the container terminal protocol over the exec calls (`newDockerManagerTerminalSession`), plus `serveContainerTerminalSessionWith`, the options (read limit, ping, pong wait) that only the Docker Manager route uses. `/api/containers` and the other terminals keep their exact behaviour.

Not in this part: the routes (`/logs?follow=1`, `/terminal`, the SSE writing, the host and protection rules) are Part C; the UI is Part D. Spec: "internal/dockerwatch", "Desktop app" (Logs, Terminal), "Security", "Error handling". Binding interfaces: `CONTRACT.md` ("Part B surface", "Log stream messages", decisions 3, 8 to 11, 15).

**Deviations from `CONTRACT.md`**

1. **`Opened` hooks (additive).** `dockerhost.LogOptions.Opened func()` and `dockerwatch.FollowOptions.Opened func()`: called once when the stream is established (the Engine accepted the log request; for a project: the project was listed), before the first line or notice. An error that comes first (unknown container 404, no free slot `ErrTooManyStreams`, unreachable host, refused request) is returned without a call. Reason: the contract wants 429 `too_many_streams` and the usual 404/502 answers for a log follow *and* an SSE answer; without the hook the route cannot know whether it may still answer with a plain status. Side effect: `LogOptions` holds a func and cannot be compared with `==`.
2. **`ProjectSelector.Matches` is exported** (the contract has the struct only): Part C needs it to answer 404 `project_not_found` for an external project before it starts the stream.
3. **`FollowOptions.Tail`**: `0` = no history, clamped to `MaxLogTail` (5000); a `Since` without a `Tail` asks for the last 5000 lines since then (the Engine takes no history with `tail=0`). The defaults of the contract (200 for a container, 100 for a project) are applied by the route (Part C), not here.
4. **Extra exported names**: `dockerhost.MaxLogLineBytes`, `dockerhost.ErrInvalidExecID`; `dockerwatch.MaxLogTail`, `MaxLogHistory`, `NoticeNotFollowed`, `NoticeAttached`, `NoticeDetached`, `NoticeTruncatedHistory`.
5. **`ExecCreate(tty=false)`** attaches nothing (no stdin, stdout or stderr): it is the helper exec of `End`, started with `ExecStartDetached`. `tty=true` attaches all three, like the existing terminal payload.
6. **Project history reads take no stream slot.** The per-container history reads of a project follower are short non-follow requests (four at a time, each given up after 30 s and then reported as not followed, so a hung host cannot hold back the other containers' history); only open live streams hold an `Acquire` slot. A project follower reads the history of stopped containers too but follows only running, paused or restarting ones.
7. **`FollowContainer` ignores its `notice` callback** (kept for the signature; notices exist for projects).
8. **Notice texts are English.** The UI localizes by `code`, `services` and `container`; `message` is the fallback.
9. **Extra test file** `internal/server/containers_terminal_options_test.go` (the options tests live next to the existing terminal tests).

**Notes for Part C (routes)**

- **Single container** (`GET /hosts/{h}/containers/{ref}/logs?follow=1`): call `hub.FollowContainer(r.Context(), host, ref, dockerwatch.FollowOptions{Tail, Since, Opened}, out, notice)` on the handler goroutine. Parse `tail` (default 200, 0..5000, otherwise 400) and `since` (RFC 3339) first. Put the SSE headers and the first flush into `Opened`. An error returned before `Opened` was called is a plain JSON answer: `errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrTooManyStreams)` is 429 `too_many_streams`, `dockerhost.StatusOf(err) == 404` is the unknown container, everything else goes through `dockerhost.ClassifyError`. After `Opened`: a nil return is `end {reason: "ended"}`, `context.Canceled` (the client left) sends nothing, any other error is `end {reason: "error", code, message}`. `out` becomes the SSE event `lines` (JSON of the `LogBatch`), `notice` the event `notice`.
- `out` and `notice` are never called concurrently with each other, but the 15 s comment heartbeat is the route's own goroutine: give it the same write mutex as `out` and `notice`. A failing `out` (client gone, write deadline) ends the follow; return that error from `out`.
- **Project / stack** routes: `hub.FollowProject(ctx, host, sel, opt, out, notice)`. Managed stack: `ProjectSelector{Project: name, WorkingDir: <stacks_dir>/<name>}`. External project: `{Project: project}`, or `{Project: project, WorkingDir: <stack folder>, Exclude: true}` when a stack of that name exists. `404 project_not_found`: list with `dockerhost.ListContainers` and count `sel.Matches`; a stack without containers is a valid stream (nothing is sent until one starts). Default `tail` 100. `FollowProject` returns only when the context ends, when `out` fails or when the project cannot be listed at the start.
- **Terminal route**: after the checks of decision 11 take a slot with `release, err := hub.Acquire(host)` (429 on `ErrTooManyStreams`) and `defer release()`; create the session before the upgrade like the existing handler (`newDockerManagerTerminalSession(r.Context(), client, ref, 120, 30)`: a `*dockerhost.StatusError` 404 is gone, 409 is `container_not_running`; the rest through `ClassifyError`); upgrade with `containerTerminalUpgrader`; then `serveDockerManagerTerminal(r.Context(), conn, session)`. If the request context ended before the upgrade, `session.Close()` and answer 408 as the existing handler does.
- The hub's `Close` does not wait for followers: their contexts are the requests' contexts.

**Open points** (to confirm with the live tests of Task B6, `AURAGO_DOCKER_WATCH_LIVE=1`)

- That a real Engine delivers the `tail=N&since=T` combination as the project follower assumes (tail first, then the `since` filter), and that `tail=0&follow=1` starts at the end of the log. Both are the documented behaviour of the json-file and local log drivers; the live follow test checks that the numbered lines of history and live part are consecutive.
- A crash-looping container makes the project follower send a `detached`/`attached` pair per restart, at most one per second. If that is too chatty in the UI, Part D can fold them.

### Task B1: `dockerhost.FollowLogs`: a container's log as lines

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerhost/engine_logs_exec.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerhost/engine_logs_test.go`

`FollowLogs` is the Engine call under every log follow. It reads `Config.Tty` once (`GET /containers/{id}/json`), then asks `GET /containers/{id}/logs` with `stdout=1&stderr=1&timestamps=1`, `follow`, `tail` (clamped to 0..5000) and `since` (`seconds.nanoseconds`) on `Client.StreamingHTTPClient()`, which has no total timeout, so only the context ends a followed log. A TTY stream is read raw, any other one is demultiplexed with the existing `DemuxStreams` (its frame parser is the one `ContainerLogs` uses). The bytes are cut into `LogLine`s by a small writer per stream: the Engine's timestamp moves into `LogLine.Time`, a trailing carriage return goes, invalid UTF-8 is replaced, and a line longer than `MaxLogLineBytes` (16 KiB) is cut on a character boundary and flagged `Truncated`; the rest of that line is dropped while it is read, so the memory per call is one line. A last line without a newline is delivered at the end. The return value is nil when the log ended, `ctx.Err()` when the context ended and the callback's own error when it failed; an Engine refusal is a `*StatusError`. `LogOptions.Opened` is called once when the Engine has accepted the request. Tests use the fake Engine of `fakeengine_test.go` (`fe.on`, `fe.json`, `muxFrame`).

```go
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

const logTS = "2026-10-28T07:33:29.123456789Z"

// logsEngine registers the container "web" with the given Tty flag and serves
// its log with body.
func logsEngine(t *testing.T, tty bool, body func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)) *fakeEngine {
	t.Helper()
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	if tty {
		fe.json("GET", "/containers/web/json", http.StatusOK, `{"Config":{"Tty":true}}`)
	} else {
		fe.json("GET", "/containers/web/json", http.StatusOK, `{"Config":{"Tty":false}}`)
	}
	fe.on("GET", "/containers/web/logs", body)
	return fe
}

func collectLogs(t *testing.T, fe *fakeEngine, opt LogOptions) ([]LogLine, error) {
	t.Helper()
	var lines []LogLine
	err := FollowLogs(context.Background(), fe.client(t), "web", opt, func(l LogLine) error {
		lines = append(lines, l)
		return nil
	})
	return lines, err
}

func TestFollowLogsDemultiplexesAndStripsTimestamps(t *testing.T) {
	var query url.Values
	fe := logsEngine(t, false, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		query = r.URL.Query()
		var b bytes.Buffer
		b.Write(muxFrame(1, logTS+" hello\n"))
		b.Write(muxFrame(2, "2026-10-28T07:33:30.000000001Z boom\n"))
		// one line split across two frames, then two lines in one frame
		b.Write(muxFrame(1, "2026-10-28T07:33:31.5Z part"))
		b.Write(muxFrame(1, "ial\n2026-10-28T07:33:32Z a\n2026-10-28T07:33:33Z b\n"))
		b.Write(muxFrame(1, "2026-10-28T07:33:34Z no newline at the end"))
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/vnd.docker.multiplexed-stream")
		_, _ = w.Write(b.Bytes())
	})
	since := time.Unix(1730000000, 123).UTC()
	opened := 0
	lines, err := collectLogs(t, fe, LogOptions{Tail: 50, Since: since, Follow: true, Opened: func() { opened++ }})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FollowLogs: %v", err)
	}
	if opened != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Opened was called %d times, want once", opened)
	}
	want := []LogLine{
		{Stream: "out", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 29, 123456789, time.UTC), Text: "hello"},
		{Stream: "err", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 30, 1, time.UTC), Text: "boom"},
		{Stream: "out", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 31, 500000000, time.UTC), Text: "partial"},
		{Stream: "out", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 32, 0, time.UTC), Text: "a"},
		{Stream: "out", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 33, 0, time.UTC), Text: "b"},
		{Stream: "out", Time: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 34, 0, time.UTC), Text: "no newline at the end"},
	}
	if !slices.Equal(lines, want) {
		t.Fatalf("lines = %+v\nwant %+v", lines, want)
	}
	for key, value := range map[string]string{"follow": "1", "tail": "50", "timestamps": "1", "stdout": "1", "stderr": "1", "since": "1730000000.000000123"} {
		if got := query.Get(key); got != value {
			t.Errorf("query %s = %q, want %q (query %v)", key, got, value, query)
		}
	}
}

func TestFollowLogsReadsATTYStreamRaw(t *testing.T) {
	long := strings.Repeat("a", MaxLogLineBytes+5000)
	euro := strings.Repeat("€", MaxLogLineBytes) // 3 bytes each: the cut falls inside a character
	fe := logsEngine(t, true, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" first\r\n")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" "+long+"\r\n")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" "+euro+"\n")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" \x1b[31mred\x1b[0m\n")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, "no timestamp here\n")
	})
	before := time.Now().Add(-time.Second)
	lines, err := collectLogs(t, fe, LogOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FollowLogs: %v", err)
	}
	if len(lines) != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("got %d lines, want 5: %+v", len(lines), lines)
	}
	if lines[0].Text != "first" || lines[0].Stream != "out" || lines[0].Truncated {
		t.Fatalf("line 0 = %+v, want the text without the carriage return", lines[0])
	}
	if !lines[1].Truncated || lines[1].Text != long[:MaxLogLineBytes] {
		t.Fatalf("long line: truncated=%v len=%d, want a cut at %d", lines[1].Truncated, len(lines[1].Text), MaxLogLineBytes)
	}
	if !lines[2].Truncated || !utf8.ValidString(lines[2].Text) || len(lines[2].Text) != MaxLogLineBytes-1 {
		t.Fatalf("multi-byte line: truncated=%v valid=%v len=%d, want a cut on a character boundary at %d",
			lines[2].Truncated, utf8.ValidString(lines[2].Text), len(lines[2].Text), MaxLogLineBytes-1)
	}
	if lines[3].Text != "\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m" || lines[3].Truncated {
		t.Fatalf("ANSI line = %+v, want the escape sequences kept", lines[3])
	}
	if lines[4].Text != "no timestamp here" || lines[4].Time.Before(before) {
		t.Fatalf("line without a timestamp = %+v, want the whole text and the arrival time", lines[4])
	}
}

func TestFollowLogsReturnsTheCallbackErrorAndStopsOnContext(t *testing.T) {
	handlerDone := make(chan struct{})
	fe := logsEngine(t, true, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		defer close(handlerDone)
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" one\n"+logTS+" two\n")
		w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
		<-r.Context().Done() // a followed log that stays quiet
	})
	c := fe.client(t)

	stop := errors.New("stop here")
	calls := 0
	err := FollowLogs(context.Background(), c, "web", LogOptions{Follow: true}, func(LogLine) error {
		calls++
		return stop
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, stop) || calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("FollowLogs = %v after %d calls, want the callback error after the first line", err, calls)
	}
	<-handlerDone

	fe2 := logsEngine(t, true, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logTS+" one\n")
		w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
		<-r.Context().Done()
	})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	got := make(chan error, 1)
	first := make(chan struct{}, 1)
	go func() {
		got <- FollowLogs(ctx, fe2.client(t), "web", LogOptions{Follow: true}, func(LogLine) error {
			select {
			case first <- struct{}{}:
			default:
			}
			return nil
		})
	}()
	select {
	case <-first:
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("no line arrived")
	}
	cancel()
	select {
	case err := <-got:
		if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
			t.Fatalf("FollowLogs after cancel = %v, want context.Canceled", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("FollowLogs did not return after the context ended")
	}
}

func TestFollowLogsReportsEngineAnswers(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	c := fe.client(t)
	opened := func() { t.Error("Opened was called although the Engine refused the request") }
	err := FollowLogs(context.Background(), c, "gone", LogOptions{Opened: opened}, func(LogLine) error { return nil })
	if StatusOf(err) != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("unknown container: %v (status %d), want 404", err, StatusOf(err))
	}
	fe.json("GET", "/containers/web/json", http.StatusOK, `{"Config":{"Tty":false}}`)
	fe.json("GET", "/containers/web/logs", http.StatusNotImplemented, `{"message":"configured logging driver does not support reading"}`)
	err = FollowLogs(context.Background(), c, "web", LogOptions{Opened: opened}, func(LogLine) error { return nil })
	if StatusOf(err) != http.StatusNotImplemented || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "does not support reading") {
		t.Fatalf("log driver without reads: %v (status %d), want the 501 answer", err, StatusOf(err))
	}
	if err := FollowLogs(context.Background(), c, "../x", LogOptions{}, func(LogLine) error { return nil }); !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidContainerRef) {
		t.Fatalf("unsafe reference: %v, want ErrInvalidContainerRef", err)
	}
}

func TestLogQueryClampsTailAndFormatsSince(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		opt  LogOptions
		want string
	}{
		{LogOptions{}, "stderr=1&stdout=1&tail=0&timestamps=1"},
		{LogOptions{Tail: 200, Follow: true}, "follow=1&stderr=1&stdout=1&tail=200&timestamps=1"},
		{LogOptions{Tail: 99999}, "stderr=1&stdout=1&tail=5000&timestamps=1"},
		{LogOptions{Tail: -3}, "stderr=1&stdout=1&tail=0&timestamps=1"},
		{LogOptions{Tail: 100, Follow: true, Since: time.Unix(1730000000, 5).UTC()}, "follow=1&since=1730000000.000000005&stderr=1&stdout=1&tail=100&timestamps=1"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		if got := logQuery(tc.opt); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("logQuery(%+v) = %q, want %q", tc.opt, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerhost

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// MaxLogLineBytes is the longest log line text FollowLogs delivers. A longer
// line is cut (on a character boundary) and flagged Truncated; the rest of that
// line is dropped without being buffered.
const MaxLogLineBytes = 16 << 10

// logTimestampMax bounds the timestamp prefix the Engine puts in front of a line
// (RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, "2026-10-28T07:33:29.123456789Z" is 30 bytes).
const logTimestampMax = 48

// LogOptions selects what FollowLogs reads.
type LogOptions struct {
	// Tail is the number of history lines (0..5000, anything else is clamped)
	// taken from the end of the log; 0 means no history. The Engine applies Since
	// to the lines Tail selects, and a Tail of 0 follows from the end of the log,
	// so Since brings lines older than "now" only together with a Tail.
	Tail int
	// Since limits the lines to the ones at or after this time; zero = not set.
	Since time.Time
	// Follow keeps the stream open for new lines until the container stops.
	Follow bool
	// Opened, when set, is called once when the Engine has accepted the request
	// and before the first line is delivered. An error that comes before it (an
	// unknown container, a refusal) is never followed by a call, so a caller
	// that streams the lines on can still answer such an error as a plain
	// response. Because of this field a LogOptions cannot be compared with ==.
	Opened func()
}

// LogLine is one line of a container log.
type LogLine struct {
	Stream    string    // "out" | "err" ("out" for TTY containers)
	Time      time.Time // from the Engine timestamp (timestamps=1 is always sent)
	Text      string    // without the timestamp and the trailing newline, at most MaxLogLineBytes
	Truncated bool      // the line was longer than MaxLogLineBytes
}

// logSink carries the callback of one FollowLogs call and the first error it
// returned, so the caller can tell a callback error from a read error.
type logSink struct {
	fn  func(LogLine) error
	err error
	now func() time.Time
}

// logLineSplitter is the io.Writer behind one stream (stdout or stderr) of a
// log. It cuts the bytes into lines, strips the Engine's timestamp and keeps at
// most one capped line in memory.
type logLineSplitter struct {
	stream string
	sink   *logSink
	buf    []byte
	over   bool // the current line exceeded the buffer; its remaining bytes are dropped
}

const logLineBufMax = logTimestampMax + 1 + MaxLogLineBytes

func (s *logLineSplitter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	total := len(p)
	for len(p) > 0 {
		i := bytes.IndexByte(p, '\n')
		if i < 0 {
			s.keep(p)
			return total, nil
		}
		s.keep(p[:i])
		p = p[i+1:]
		if err := s.emit(); err != nil {
			return total - len(p), err
		}
	}
	return total, nil
}

func (s *logLineSplitter) keep(chunk []byte) {
	room := logLineBufMax - len(s.buf)
	if room <= 0 {
		if len(chunk) > 0 {
			s.over = true
		}
		return
	}
	if len(chunk) > room {
		s.buf = append(s.buf, chunk[:room]...)
		s.over = true
		return
	}
	s.buf = append(s.buf, chunk...)
}

// finish emits a last line that has no trailing newline.
func (s *logLineSplitter) finish() error {
	if len(s.buf) == 0 && !s.over {
		return nil
	}
	return s.emit()
}

func (s *logLineSplitter) emit() error {
	line := s.buf
	truncated := s.over
	s.buf = s.buf[:0]
	s.over = false
	if s.sink.err != nil {
		return s.sink.err
	}
	line = bytes.TrimSuffix(line, []byte{'\r'})
	at, text := splitLogTimestamp(line, s.sink.now)
	if len(text) > MaxLogLineBytes {
		cut := MaxLogLineBytes
		for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(text[cut]) {
			cut--
		}
		text = text[:cut]
		truncated = true
	}
	out := LogLine{Stream: s.stream, Time: at, Text: strings.ToValidUTF8(string(text), string(utf8.RuneError)), Truncated: truncated}
	if err := s.sink.fn(out); err != nil {
		s.sink.err = err
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

// splitLogTimestamp separates the Engine's timestamp prefix from the text. A line
// without a parsable prefix keeps its whole text and gets the time of arrival.
func splitLogTimestamp(line []byte, now func() time.Time) (time.Time, []byte) {
	head, rest := line, []byte(nil)
	if sp := bytes.IndexByte(line, ' '); sp >= 0 {
		head, rest = line[:sp], line[sp+1:]
	}
	if len(head) >= len("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z") && len(head) <= logTimestampMax {
		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, string(head)); err == nil {
			return t.UTC(), rest
		}
	}
	return now().UTC(), line
}

// logQuery builds the query of GET /containers/{id}/logs.
func logQuery(opt LogOptions) string {
	q := url.Values{}
	q.Set("stdout", "1")
	q.Set("stderr", "1")
	q.Set("timestamps", "1")
	if opt.Follow {
		q.Set("follow", "1")
	}
	q.Set("tail", strconv.Itoa(min(max(opt.Tail, 0), logTailMax)))
	if !opt.Since.IsZero() {
		since := opt.Since.UTC()
		q.Set("since", fmt.Sprintf("%d.%09d", since.Unix(), since.Nanosecond()))
	}
	return q.Encode()
}

// FollowLogs streams a container's log lines to fn until ctx ends, the log ends
// (the container stopped, or the log was not followed) or fn fails. It reads
// Config.Tty once and demultiplexes non-TTY streams; the Engine's timestamps
// are always requested and removed from the text. It returns nil when the log
// ended, ctx.Err() when ctx ended, the error of fn when fn failed and a
// *StatusError (404 gone, 409 and others) when the Engine refused the request.
// The request uses the streaming client of c, which has no total timeout.
func FollowLogs(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, ref string, opt LogOptions, fn func(LogLine) error) error {
	if err := validateContainerRef(ref); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var inspect struct {
		Config struct {
			Tty bool `json:"Tty"`
		} `json:"Config"`
	}
	esc := url.PathEscape(ref)
	if err := engineJSON(ctx, c, http.MethodGet, "containers/"+esc+"/json", &inspect); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, dockerutil.Endpoint("containers/"+esc+"/logs?"+logQuery(opt)), nil)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	resp, err := c.StreamingHTTPClient().Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		if ctx.Err() != nil {
			return ctx.Err()
		}
		return fmt.Errorf("Docker request: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(dockerutil.EngineErrorMessage(dockerutil.ReadErrorBody(resp.Body)), 512)
		return &StatusError{Status: resp.StatusCode, Err: fmt.Errorf("Docker API returned %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, message)}
	}

	if opt.Opened != nil {
		opt.Opened()
	}
	sink := &logSink{fn: fn, now: time.Now}
	stdout := &logLineSplitter{stream: "out", sink: sink}
	stderr := &logLineSplitter{stream: "err", sink: sink}
	var readErr error
	if inspect.Config.Tty {
		_, readErr = io.Copy(stdout, resp.Body)
	} else {
		readErr = DemuxStreams(resp.Body, stdout, stderr)
	}
	switch {
	case sink.err != nil:
		return sink.err
	case ctx.Err() != nil:
		return ctx.Err()
	case readErr != nil:
		return fmt.Errorf("read container logs: %w", readErr)
	}
	if err := stdout.finish(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return stderr.finish()
}
```

- Modify: `internal/dockerhost/AGENTS.md`

The four calls the Docker Manager terminal is built from, all on a `*dockerutil.Client`: `ExecCreate` (`tty=true` is an interactive session with a pseudo terminal and stdin, stdout and stderr attached; `tty=false` attaches nothing, it is the helper that `End` starts), `ExecStart`, `ExecResize` and `ExecStartDetached` (`{"Detach":true,"Tty":false}`). `ExecStart` writes the same hand-built upgrade request as `openDockerExecStartStream` in `internal/server/containers_terminal.go` (`POST /v<version>/exec/{id}/start`, `Connection: Upgrade`, `Upgrade: tcp`, body `{"Detach":false,"Tty":true}`; `101` or `200` answers), but on a connection from `Client.Dial` and with the version `Client.APIVersion` negotiated instead of `tools.DockerConfig`, which is what makes the terminal work on TLS, mutual TLS and SSH hosts (decision 3). The returned stream reads through the buffer that parsed the response header, so bytes the Engine sent right behind it are not lost; it exposes `SetWriteDeadline` (the serve loop's stalled-stdin bound), and `Close` closes the connection. The context bounds the handshake only (a peer that never answers is cut off when it ends); the stream outlives it. A refusal is a `*StatusError` (404 unknown exec, 409 container not running or paused). This task edits the file B1 created (two edits: the import block, then the exec code appended after `FollowLogs`) and adds the `dockerhost` guide bullet for B1 and B2.

```go
// seenExec is what the hijacking fake saw of the exec start request.
type seenExec struct {
	method, path, body string
	header             http.Header
}

// hijackExec answers POST /exec/<id>/start like dockerd: 101 and then a raw
// duplex stream, here an echo of whatever the client writes.
func hijackExec(t *testing.T, fe *fakeEngine, route string, seen *seenExec, firstBytes string) {
	t.Helper()
	fe.on("POST", route, func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
		seen.method, seen.path, seen.header, seen.body = r.Method, r.URL.Path, r.Header.Clone(), string(body)
		conn, buf, err := w.(http.Hijacker).Hijack()
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("hijack: %v", err)
			return
		}
		defer conn.Close()
		// The header and the first stream bytes leave in one write.
		_, _ = buf.WriteString("HTTP/1.1 101 UPGRADED\r\nContent-Type: application/vnd.docker.raw-stream\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: tcp\r\n\r\n" + firstBytes)
		_ = buf.Flush()
		chunk := make([]byte, 64)
		for {
			n, err := buf.Read(chunk)
			if n > 0 {
				_, _ = conn.Write(chunk[:n])
			}
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
		}
	})
}

func TestExecStartHijacksTheConnectionWithTheNegotiatedVersion(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	fe.setVersion("1.43", "24.0.0")
	var seen seenExec
	hijackExec(t, fe, "/exec/e1e1e1/start", &seen, "prompt$ ")
	c := fe.client(t)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	stream, err := ExecStart(ctx, c, "e1e1e1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ExecStart: %v", err)
	}
	defer stream.Close()

	got := make([]byte, len("prompt$ "))
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(stream, got); err != nil || string(got) != "prompt$ " {
		t.Fatalf("first stream bytes = %q, %v; the bytes behind the response header must not be lost", got, err)
	}
	if _, err := stream.Write([]byte("ls\r")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write: %v", err)
	}
	echo := make([]byte, 3)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(stream, echo); err != nil || string(echo) != "ls\r" {
		t.Fatalf("echo = %q, %v", echo, err)
	}
	if _, ok := stream.(interface{ SetWriteDeadline(time.Time) error }); !ok {
		t.Fatal("the stream must expose SetWriteDeadline for the terminal's write bound")
	}

	if seen.path != "/v1.43/exec/e1e1e1/start" || seen.method != http.MethodPost {
		t.Fatalf("request = %s %s, want POST /v1.43/exec/e1e1e1/start (the negotiated version)", seen.method, seen.path)
	}
	if !strings.EqualFold(seen.header.Get("Connection"), "Upgrade") || seen.header.Get("Upgrade") != "tcp" || seen.header.Get("Content-Type") != "application/json" {
		t.Fatalf("headers = %v, want an upgrade to tcp with a JSON body", seen.header)
	}
	if seen.body != `{"Detach":false,"Tty":true}` {
		t.Fatalf("body = %q", seen.body)
	}
	if err := stream.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Close: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := stream.Read(make([]byte, 1)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Read after Close must fail")
	}
}

func TestExecStartReportsRefusalsAndHonoursTheContext(t *testing.T) {
	fe := newFakeEngine(t)
	fe.on("POST", "/exec/dead/start", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict)
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"message":"Container abc is paused"}`)
	})
	silent := make(chan struct{})
	t.Cleanup(func() { close(silent) })
	fe.on("POST", "/exec/silent/start", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		select { // a peer that accepts the request and never answers
		case <-silent:
		case <-r.Context().Done():
		}
	})
	c := fe.client(t)

	_, err := ExecStart(context.Background(), c, "dead")
	if StatusOf(err) != http.StatusConflict || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "is paused") {
		t.Fatalf("refused start: %v (status %d), want the 409 answer", err, StatusOf(err))
	}
	if _, err := ExecStart(context.Background(), c, "unknown"); StatusOf(err) != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("unknown exec: %v (status %d), want 404", err, StatusOf(err))
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
	defer cancel()
	began := time.Now()
	if _, err := ExecStart(ctx, c, "silent"); !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		t.Fatalf("silent peer: %v, want the context deadline", err)
	}
	if time.Since(began) > 5*time.Second {
		t.Fatal("ExecStart held the handshake past the context")
	}
	if _, err := ExecStart(context.Background(), c, "../x"); !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidExecID) {
		t.Fatalf("unsafe exec id: %v, want ErrInvalidExecID", err)
	}
}
```

```go
// execStartBody is the body of POST /exec/{id}/start.
type execStartBody struct {
	Detach bool `json:"Detach"`
	Tty    bool `json:"Tty"`
}

type execCreateBody struct {
	AttachStdin  bool     `json:"AttachStdin"`
	AttachStdout bool     `json:"AttachStdout"`
	AttachStderr bool     `json:"AttachStderr"`
	Tty          bool     `json:"Tty"`
	Cmd          []string `json:"Cmd"`
	Env          []string `json:"Env,omitempty"`
}

// ErrInvalidExecID is returned for an exec id that is unsafe in an API path.
var ErrInvalidExecID = errors.New("invalid exec id")

func validateExecID(id string) error {
	if validateContainerRef(id) != nil {
		return ErrInvalidExecID
	}
	return nil
}

// execJSON is Client.DoJSON with a request body that wraps a non-2xx answer in
// a *StatusError.
func execJSON(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, method, path string, body, out any) error {
	status, err := c.DoJSON(ctx, method, path, body, out)
	if err != nil && status != 0 && (status < 200 || status >= 300) {
		return &StatusError{Status: status, Err: err}
	}
	return err
}

// ExecCreate creates an exec in a running container and returns its id. With
// tty it is an interactive session: a pseudo terminal with stdin, stdout and
// stderr attached. Without tty nothing is attached (a helper to be started
// with ExecStartDetached). Env entries are "NAME=value".
func ExecCreate(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, ref string, cmd, env []string, tty bool) (string, error) {
	if err := validateContainerRef(ref); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if len(cmd) == 0 {
		return "", errors.New("exec command is empty")
	}
	body := execCreateBody{AttachStdin: tty, AttachStdout: tty, AttachStderr: tty, Tty: tty, Cmd: cmd, Env: env}
	var created struct {
		ID string `json:"Id"`
	}
	if err := execJSON(ctx, c, http.MethodPost, "containers/"+url.PathEscape(ref)+"/exec", body, &created); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if created.ID == "" {
		return "", errors.New("Docker exec create returned no id")
	}
	return created.ID, nil
}

// ExecStart hijacks POST /exec/{id}/start ({"Detach":false,"Tty":true}). The
// connection is dialled with c.Dial and the request is written with the API
// version c.APIVersion negotiated, so TLS, mutual TLS and SSH hosts work like
// the local socket. The result is the raw terminal stream; Read is buffered (it
// returns bytes the Engine sent right behind the response header) and Close
// closes the connection. ctx bounds the handshake only: the stream outlives it.
// An Engine refusal is a *StatusError (404 unknown exec, 409 container not
// running or paused).
func ExecStart(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, execID string) (io.ReadWriteCloser, error) {
	if err := validateExecID(execID); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	version, err := c.APIVersion(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	conn, err := c.Dial(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("connect to Docker engine: %w", err)
	}
	// A peer that never answers must not hold the handshake past ctx.
	stop := context.AfterFunc(ctx, func() { _ = conn.Close() })
	stream, err := execUpgrade(ctx, conn, version, execID)
	if err != nil {
		stop()
		_ = conn.Close()
		if ctx.Err() != nil {
			return nil, ctx.Err()
		}
		return nil, err
	}
	if !stop() { // ctx ended while the handshake finished: the connection is closed
		_ = conn.Close()
		return nil, ctx.Err()
	}
	return stream, nil
}

func execUpgrade(ctx context.Context, conn net.Conn, version, execID string) (*execStream, error) {
	body, _ := json.Marshal(execStartBody{Detach: false, Tty: true})
	target := "http://docker/v" + strings.TrimPrefix(version, "v") + "/exec/" + url.PathEscape(execID) + "/start"
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, target, bytes.NewReader(body))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("build docker exec start request: %w", err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	req.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
	req.Header.Set("Upgrade", "tcp")
	if err := req.Write(conn); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("send docker exec start request: %w", err)
	}
	reader := bufio.NewReader(conn)
	resp, err := http.ReadResponse(reader, req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read docker exec start response: %w", err)
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK && resp.StatusCode != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
		defer resp.Body.Close()
		message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(dockerutil.EngineErrorMessage(dockerutil.ReadErrorBody(resp.Body)), 512)
		return nil, &StatusError{Status: resp.StatusCode, Err: fmt.Errorf("Docker API returned %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, message)}
	}
	return &execStream{Conn: conn, reader: reader}, nil
}

// execStream is a hijacked exec connection. Reads go through the buffer that
// parsed the response header; everything else (Write, Close, the deadlines)
// is the connection's.
type execStream struct {
	net.Conn
	reader *bufio.Reader
}

func (s *execStream) Read(p []byte) (int, error) { return s.reader.Read(p) }

// ExecResize sets the size of an exec's terminal.
func ExecResize(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, execID string, cols, rows int) error {
	if err := validateExecID(execID); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if cols <= 0 || rows <= 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid terminal size %dx%d", cols, rows)
	}
	return engineJSON(ctx, c, http.MethodPost, fmt.Sprintf("exec/%s/resize?h=%d&w=%d", url.PathEscape(execID), rows, cols), nil)
}

// ExecStartDetached starts an exec in the background ({"Detach":true,"Tty":false});
// the Engine answers when the process has started.
func ExecStartDetached(ctx context.Context, c *dockerutil.Client, execID string) error {
	if err := validateExecID(execID); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return execJSON(ctx, c, http.MethodPost, "exec/"+url.PathEscape(execID)+"/start", execStartBody{Detach: true, Tty: false}, nil)
}
```

with:

```markdown
- Log follow and exec (`engine_logs_exec.go`): `FollowLogs` inspects `Config.Tty` once, always sends `timestamps=1`, reads a TTY stream raw and demultiplexes the others with `DemuxStreams`, moves the Engine's timestamp into `LogLine.Time` (a line without one gets the arrival time) and cuts a line at `MaxLogLineBytes` (16 KiB, on a character boundary, flagged `Truncated`; the rest of that line is dropped while reading, never buffered). It returns nil when the log ends, `ctx.Err()` when the context ended and the callback's own error; the request uses `Client.StreamingHTTPClient()` (no total timeout). `LogOptions.Opened` is called once when the Engine has accepted the request, before the first line, and never when an error comes first (unknown container, refusal): a route that streams the lines on can answer such an error as a plain response and switch to an event stream from there (the field makes `LogOptions` incomparable with `==`). `LogOptions.Tail` is clamped to 0..5000; 0 follows from the end of the log, so `Since` brings older lines only together with a `Tail` (the Engine applies `Since` to the lines the tail selects). `ExecStart` hijacks `POST /exec/{id}/start` over `Client.Dial` with the version `Client.APIVersion` negotiated (no `tools.DockerConfig`), so TLS, mutual TLS and SSH hosts work like the local socket; `ctx` bounds the handshake only, the returned stream is buffered for reads and its `Close` closes the connection. `ExecCreate` with `tty` attaches stdin, stdout and stderr to a pseudo terminal, without it nothing is attached (a helper for `ExecStartDetached`). Refusals are a `*StatusError` (404 unknown container or exec, 409 container not running or paused). Verify `TestFollowLogs*`, `TestLogQuery*` and `TestExec*`.
- Redaction reuses the admin inspect:
```

### Task B3: dockerwatch log types and the line batcher

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_types.go`
- Create: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_batch.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_types_test.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_batch_test.go`

The JSON types of the log stream (`LogEntry`, `LogBatch`, `Notice` with its four codes), `FollowOptions` (with the `Opened` hook and the rule that turns `Tail`/`Since` into an Engine tail), `ProjectSelector` with `Matches`, the limits, and `logBatcher`. The batcher turns single entries into `LogBatch` messages: a batch leaves when it has 200 entries or 100 ms after its first entry. All calls to `out` and `notice` run under one mutex in the order the entries and notices were added, so the receiver never sees concurrent calls and a notice always comes after the lines added before it; because a flush runs under the mutex a slow receiver slows the producers (back pressure instead of an unbounded buffer). The first error of `out` or `notice` is sticky and reported once to an `onFail` hook, which makes the follower stop reading instead of waiting for its next line. The timer is injected, so the tests fire it by hand. `ProjectSelector.Matches` compares compose project and cleaned working dir (see the type's comment). B4 and B5 use these files; the constants for the project follower live here too.

```go
	"time"
)

// logsFakeTimers is a timer source that fires only when the test says so.
type logsFakeTimers struct {
	armed   int
	stopped int
	fn      func()
}

type logsFakeTimer struct {
	owner *logsFakeTimers
	live  bool
}

func (t *logsFakeTimer) Stop() bool {
	was := t.live
	t.live = false
	if was {
		t.owner.stopped++
	}
	return was
}

func (f *logsFakeTimers) after(_ time.Duration, fn func()) logTimer {
	f.armed++
	t := &logsFakeTimer{owner: f, live: true}
	f.fn = func() {
		if t.live {
			t.live = false
			fn()
		}
	}
	return t
}

func (f *logsFakeTimers) fire() {
	if f.fn != nil {
		f.fn()
	}
}

// logsBase is the time of line 0 in the log fixtures.
var logsBase = time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

func logsEntry(text string) LogEntry { return LogEntry{T: logsBase, S: "out", Text: text} }

func TestLogBatcherFlushesOnTheTimerAndWhenFull(t *testing.T) {
	var batches []LogBatch
	timers := &logsFakeTimers{}
	b := newLogBatcher(func(b LogBatch) error { batches = append(batches, b); return nil }, nil, nil, 3, 100*time.Millisecond, timers.after)

	_ = b.add(logsEntry("a"))
	_ = b.add(logsEntry("b"))
	if len(batches) != 0 || timers.armed != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("after two lines: %d batches, %d timers armed; want none sent and one timer for the batch", len(batches), timers.armed)
	}
	timers.fire()
	if len(batches) != 1 || len(batches[0].Lines) != 2 || batches[0].Lines[0].Text != "a" || batches[0].Lines[1].Text != "b" {
		t.Fatalf("batches after the timer = %+v, want one batch a,b", batches)
	}

	_ = b.add(logsEntry("c"))
	_ = b.add(logsEntry("d"))
	_ = b.add(logsEntry("e")) // the third line fills the batch
	if len(batches) != 2 || len(batches[1].Lines) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("batches after a full batch = %+v, want a second batch c,d,e at once", batches)
	}
	timers.fire() // the timer of that batch was stopped: nothing is left to send
	if len(batches) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("a stopped timer sent %d batches", len(batches))
	}

	_ = b.add(logsEntry("f"))
	if err := b.close(); err != nil || len(batches) != 3 || batches[2].Lines[0].Text != "f" {
		t.Fatalf("close = %v, batches %+v; want the last line sent", err, batches)
	}
	if err := b.add(logsEntry("g")); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a closed batcher must refuse lines")
	}
}

func TestLogBatcherSendsANoticeAfterTheLinesAddedBeforeIt(t *testing.T) {
	var calls []string
	timers := &logsFakeTimers{}
	b := newLogBatcher(
		func(b LogBatch) error { calls = append(calls, "lines"); return nil },
		func(n Notice) error { calls = append(calls, "notice:"+n.Code); return nil },
		nil, 200, 100*time.Millisecond, timers.after)
	_ = b.add(logsEntry("a"))
	if err := b.send(Notice{Code: NoticeDetached}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_ = b.add(logsEntry("b"))
	_ = b.close()
	want := []string{"lines", "notice:detached", "lines"}
	if len(calls) != len(want) || calls[0] != want[0] || calls[1] != want[1] || calls[2] != want[2] {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %v, want %v", calls, want)
	}
}

func TestLogBatcherKeepsTheFirstError(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("receiver gone")
	calls := 0
	var told []error
	b := newLogBatcher(func(LogBatch) error { calls++; return boom }, nil, func(err error) { told = append(told, err) }, 1, time.Hour, (&logsFakeTimers{}).after)
	if err := b.add(logsEntry("a")); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Fatalf("add = %v, want the receiver's error", err)
	}
	if err := b.add(logsEntry("b")); !errors.Is(err, boom) || calls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("second add = %v after %d out calls, want the same error without another call", err, calls)
	}
	if !errors.Is(b.failure(), boom) || !errors.Is(b.send(Notice{}), boom) {
		t.Fatal("failure and notices must report the sticky error")
	}
	if len(told) != 1 || !errors.Is(told[0], boom) {
		t.Fatalf("onFail was told %v, want the error once", told)
	}
}
```

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"path"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
)

// Log follow limits.
const (
	// MaxLogTail is the largest history a follower reads per container.
	MaxLogTail = 5000
	// MaxLogHistory is the most history lines a project follower sends before
	// it goes live: the newest ones of the merged per-container tails.
	MaxLogHistory = 5000

	logFlushInterval   = 100 * time.Millisecond // a batch leaves at the latest this long after its first line
	logFlushLines      = 200                    // ... or as soon as it has this many lines
	logHistoryBytes    = 4 << 20                // text bytes of history kept per container while merging
	logHistoryParallel = 4                      // history reads in flight at once
	logHistoryTimeout  = 30 * time.Second       // one history read of a project follower is given up after this long
	logSettle          = time.Second            // pause before a project re-checks its containers after a stream ended
)

// Codes of Notice.Code.
const (
	NoticeNotFollowed      = "not_followed"
	NoticeAttached         = "attached"
	NoticeDetached         = "detached"
	NoticeTruncatedHistory = "truncated_history"
)

// FollowOptions select the history a follower reads before it goes live.
// Tail is per container: 0 means no history, at most MaxLogTail. A Since without
// a Tail asks for every line since then (up to MaxLogTail). The server applies
// the defaults of the routes (200 for a container, 100 for a project).
type FollowOptions struct {
	Tail  int
	Since time.Time
	// Opened, when set, is called once when the stream is established: for a
	// container when the Engine has accepted the log request, for a project when
	// the project has been listed. It comes before the first out or notice call.
	// An error that comes earlier (unknown container, no free stream slot,
	// unreachable host) is returned without a call, so the route can still answer
	// it as a plain response and switch to an event stream only from here on.
	Opened func()
}

// tail is the Engine tail the options ask for.
func (o FollowOptions) tail() int {
	switch {
	case o.Tail > MaxLogTail:
		return MaxLogTail
	case o.Tail <= 0 && !o.Since.IsZero():
		return MaxLogTail
	case o.Tail < 0:
		return 0
	}
	return o.Tail
}

// LogEntry is one line of a followed log (SSE `lines` message).
type LogEntry struct {
	T     time.Time `json:"t"`
	S     string    `json:"s"` // out | err
	Text  string    `json:"text"`
	Trunc bool      `json:"trunc"`
	Svc   string    `json:"svc,omitempty"` // compose service; project streams only
	Ctr   string    `json:"ctr,omitempty"` // 12-character container id; project streams only
}

// LogBatch is one SSE `lines` message.
type LogBatch struct {
	Lines []LogEntry `json:"lines"`
}

// Notice is one SSE `notice` message: something about which containers of a
// project are followed.
type Notice struct {
	Code      string   `json:"code"` // not_followed | attached | detached | truncated_history
	Message   string   `json:"message"`
	Services  []string `json:"services,omitempty"`
	Container string   `json:"container,omitempty"`
}

// ProjectSelector chooses the containers of a compose project.
type ProjectSelector struct {
	Project    string // com.docker.compose.project
	WorkingDir string // when set: only containers whose working dir equals it (a managed stack) ...
	Exclude    bool   // ... or, with Exclude, only those whose working dir differs (an external project sharing a stack's name)
}

// Matches reports whether the container belongs to the selection. Working
// directories are compared as cleaned paths; a container without the label never
// equals one.
func (s ProjectSelector) Matches(c dockerhost.ContainerSummary) bool {
	if s.Project == "" || c.ComposeProject != s.Project {
		return false
	}
	if s.WorkingDir == "" {
		return true
	}
	same := c.ComposeWorkingDir != "" && path.Clean(c.ComposeWorkingDir) == path.Clean(s.WorkingDir)
	return same != s.Exclude
}

func logEntryOf(l dockerhost.LogLine) LogEntry {
	return LogEntry{T: l.Time, S: l.Stream, Text: l.Text, Trunc: l.Truncated}
}
```

Create `internal/dockerwatch/logs_batch.go`:

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"errors"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// logTimer is what the batcher needs from a timer (*time.Timer, or a fake in tests).
type logTimer interface{ Stop() bool }

func logAfterFunc(d time.Duration, f func()) logTimer { return time.AfterFunc(d, f) }

var errLogBatcherClosed = errors.New("log stream closed")

// logBatcher turns single log entries into LogBatch messages: a batch leaves
// when it has max entries or interval after its first entry, whichever comes
// first. All calls to out and notice are serialized under one mutex and happen
// in the order the entries and notices were added; a slow receiver therefore
// slows the producers down (back pressure) instead of buffering without bound.
// The first error of out or notice is sticky: every later call returns it, and
// onFail is told once, so the follower stops reading instead of waiting for its
// next line.
type logBatcher struct {
	out      func(LogBatch) error
	notice   func(Notice) error
	onFail   func(error)
	max      int
	interval time.Duration
	after    func(d time.Duration, f func()) logTimer

	mu      sync.Mutex
	pending []LogEntry
	timer   logTimer
	err     error
	closed  bool
}

func newLogBatcher(out func(LogBatch) error, notice func(Notice) error, onFail func(error), max int, interval time.Duration, after func(time.Duration, func()) logTimer) *logBatcher {
	if notice == nil {
		notice = func(Notice) error { return nil }
	}
	if onFail == nil {
		onFail = func(error) {}
	}
	return &logBatcher{out: out, notice: notice, onFail: onFail, max: max, interval: interval, after: after}
}

// setErr records the first error.
func (b *logBatcher) setErr(err error) {
	if b.err == nil {
		b.err = err
		b.onFail(err)
	}
}

// add queues one entry.
func (b *logBatcher) add(e LogEntry) error {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.addLocked(e)
}

// addAll queues entries in order (the merged history).
func (b *logBatcher) addAll(entries []LogEntry) error {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	for _, e := range entries {
		if err := b.addLocked(e); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (b *logBatcher) addLocked(e LogEntry) error {
	if b.err != nil {
		return b.err
	}
	if b.closed {
		return errLogBatcherClosed
	}
	b.pending = append(b.pending, e)
	if len(b.pending) >= b.max {
		return b.flushLocked()
	}
	if b.timer == nil {
		b.timer = b.after(b.interval, b.onTimer)
	}
	return nil
}

func (b *logBatcher) onTimer() {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.timer = nil
	_ = b.flushLocked()
}

// flushLocked sends what is pending.
func (b *logBatcher) flushLocked() error {
	if b.timer != nil {
		b.timer.Stop()
		b.timer = nil
	}
	if len(b.pending) == 0 || b.err != nil {
		return b.err
	}
	lines := b.pending
	b.pending = nil
	if err := b.out(LogBatch{Lines: lines}); err != nil {
		b.setErr(err)
	}
	return b.err
}

// send delivers a notice after the entries added before it.
func (b *logBatcher) send(n Notice) error {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if err := b.flushLocked(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if b.closed {
		return errLogBatcherClosed
	}
	if err := b.notice(n); err != nil {
		b.setErr(err)
	}
	return b.err
}

// failure returns the sticky error, if any.
func (b *logBatcher) failure() error {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.err
}

// close sends what is pending and refuses further entries.
func (b *logBatcher) close() error {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	err := b.flushLocked()
	b.closed = true
	return err
}
```

### Task B4: `Hub.FollowContainer`

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_follow.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_fake_test.go`
- Test: `internal/dockerwatch/logs_follow_test.go`

`logEnv` is everything a follower takes from the outside: the `Hosts`, the stream budget (`Acquire`), the event feed (`WatchHost`), the Engine calls (`dockerhost.FollowLogs`, `dockerhost.ListContainers`) and the timing. `Hub.logEnv()` fills it from the hub; the tests fill it with fakes, which is how the project cases (B5) run without an Engine and in milliseconds. `FollowContainer` takes one stream slot, gets the host's client, follows the log with the options' tail (`Tail` 0 without `Since` means no history) and passes every line to the batcher. It returns `ctx.Err()` when the caller ended it, the receiver's error when `out` failed (the batcher cancels the read at once), otherwise the Engine or transport error unchanged, and nil when the log ends. One test runs the whole path over a real `httptest` Engine and a real hub (`New(hosts, Options{})`, the real `Acquire`), so it also checks the integration with Part A's hub: the slot comes back, no slot means no request.

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
)

// logsLine is a log line `sec` seconds after logsBase.
func logsLine(sec int, stream, text string) dockerhost.LogLine {
	return dockerhost.LogLine{Stream: stream, Time: logsBase.Add(time.Duration(sec) * time.Second), Text: text}
}

// logsCtrOf is a container of a compose project. id is one character that
// fills the 64-character id.
func logsCtrOf(id, project, service, workingDir, state string) dockerhost.ContainerSummary {
	full := strings.Repeat(id, 64)
	return dockerhost.ContainerSummary{
		ID: full[:12], FullID: full, Names: []string{project + "-" + service + "-1"},
		State: state, ComposeProject: project, ComposeService: service, ComposeWorkingDir: workingDir,
	}
}

// logsWaitFor polls cond until it holds.
func logsWaitFor(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// logsSink receives what a follower sends.
type logsSink struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	batches []LogBatch
	notices []Notice
	outErr  error // returned by out once set
}

func (s *logsSink) out(b LogBatch) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.outErr != nil {
		return s.outErr
	}
	s.batches = append(s.batches, b)
	return nil
}

func (s *logsSink) notice(n Notice) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.notices = append(s.notices, n)
	return nil
}

func (s *logsSink) lines() []LogEntry {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	var all []LogEntry
	for _, b := range s.batches {
		all = append(all, b.Lines...)
	}
	return all
}

func (s *logsSink) texts() []string {
	var out []string
	for _, l := range s.lines() {
		out = append(out, l.Text)
	}
	return out
}

func (s *logsSink) noticeList() []Notice {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]Notice(nil), s.notices...)
}

func (s *logsSink) waitLines(t *testing.T, n int) {
	t.Helper()
	logsWaitFor(t, "log lines", func() bool { return len(s.lines()) >= n })
}

// waitNotice waits for the n-th (1-based) notice with the code and returns it.
func (s *logsSink) waitNotice(t *testing.T, code string, n int) Notice {
	t.Helper()
	var found Notice
	logsWaitFor(t, "notice "+code, func() bool {
		count := 0
		for _, got := range s.noticeList() {
			if got.Code == code {
				count++
				if count == n {
					found = got
					return true
				}
			}
		}
		return false
	})
	return found
}

func (s *logsSink) countNotices(code string) int {
	count := 0
	for _, got := range s.noticeList() {
		if got.Code == code {
			count++
		}
	}
	return count
}

// logsRead is what a log read asked for (LogOptions without its callback, so it can be compared).
type logsRead struct {
	Tail   int
	Since  time.Time
	Follow bool
}

// logsCall is one log read the fake Engine served.
type logsCall struct {
	ref  string
	read logsRead
}

// logsFakeEngine replaces the Engine calls, the event feed and the stream
// budget of a logEnv. A read serves the container's history (the last Tail
// lines at or after Since) and, when it follows, then waits for lines pushed
// with push until end, the context or a refusal set with refuse.
type logsFakeEngine struct {
	mu         sync.Mutex
	containers []dockerhost.ContainerSummary
	history    map[string][]dockerhost.LogLine
	feeds      map[string]chan dockerhost.LogLine
	refused    map[string]error
	hang       map[string]bool // history reads of these containers never answer
	calls      []logsCall
	lists      int
	slots      int // stream slots of the host
	used       int
	watcher    func(Event)
}

func newLogsFakeEngine() *logsFakeEngine {
	return &logsFakeEngine{
		history: map[string][]dockerhost.LogLine{},
		feeds:   map[string]chan dockerhost.LogLine{},
		refused: map[string]error{},
		hang:    map[string]bool{},
		slots:   MaxStreamsPerHost,
	}
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) env() logEnv {
	return logEnv{
		hosts: logsFakeHosts{},
		acquire: func(string) (func(), error) {
			f.mu.Lock()
			defer f.mu.Unlock()
			if f.used >= f.slots {
				return nil, ErrTooManyStreams
			}
			f.used++
			return func() { f.mu.Lock(); f.used--; f.mu.Unlock() }, nil
		},
		watch: func(_ string, fn func(Event)) func() {
			f.mu.Lock()
			f.watcher = fn
			f.mu.Unlock()
			return func() {}
		},
		follow:         f.follow,
		list:           f.list,
		after:          logAfterFunc,
		flushEvery:     5 * time.Millisecond,
		flushLines:     logFlushLines,
		settle:         5 * time.Millisecond,
		historyTimeout: time.Second,
	}
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) list(context.Context, *dockerutil.Client) ([]dockerhost.ContainerSummary, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.lists++
	return append([]dockerhost.ContainerSummary(nil), f.containers...), nil
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) feed(ref string) chan dockerhost.LogLine {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	ch := f.feeds[ref]
	if ch == nil {
		ch = make(chan dockerhost.LogLine, 64)
		f.feeds[ref] = ch
	}
	return ch
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) follow(ctx context.Context, _ *dockerutil.Client, ref string, opt dockerhost.LogOptions, fn func(dockerhost.LogLine) error) error {
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.calls = append(f.calls, logsCall{ref: ref, read: logsRead{Tail: opt.Tail, Since: opt.Since, Follow: opt.Follow}})
	refusal := f.refused[ref]
	lines := f.history[ref]
	hang := f.hang[ref] && !opt.Follow
	f.mu.Unlock()
	if refusal != nil {
		return refusal
	}
	if hang {
		<-ctx.Done()
		return ctx.Err()
	}
	if opt.Opened != nil {
		opt.Opened()
	}
	var served []dockerhost.LogLine
	for _, l := range lines {
		if opt.Since.IsZero() || !l.Time.Before(opt.Since) {
			served = append(served, l)
		}
	}
	if len(served) > opt.Tail {
		served = served[len(served)-opt.Tail:]
	}
	for _, l := range served {
		if err := fn(l); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if !opt.Follow {
		return nil
	}
	feed := f.feed(ref)
	for {
		select {
		case l, ok := <-feed:
			if !ok {
				return nil
			}
			if err := fn(l); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return ctx.Err()
		}
	}
}

// push sends a live line of a container.
func (f *logsFakeEngine) push(ref string, l dockerhost.LogLine) { f.feed(ref) <- l }

// end ends the container's live stream (it stopped); the next read starts a new one.
func (f *logsFakeEngine) end(ref string) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	ch := f.feeds[ref]
	delete(f.feeds, ref)
	f.mu.Unlock()
	if ch != nil {
		close(ch)
	}
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) setState(id, state string) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	for i := range f.containers {
		if f.containers[i].ID[:1] == id {
			f.containers[i].State = state
		}
	}
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) callList() []logsCall {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]logsCall(nil), f.calls...)
}

// liveCalls are the reads that follow.
func (f *logsFakeEngine) liveCalls(ref string) []logsCall {
	var out []logsCall
	for _, c := range f.callList() {
		if c.ref == ref && c.read.Follow {
			out = append(out, c)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) listCount() int {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.lists
}

func (f *logsFakeEngine) slotsInUse() int {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.used
}

// emit delivers an event to the follower's watcher, like the hub's events watcher.
func (f *logsFakeEngine) emit(ev Event) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	fn := f.watcher
	f.mu.Unlock()
	if fn != nil {
		fn(ev)
	}
}

type logsFakeHosts struct{}

func (logsFakeHosts) Host(context.Context, string) (dockerhost.Host, error) {
	return dockerhost.Host{}, nil
}

func (logsFakeHosts) Client(context.Context, string) (*dockerutil.Client, error) { return nil, nil }
```

```go
package dockerwatch

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerutil"
	"aurago/internal/testutil"
)

// logsHTTPHosts serves one Engine over HTTP that has the container "web" (a TTY
// container) and records the query of its log request.
type logsHTTPHosts struct {
	client *dockerutil.Client
	mu     sync.Mutex
	query  url.Values
	hits   int
}

func newLogsHTTPHosts(t *testing.T, logBody string) *logsHTTPHosts {
	t.Helper()
	h := &logsHTTPHosts{}
	server := testutil.NewHTTPServer(t, http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		h.mu.Lock()
		h.hits++
		h.mu.Unlock()
		switch {
		case r.URL.Path == "/version":
			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"ApiVersion":"1.45","MinAPIVersion":"1.24"}`)
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/containers/web/json"):
			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"Config":{"Tty":true}}`)
		case strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/containers/web/logs"):
			h.mu.Lock()
			h.query = r.URL.Query()
			h.mu.Unlock()
			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, logBody)
		default:
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
			_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"message":"no such container"}`)
		}
	}))
	t.Cleanup(server.Close)
	h.client = dockerutil.NewClient("tcp://"+server.Listener.Addr().String(), 5*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(h.client.CloseIdleConnections)
	return h
}

func (h *logsHTTPHosts) Host(context.Context, string) (dockerhost.Host, error) {
	return dockerhost.Host{}, nil
}

func (h *logsHTTPHosts) Client(context.Context, string) (*dockerutil.Client, error) {
	return h.client, nil
}

func TestFollowContainerStreamsTheEnginesLogThroughTheHub(t *testing.T) {
	body := "2026-10-28T07:00:01.000000000Z first\r\n2026-10-28T07:00:02.000000000Z second\n2026-10-28T07:00:03.000000000Z third\n"
	hosts := newLogsHTTPHosts(t, body)
	hub := New(hosts, Options{})
	sink := &logsSink{}
	since := logsBase.Add(-time.Hour)
	opened := 0
	opt := FollowOptions{Tail: 50, Since: since, Opened: func() {
		if len(sink.lines()) != 0 {
			t.Error("Opened came after the first line")
		}
		opened++
	}}

	err := hub.FollowContainer(context.Background(), "h1", "web", opt, sink.out, sink.notice)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FollowContainer: %v", err)
	}
	if opened != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Opened was called %d times, want once", opened)
	}
	if got := sink.texts(); len(got) != 3 || got[0] != "first" || got[1] != "second" || got[2] != "third" {
		t.Fatalf("lines = %v, want the three lines without timestamps", got)
	}
	if first := sink.lines()[0]; first.S != "out" || !first.T.Equal(logsBase.Add(time.Second)) || first.Svc != "" || first.Ctr != "" {
		t.Fatalf("first entry = %+v, want a plain entry (no service or container on a single stream)", first)
	}
	if len(sink.batches) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d batches, want the three lines in one", len(sink.batches))
	}
	hosts.mu.Lock()
	q := hosts.query
	hosts.mu.Unlock()
	if q.Get("follow") != "1" || q.Get("tail") != "50" || q.Get("timestamps") != "1" || q.Get("since") == "" {
		t.Fatalf("log query = %v, want follow=1, tail=50, timestamps=1 and since", q)
	}
	// The stream slot is free again: all of them can be taken.
	for i := 0; i < MaxStreamsPerHost; i++ {
		release, err := hub.Acquire("h1")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("slot %d after the follow ended: %v", i, err)
		}
		defer release()
	}
}

func TestFollowContainerNeedsAFreeStreamSlot(t *testing.T) {
	hosts := newLogsHTTPHosts(t, "")
	hub := New(hosts, Options{})
	for i := 0; i < MaxStreamsPerHost; i++ {
		release, err := hub.Acquire("h1")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		defer release()
	}
	opt := FollowOptions{Tail: 10, Opened: func() { t.Error("Opened was called without a stream") }}
	err := hub.FollowContainer(context.Background(), "h1", "web", opt, (&logsSink{}).out, nil)
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrTooManyStreams) {
		t.Fatalf("FollowContainer without a free slot = %v, want ErrTooManyStreams", err)
	}
	hosts.mu.Lock()
	hits := hosts.hits
	hosts.mu.Unlock()
	if hits != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the Engine got %d requests although no slot was free", hits)
	}
}
```
