```go
// dmLiveFixture is the Docker Manager server of newDMFixture (host registry,
// fake Engines) with the fake hub and the fake stacks service routed in, served
// over HTTP so that event streams can be read while they are open.
type dmLiveFixture struct {
	*dmFixture
	live     *dmFakeLive
	stacks   *dmFakeStacks
	noStacks bool
	readOnly bool
	srv      *httptest.Server
}

func newDMLiveFixture(t *testing.T) *dmLiveFixture {
	t.Helper()
	f := &dmLiveFixture{dmFixture: newDMFixture(t), live: newDMFakeLive(), stacks: newDMFakeStacks()}
	f.srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		dm := &dmRequest{s: f.s, w: w, r: r, readOnly: f.readOnly, live: f.live}
		if !f.noStacks {
			dm.stacks = f.stacks
		}
		dm.route(dockerManagerSegments(r.URL.Path))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(f.srv.Close)
	t.Cleanup(f.srv.CloseClientConnections)
	return f
}

// dmStream is an open event stream response. Reads are bounded by the context
// of the request, so a missing frame fails the test instead of hanging it.
type dmStream struct {
	t      *testing.T
	resp   *http.Response
	reader *bufio.Reader
	cancel context.CancelFunc
}

// dmFrame is one event of a stream: its name and data, or a comment line.
type dmFrame struct {
	event, data, comment string
}

func (f dmFrame) json(t *testing.T) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var out map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(f.data), &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("data of event %q is not a JSON object: %q", f.event, f.data)
	}
	return out
}

// open sends a request to the fixture's server and returns the response.
func (f *dmLiveFixture) open(method, path string, body io.Reader) *dmStream {
	f.t.Helper()
	return dmOpenStream(f.t, method, f.srv.URL+"/api/docker-manager"+path, body, nil)
}

// dmOpenStream sends a request and returns the open response; the stream is
// closed when the test ends.
func dmOpenStream(t *testing.T, method, url string, body io.Reader, headers map[string]string) *dmStream {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, url, body)
	if err != nil {
		cancel()
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for key, value := range headers {
		req.Header.Set(key, value)
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		cancel()
		t.Fatalf("%s %s: %v", method, url, err)
	}
	st := &dmStream{t: t, resp: resp, reader: bufio.NewReader(resp.Body), cancel: cancel}
	t.Cleanup(st.close)
	return st
}

func (s *dmStream) close() {
	s.cancel()
	_ = s.resp.Body.Close()
}

// next reads the next frame (an event with its data, or a comment line).
func (s *dmStream) next() dmFrame {
	s.t.Helper()
	var frame dmFrame
	for {
		line, err := s.reader.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil {
			s.t.Fatalf("stream ended while waiting for a frame: %v (partial %+v)", err, frame)
		}
		line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r\n")
		switch {
		case line == "":
			if frame != (dmFrame{}) {
				return frame
			}
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, ": "):
			frame.comment = strings.TrimPrefix(line, ": ")
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "event: "):
			frame.event = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "event: ")
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "data: "):
			frame.data = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "data: ")
		}
	}
}

// nextEvent skips comment lines and returns the next event.
func (s *dmStream) nextEvent() dmFrame {
	s.t.Helper()
	for {
		if frame := s.next(); frame.event != "" {
			return frame
		}
	}
}

// expectEnd checks that the stream has ended (EOF).
func (s *dmStream) expectEnd() {
	s.t.Helper()
	if line, err := s.reader.ReadString('\n'); err != io.EOF {
		s.t.Fatalf("stream = %q, %v; want the end of the stream", line, err)
	}
}

// body reads the whole (non-streaming) answer as JSON.
func (s *dmStream) body() map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	raw, err := io.ReadAll(s.reader)
	if err != nil {
		s.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var out map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &out); err != nil {
		s.t.Fatalf("answer %q is not JSON: %v", raw, err)
	}
	return out
}

// expectError checks a JSON error answer.
func (s *dmStream) expectError(status int, code string) map[string]any {
	s.t.Helper()
	body := s.body()
	if s.resp.StatusCode != status || body["status"] != "error" || body["code"] != code {
		s.t.Fatalf("answer = %d %v, want %d error %q", s.resp.StatusCode, body, status, code)
	}
	return body
}

// withHeartbeat shortens the idle heartbeat of the event streams for a test.
func withHeartbeat(t *testing.T, d time.Duration) {
	t.Helper()
	old := dmSSEHeartbeat
	dmSSEHeartbeat = d
	t.Cleanup(func() { dmSSEHeartbeat = old })
}
```

```go
func TestInitDockerHostsOpensTheLiveHubAndCloseEndsIt(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMFixture(t)
	if f.s.DockerWatch == nil {
		t.Fatal("initDockerHosts left DockerWatch nil")
	}
	if f.s.dockerOpsBridge == nil {
		t.Fatal("the stacks service is open but its operations are not forwarded to the hub")
	}
	client, err := f.s.DockerWatch.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Attach: %v", err)
	}

	f.s.closeDockerHosts()
	select {
	case _, open := <-client.Messages():
		if open {
			t.Fatal("a message arrived on a client of the closed hub")
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("closeDockerHosts left a stream client open")
	}
	if _, err := f.s.DockerWatch.Attach(); !errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrHubClosed) {
		t.Fatalf("Attach after close = %v, want ErrHubClosed", err)
	}
	if f.s.dockerOpsBridge != nil {
		t.Fatal("the operation bridge outlived the hub")
	}
	f.s.closeDockerHosts() // the cleanup of the fixture calls it again
}

// dmFakeObserver stands in for the stacks service: it keeps the callback.
type dmFakeObserver struct {
	fn        func(dockerstacks.Operation)
	cancelled bool
}

func (o *dmFakeObserver) Observe(fn func(dockerstacks.Operation)) func() {
	o.fn = fn
	return func() { o.cancelled = true }
}

// dmRecordingPublisher stands in for the hub: it records what is published.
type dmRecordingPublisher struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	hosts []string
	msgs  []dockerwatch.Message
}

func (p *dmRecordingPublisher) Publish(host string, msg dockerwatch.Message) {
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	p.hosts = append(p.hosts, host)
	p.msgs = append(p.msgs, msg)
}

	observer, publisher := &dmFakeObserver{}, &dmRecordingPublisher{}
	cancel := bridgeDockerOperations(observer, publisher)

	observer.fn(dockerstacks.Operation{
		ID: "op_0123456789abcdef", HostID: "nas", Stack: "web", Kind: dockerstacks.KindUp,

	}

	if err != nil {

	}

			Stack  string `json:"stack"`
			Kind   string `json:"kind"`
			State  string `json:"state"`

		} `json:"operation"`
	}

	}
}

func TestDockerManagerLiveFailureCodes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name         string
		err          error
		notFoundCode string
		status       int
		code         string
	}{
		{"no stream slot", fmt.Errorf("follow: %w", dockerwatch.ErrTooManyStreams), "", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too_many_streams"},
		{"no stream client", dockerwatch.ErrTooManyClients, "", http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too_many_streams"},
		{"hub closed", dockerwatch.ErrHubClosed, "", http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "docker_hosts_unavailable"},
		{"host forgotten", fmt.Errorf("client: %w", dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound), "", http.StatusNotFound, "host_not_found"},
		{"no such container", &dockerhost.StatusError{Status: 404, Err: errors.New("No such container")}, "container_not_found", http.StatusNotFound, "container_not_found"},
		{"engine refused", &dockerhost.StatusError{Status: 500, Err: errors.New("boom")}, "container_not_found", http.StatusBadGateway, "docker_error"},
		{"no answer", errors.New("dial tcp 127.0.0.1:2375: connection refused"), "", http.StatusBadGateway, "host_unreachable"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := dmLiveFailureOf(tc.err, tc.notFoundCode)
			if got.status != tc.status || got.code != tc.code || got.message == "" {
				t.Fatalf("failure = %+v, want %d %s with a message", got, tc.status, tc.code)
			}
			if tc.code == "host_unreachable" && got.extra["reason"] == "" {
				t.Fatalf("an unreachable host carries its reason: %+v", got)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
	"aurago/internal/dockerwatch"
)

// ── Docker Manager live data: the seam to internal/dockerwatch ──────────────
// The live routes (docker_manager_stream.go, docker_manager_logs.go,
// docker_manager_terminal_api.go and the disk-usage route below) use the hub
// through the narrow interfaces here, so the handler tests can substitute a
// fake for the failure cases that a real Engine cannot be told to produce.

// dmDFTimeout bounds GET /hosts/{id}/df: /system/df is slow on hosts with many
// images and volumes.
const dmDFTimeout = 60 * time.Second

// dmLive is what the live routes use of *dockerwatch.Hub.
type dmLive interface {
	Attach() (dmLiveClient, error)
	Client(id string) (dmLiveClient, bool)
	FollowContainer(ctx context.Context, host, ref string, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error
	FollowProject(ctx context.Context, host string, sel dockerwatch.ProjectSelector, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error
	Acquire(host string) (release func(), err error)
	DiskUsage(ctx context.Context, host string, refresh bool) (usage dockerhost.DiskUsage, fetchedAt time.Time, cached bool, err error)
}

// dmLiveClient is one open /stream as the handlers see it (*dockerwatch.Client).
type dmLiveClient interface {
	ID() string
	Messages() <-chan dockerwatch.Message
	Set(sub dockerwatch.Subscription) (dockerwatch.Accepted, error)
	Close()
}

// dmWatchHub adapts the hub: Attach and Client return the interface, never a
// nil *dockerwatch.Client wrapped in a non-nil interface.
type dmWatchHub struct{ *dockerwatch.Hub }

func (h dmWatchHub) Attach() (dmLiveClient, error) {
	c, err := h.Hub.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return c, nil
}

func (h dmWatchHub) Client(id string) (dmLiveClient, bool) {
	c, ok := h.Hub.Client(id)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	return c, true
}

var (
	_ dmLive       = dmWatchHub{}
	_ dmLiveClient = (*dockerwatch.Client)(nil)
)

// liveService returns the live data hub, or answers 503. The hub exists as soon
// as the host registry does, so this only fires for a server that never opened
// either.
func (dm *dmRequest) liveService() (dmLive, bool) {
	if dm.live == nil {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, dmCodeUnavailable, "The Docker live data service is not available", nil)
		return nil, false
	}
	return dm.live, true
}

// dmLiveFailureOf classifies an error of a live call that touched a host: the
// stream budget (429), a host the registry forgot (404) and then everything
// engineFailureOf knows.
func dmLiveFailureOf(err error, notFoundCode string) dmFailure {
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrTooManyStreams):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusTooManyRequests, dmCodeTooManyStreams, "Too many live connections to this Docker host are open; close a log or terminal panel and try again", nil}
	case errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrTooManyClients):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusTooManyRequests, dmCodeTooManyStreams, "Too many live streams are open; close another Docker Manager window and try again", nil}
	case errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrHubClosed):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusServiceUnavailable, dmCodeUnavailable, "The Docker live data service is shutting down", nil}
	case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusNotFound, dmCodeHostNotFound, "Docker host not found", nil}
	}
	return engineFailureOf(err, notFoundCode)
}

func (dm *dmRequest) liveFailure(err error, notFoundCode string) {
	dm.writeFailure(dmLiveFailureOf(err, notFoundCode))
}

// diskUsage serves GET /hosts/{id}/df[?refresh=1]: Docker's own disk use on the
// host (images, containers, volumes, build cache) from the hub's cache; refresh
// reads it again when the cache is older than a minute. docker.readonly allows it.
func (dm *dmRequest) diskUsage(hostID string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmDFTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if _, ok := dm.host(ctx, hostID); !ok {
		return
	}
	usage, fetchedAt, cached, err := live.DiskUsage(ctx, hostID, dmTruthy(dm.r.URL.Query().Get("refresh")))
	if err != nil {
		dm.liveFailure(err, "")
		return
	}
	dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"df": usage, "fetched_at": fetchedAt, "cached": cached})
}

// ── Operation bridge ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// dmOperationObserver is *dockerstacks.Service as the bridge uses it.
type dmOperationObserver interface {
	Observe(fn func(dockerstacks.Operation)) (cancel func())
}

// dmPublisher is *dockerwatch.Hub as the bridge uses it.
type dmPublisher interface {
	Publish(host string, msg dockerwatch.Message)
}

var (
	_ dmOperationObserver = (*dockerstacks.Service)(nil)
	_ dmPublisher         = (*dockerwatch.Hub)(nil)
)

// dmOperationMessage is the data of the `operation` stream message.
type dmOperationMessage struct {
	Host      string                 `json:"host"`
	Operation dockerstacks.Operation `json:"operation"`
}

// bridgeDockerOperations forwards every state change of a stack operation (never
// its output) to the stream clients subscribed to the operation's host. The
// observer runs with the service's locks held, and Publish never blocks. The
// returned func stops the forwarding.
func bridgeDockerOperations(src dmOperationObserver, dst dmPublisher) (cancel func()) {
	return src.Observe(func(op dockerstacks.Operation) {
		op.Output = ""
		dst.Publish(op.HostID, dockerwatch.Message{
			Event: dockerwatch.MsgOperation,
			Data:  dmOperationMessage{Host: op.HostID, Operation: op},
		})
	})
}

// initDockerWatch creates the live data hub on the host registry and connects
// the stacks service's operation state changes to it. The hub starts nothing
// until a stream client subscribes.
func (s *Server) initDockerWatch() {
	hub := dockerwatch.New(s.DockerHosts, dockerwatch.Options{Logger: s.Logger})
	s.DockerWatch = hub
	if s.DockerStacks != nil {
		s.dockerOpsBridge = bridgeDockerOperations(s.DockerStacks, hub)
	}
}

// closeDockerWatch stops the operation bridge and closes the hub: every open
// stream ends and the watchers and samplers stop.
func (s *Server) closeDockerWatch() {
	if s.dockerOpsBridge != nil {
		s.dockerOpsBridge()
		s.dockerOpsBridge = nil
	}
	if s.DockerWatch != nil {
		s.DockerWatch.Close()
	}
}
```

```go
// engineFailure answers an error from an Engine call or from the client of a
// host. dockerhost.StatusOf separates the cases: a rejected action or container
// reference is a 400; 404 with notFoundCode (when given) is "no such object";
// any other Engine status is docker_error; status 0 means nothing answered
// (dial, TLS, SSH, timeout or a client that could not be built) and becomes
// host_unreachable with the classified reason.
func (dm *dmRequest) engineFailure(err error, notFoundCode string) {
	message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(err.Error(), 512)
	status := dockerhost.StatusOf(err)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrInvalidAction):
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeInvalidAction, message, nil)
	case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrInvalidContainerRef):
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, message, nil)
	case status == http.StatusNotFound && notFoundCode != "":
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusNotFound, notFoundCode, message, nil)
	case status > 0:
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadGateway, dmCodeDockerError, message, nil)
	default:
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadGateway, dmCodeHostUnreachable, message, dmFields{"reason": dockerhost.ClassifyError(err)})
	}
}
```

with

```go
// engineFailure answers an error from an Engine call or from the client of a
// host (see engineFailureOf).
func (dm *dmRequest) engineFailure(err error, notFoundCode string) {
	dm.writeFailure(engineFailureOf(err, notFoundCode))
}

// engineFailureOf classifies an error from an Engine call or from the client of
// a host. dockerhost.StatusOf separates the cases: a rejected action or
// container reference is a 400; 404 with notFoundCode (when given) is "no such
// object"; any other Engine status is docker_error; status 0 means nothing
// answered (dial, TLS, SSH, timeout or a client that could not be built) and
// becomes host_unreachable with the classified reason. The live routes use it
// for the closing event of a stream as well.
func engineFailureOf(err error, notFoundCode string) dmFailure {
	message := dockerutil.SanitizeOneLine(err.Error(), 512)
	status := dockerhost.StatusOf(err)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrInvalidAction):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeInvalidAction, message, nil}
	case errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrInvalidContainerRef):
		return dmFailure{http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, message, nil}
	case status == http.StatusNotFound && notFoundCode != "":
		return dmFailure{http.StatusNotFound, notFoundCode, message, nil}
	case status > 0:
		return dmFailure{http.StatusBadGateway, dmCodeDockerError, message, nil}
	default:
		return dmFailure{http.StatusBadGateway, dmCodeHostUnreachable, message, dmFields{"reason": dockerhost.ClassifyError(err)}}
	}
}
```

### Task C2: The live stream and its subscriptions

**Files:**
- Create (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_live_engine_test.go`
- Create (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_stream_test.go`
- Create: `internal/server/docker_manager_stream.go`
- Modify: `internal/server/docker_manager_api.go`
- Modify (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_fixture_test.go`

`GET /stream` writes one server-sent event stream per open Docker Manager window: `hello` with the stream id, then the hub client's messages under their `dockerwatch.Msg*` names (the data is the JSON of the message type), a comment line every `dmSSEHeartbeat` and a write deadline of 30 s per write (`dmEventStream`, as the operation stream). One goroutine writes; the handler returns when the request ends, a write fails or the hub closes the client (a client that fell 512 messages behind gets `dropped` and is closed), and it always closes the hub client. The 33rd open stream is 429 `too_many_streams`. `PUT /stream/subscriptions` names the stream by the id of its hello and replaces the whole subscription. The hub checks the shape of ids and the limits but not whether a host exists, so the handler asks the registry first: a host it does not know, or cannot look up, is dropped from all three lists and listed in `rejected` with a reason; the request does not fail for it. A limit or a malformed container id is 400 `bad_request` with the hub's message. The hub sends the current `host_status` of every host that is new to the stream on `Set` and the history of a container with a ring before its live points (Part A); the end-to-end tests pin both through this layer. The tests need a fake Engine that keeps `/events` open, answers stats and serves the other live calls, and a server on the real hub and registry: `docker_manager_live_engine_test.go` (also used by Tasks C3 and C4). `newDMServer` is the server setup of `newDMFixture`, extracted so that the new fixture can use it with another Engine.

```go
// newDMServer is a server with Docker enabled, a vault and the host registry
// (with the stacks service and the live data hub) open on the local Engine at
// endpoint (docker.host). It is closed when the test ends.
func newDMServer(t *testing.T, endpoint string) *Server {
	t.Helper()
	tools.ConfigureRuntimePermissions(tools.RuntimePermissions{DockerEnabled: true})
	t.Cleanup(tools.ClearRuntimePermissionsForTest)

	dir := t.TempDir()
	vault, err := security.NewVault(strings.Repeat("d", 64), filepath.Join(dir, "vault.bin"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NewVault: %v", err)
	}
	s := testContainerServer(true, false)
	s.Cfg.Docker.Host = endpoint
	s.Cfg.Directories.DataDir = dir
	s.Vault = vault
	s.initDockerHosts()
	t.Cleanup(s.closeDockerHosts)
	if s.DockerHosts == nil {
		t.Fatal("initDockerHosts left DockerHosts nil")
```

**Create `internal/server/docker_manager_live_engine_test.go`**

```go
package server

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"

	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
)

// dmLiveEngine is a fake Engine for the live routes of the Docker Manager: the
// container list, a few inspect documents, a held event feed, the held log
// stream of any container, the disk usage and (through the terminal fake of
// docker_manager_terminal_test.go) exec create, hijacked start, resize and a
// detached start. The exec calls address the container "web", whatever the path.
type dmLiveEngine struct {
	t    *testing.T
	srv  *httptest.Server
	term *dmTermEngine
	hold chan struct{} // closing it ends the held log follows

	mu         sync.Mutex
	containers string
	logQueries []string
	events     int
	statsCalls int
}

// dmLiveInspect is the inspect answer per container name: running or not, and labels.
var dmLiveInspect = map[string]struct {
	running bool
	labels  map[string]string
}{
	"web":     {true, nil},
	"stopped": {false, nil},
	"helper":  {true, map[string]string{dockerstacks.LabelRole: dockerstacks.RoleRunner}},
}

const dmLiveDF = `{"LayersSize":1000,"Images":[{"Size":1000,"SharedSize":0,"Containers":1}],` +
	`"Containers":[{"State":"running","SizeRw":50}],"Volumes":[{"UsageData":{"RefCount":1,"Size":200}}],"BuildCache":[{"InUse":false,"Shared":false,"Size":30}]}`

func newDMLiveEngine(t *testing.T, containers string) *dmLiveEngine {
	t.Helper()
	e := &dmLiveEngine{t: t, term: &dmTermEngine{}, hold: make(chan struct{}), containers: containers}
	e.srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(e.serve))
	t.Cleanup(e.srv.Close)
	t.Cleanup(e.srv.CloseClientConnections)
	t.Cleanup(e.release)
	return e
}

func (e *dmLiveEngine) endpoint() string { return "tcp://" + e.srv.Listener.Addr().String() }

func (e *dmLiveEngine) port() int { return e.srv.Listener.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port }

// release ends the held log follows; it can be called more than once.
func (e *dmLiveEngine) release() {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	select {
	case <-e.hold:
	default:
		close(e.hold)
	}
}

func (e *dmLiveEngine) logRequests() []string {
	e.mu.Lock()
	defer e.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), e.logQueries...)
}

func dmMuxFrame(stream byte, text string) []byte {
	header := make([]byte, 8)
	header[0] = stream
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(header[4:], uint32(len(text)))
	return append(header, text...)
}

func (e *dmLiveEngine) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	path := dmTermVersionPrefix.ReplaceAllString(r.URL.Path, "")
	parts := strings.Split(strings.Trim(path, "/"), "/")
	switch {
	case path == "/containers/json":
		e.mu.Lock()
		body := e.containers
		e.mu.Unlock()
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, body)
	case r.Method == http.MethodGet && path == "/events":
		e.mu.Lock()
		e.events++
		e.mu.Unlock()
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
		<-r.Context().Done()
	case r.Method == http.MethodGet && path == "/system/df":
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, dmLiveDF)
	case r.Method == http.MethodGet && len(parts) == 3 && parts[0] == "containers" && parts[2] == "json":
		e.inspect(w, parts[1])
	case r.Method == http.MethodGet && len(parts) == 3 && parts[0] == "containers" && parts[2] == "logs":
		e.logs(w, r)
	case r.Method == http.MethodGet && len(parts) == 3 && parts[0] == "containers" && parts[2] == "stats":
		e.stats(w)
	case r.Method == http.MethodPost && len(parts) == 3 && parts[0] == "containers" && parts[2] == "exec":
		r.URL.Path = "/containers/web/exec"
		e.term.serve(w, r)
	default:
		e.term.serve(w, r)
	}
}

func (e *dmLiveEngine) inspect(w http.ResponseWriter, name string) {
	info, ok := dmLiveInspect[name]
	if !ok {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"message":"No such container: `+name+`"}`)
		return
	}
	labels := info.labels
	if labels == nil {
		labels = map[string]string{}
	}
	doc, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"Id": strings.Repeat("a", 64), "Name": "/" + name,
		"State":  map[string]any{"Running": info.running, "Status": map[bool]string{true: "running", false: "exited"}[info.running]},
		"Config": map[string]any{"Image": "img:1", "Tty": false, "Env": []string{"PATH=/bin"}, "Cmd": []string{"sh"}, "Labels": labels},
	})
	_, _ = w.Write(doc)
}

// stats answers every stats request with counters that grow by one call's worth:
// 100 % of one core on 4 CPUs and memory that grows by 10 bytes, so the order of
// points can be told.
func (e *dmLiveEngine) stats(w http.ResponseWriter) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	e.statsCalls++
	n := uint64(e.statsCalls)
	e.mu.Unlock()
	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"read":"2026-10-28T08:00:03.25Z","pids_stats":{"current":5},`+
		`"cpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":%d},"system_cpu_usage":%d,"online_cpus":4},`+
		`"precpu_stats":{"cpu_usage":{"total_usage":%d},"system_cpu_usage":%d,"online_cpus":4},`+
		`"memory_stats":{"usage":%d,"stats":{"inactive_file":100},"limit":1073741824},`+
		`"networks":{"eth0":{"rx_bytes":10,"tx_bytes":20}}}`, n*1e9, n*4e9, (n-1)*1e9, (n-1)*4e9, 1000+n*10+100)
}

// logs answers the log request of any container with two timestamped lines (one
// per stream) and, for a follow, holds the response open until the client leaves
// or the test releases it.
func (e *dmLiveEngine) logs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	e.mu.Lock()
	e.logQueries = append(e.logQueries, r.URL.RawQuery)
	e.mu.Unlock()
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/vnd.docker.multiplexed-stream")
	_, _ = w.Write(dmMuxFrame(1, "2026-10-28T07:33:29.000000001Z hello from the engine\n"))
	_, _ = w.Write(dmMuxFrame(2, "2026-10-28T07:33:30.000000002Z something went wrong\n"))
	w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
	if q := r.URL.Query().Get("follow"); q == "1" || q == "true" {
		select {
		case <-r.Context().Done():
		case <-e.hold:
		}
	}
}

// dmLiveServer is a Docker Manager server with the real host registry, the real
// hub and a fake local Engine, served over HTTP through handleDockerManager.
type dmLiveServer struct {
	t      *testing.T
	s      *Server
	engine *dmLiveEngine
	url    string
}

func newDMLiveServer(t *testing.T, containers string) *dmLiveServer {
	t.Helper()
	engine := newDMLiveEngine(t, containers)
	s := newDMServer(t, engine.endpoint())
	srv := httptest.NewServer(handleDockerManager(s))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	t.Cleanup(srv.CloseClientConnections)
	return &dmLiveServer{t: t, s: s, engine: engine, url: srv.URL}
}

// open sends a request (a JSON body when body is not nil) and returns the open
// response as a stream; it is closed when the test ends.
func (ls *dmLiveServer) open(method, path string, body any, headers map[string]string) *dmStream {
	ls.t.Helper()
	var reader io.Reader
	if body != nil {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(body)
		if err != nil {
			ls.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		reader = bytes.NewReader(raw)
	}
	return dmOpenStream(ls.t, method, ls.url+"/api/docker-manager"+path, reader, headers)
}

// addTCPHost registers another fake Engine as a tcp host and returns its id.
func (ls *dmLiveServer) addTCPHost(name string, engine *dmLiveEngine) string {
	ls.t.Helper()
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"name": name, "kind": "tcp", "address": "127.0.0.1", "port": engine.port()})
	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	handleDockerManager(ls.s)(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/api/docker-manager/hosts", bytes.NewReader(raw)))
	var created struct {
		Host struct {
			ID string `json:"id"`
		} `json:"host"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &created); err != nil || rec.Code != http.StatusCreated || created.Host.ID == "" {
		ls.t.Fatalf("create host %s: %d %s", name, rec.Code, rec.Body.String())
	}
	return created.Host.ID
}
```

```go
// TestDockerManagerStreamDeliversWhatAClientSubscribedTo runs the whole path: the
// real hub, the real registry, a fake Engine with a held event feed and the
// operation bridge.
func TestDockerManagerStreamDeliversWhatAClientSubscribedTo(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	stream := ls.open(http.MethodGet, "/stream", nil, nil)
	hello := stream.nextEvent()
	id, _ := hello.json(t)["stream_id"].(string)
	if hello.event != "hello" || id == "" {
		t.Fatalf("hello = %+v", hello)
	}

	put := ls.open(http.MethodPut, "/stream/subscriptions", map[string]any{"stream_id": id, "hosts": []string{"local"}}, nil)
	if body := put.body(); put.resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || dmObject(t, body, "accepted")["hosts"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("PUT = %d %v", put.resp.StatusCode, body)
	}
	for {
		frame := stream.nextEvent()
		if frame.event != "host_status" {
			t.Fatalf("frame = %s %s, want host_status first", frame.event, frame.data)
		}
		if state := frame.json(t)["state"]; state == "live" {
			break
		}
	}

	observer := &dmFakeObserver{}
	bridgeDockerOperations(observer, ls.s.DockerWatch)
	observer.fn(dockerstacks.Operation{ID: "op_0123456789abcdef", HostID: "local", Stack: "shop", Kind: "up", State: "queued", Output: "dropped from the message"})
	for {
		frame := stream.nextEvent()
		if frame.event == "operation" {
			if got := dmObject(t, frame.json(t), "operation"); got["state"] != "queued" || got["output"] != "" {
				t.Fatalf("operation = %s", frame.data)
			}
			break
		}
	}

	stream.close()
	waitUntilTrue(t, "the hub client of the closed stream to go", func() bool {
		_, open := ls.s.DockerWatch.Client(id)
		return !open
	})
}

// waitUntilTrue polls cond for up to five seconds.
func waitUntilTrue(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// dmOpenLiveStream opens a stream on the real hub and returns it with its id.
func dmOpenLiveStream(t *testing.T, ls *dmLiveServer) (*dmStream, string) {
	t.Helper()
	stream := ls.open(http.MethodGet, "/stream", nil, nil)
	hello := stream.nextEvent()
	id, _ := hello.json(t)["stream_id"].(string)
	if hello.event != "hello" || id == "" {
		t.Fatalf("hello = %+v", hello)
	}
	return stream, id
}

// dmSubscribe replaces the subscription of a stream and requires a 200.
func dmSubscribe(t *testing.T, ls *dmLiveServer, id string, body map[string]any) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	body["stream_id"] = id
	put := ls.open(http.MethodPut, "/stream/subscriptions", body, nil)
	answer := put.body()
	if put.resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK || answer["status"] != "ok" {
		t.Fatalf("PUT /stream/subscriptions = %d %v", put.resp.StatusCode, answer)
	}
	return answer
}

func TestDockerManagerSubscriptionSendsTheCurrentHostStatusOfEveryNewHost(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	first, firstID := dmOpenLiveStream(t, ls)
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, firstID, map[string]any{"hosts": []string{"local"}})
	for {
		if frame := first.nextEvent(); frame.event == "host_status" && frame.json(t)["state"] == "live" {
			break
		}
	}

	// A second window finds the watcher running: its status is sent although it did not change.
	second, secondID := dmOpenLiveStream(t, ls)
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, secondID, map[string]any{"hosts": []string{"local"}})
	if frame := second.nextEvent(); frame.event != "host_status" || frame.json(t)["host"] != "local" || frame.json(t)["state"] != "live" {
		t.Fatalf("first frame after the subscription = %s %s, want host_status live", frame.event, frame.data)
	}

	// A host that leaves and comes back is new to the stream again.
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, secondID, map[string]any{"hosts": []string{}})
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, secondID, map[string]any{"hosts": []string{"local"}})
	if frame := second.nextEvent(); frame.event != "host_status" || frame.json(t)["state"] != "live" {
		t.Fatalf("frame after the host came back = %s %s, want host_status live", frame.event, frame.data)
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerSubscriptionSendsStatsHistoryBeforeLivePoints(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	first, firstID := dmOpenLiveStream(t, ls)
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, firstID, map[string]any{"stats": map[string][]string{"local": {"aaaaaaaaaaaa"}}})
	for seen := 0; seen < 2; {
		if first.nextEvent().event == "stats" {
			seen++
		}
	}

	// The container has a ring now: a window that asks later gets it first, oldest point first.
	second, secondID := dmOpenLiveStream(t, ls)
	dmSubscribe(t, ls, secondID, map[string]any{"stats": map[string][]string{"local": {"aaaaaaaaaaaa"}}})
	history := second.nextEvent()
	points, _ := history.json(t)["points"].([]any)
	if history.event != "stats_history" || history.json(t)["host"] != "local" || history.json(t)["id"] != "aaaaaaaaaaaa" || len(points) < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("first frame = %s %s, want stats_history with the points so far", history.event, history.data)
	}
	last, _ := points[len(points)-1].(map[string]any)
	live := second.nextEvent()
	point := dmObject(t, live.json(t), "point")
	if live.event != "stats" || point["t"].(float64) <= last["t"].(float64) && point["mem"].(float64) <= last["mem"].(float64) {
		t.Fatalf("frame after the history = %s %s, want a live stats point newer than %v", live.event, live.data, last)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement**

**Create `internal/server/docker_manager_stream.go`**

```go
package server

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerwatch"
)

// ── Docker Manager live stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────
// GET /stream is one server-sent event stream per open Docker Manager window; it
// carries what the hub produces (host_status, event, resync, stats,
// stats_history, stats_gone, host_stats, operation, dropped). What a window
// receives is chosen with PUT /stream/subscriptions, which names the stream by
// the id of its hello message. Both routes read only: docker.readonly allows them.

// dmStreamLimits are the limits the hello message tells the client about.
type dmStreamLimits struct {
	StatsIDs int `json:"stats_ids"`
	Hosts    int `json:"hosts"`
}

// dmStreamHello is the first message of a stream.
type dmStreamHello struct {
	StreamID    string         `json:"stream_id"`
	HeartbeatMS int64          `json:"heartbeat_ms"`
	Limits      dmStreamLimits `json:"limits"`
}

// liveStream serves GET /stream. The first frame is `hello`; then every message
// of the hub's client in order; a comment line every dmSSEHeartbeat while quiet.
// The stream ends when the request ends, when a write fails or times out, or when
// the hub closes the client (a client that fell 512 messages behind is sent
// `dropped` first). The hub client is always closed.
func (dm *dmRequest) liveStream() {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	flusher, ok := dm.w.(http.Flusher)
	if !ok {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusInternalServerError, dmCodeInternal, "streaming is not supported", nil)
		return
	}
	client, err := live.Attach()
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrTooManyClients) || errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrHubClosed) {
			dm.liveFailure(err, "")
			return
		}
		dm.internalFailure("Docker live stream could not be opened", err)
		return
	}
	defer client.Close()

	header := dm.w.Header()
	header.Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
	header.Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
	header.Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
	dm.w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
	stream := &dmEventStream{w: dm.w, flusher: flusher, rc: http.NewResponseController(dm.w)}

	hello := dmStreamHello{
		StreamID:    client.ID(),
		HeartbeatMS: dmSSEHeartbeat.Milliseconds(),
		Limits:      dmStreamLimits{StatsIDs: dockerwatch.MaxStatsIDs, Hosts: dockerwatch.MaxSubscribedHosts},
	}
	if stream.send("hello", hello) != nil {
		return
	}
	beat := time.NewTicker(dmSSEHeartbeat)
	defer beat.Stop()
	ctx := dm.r.Context()
	messages := client.Messages()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-beat.C:
			if stream.comment("heartbeat") != nil {
				return
			}
		case msg, open := <-messages:
			if !open {
				return
			}
			if stream.send(msg.Event, msg.Data) != nil {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

// dmSubscriptionRequest is the body of PUT /stream/subscriptions. It replaces
// the whole subscription of the stream.
type dmSubscriptionRequest struct {
	StreamID  string              `json:"stream_id"`
	Hosts     []string            `json:"hosts"`
	Stats     map[string][]string `json:"stats"`
	HostStats []string            `json:"host_stats"`
}

// Reasons of a rejected host.
const (
	dmRejectHostNotFound    = dmCodeHostNotFound // no host with this id (a malformed id included)
	dmRejectHostUnavailable = "host_unavailable" // the registry could not look the host up
)

// dmRejectedHost names a host of a subscription that was left out and why.
type dmRejectedHost struct {
	Host   string `json:"host"`
	Reason string `json:"reason"`
}

// liveSubscriptions serves PUT /stream/subscriptions. A host the registry does
// not know (or cannot look up) is left out of the subscription and listed in
// `rejected` with a reason; it never fails the request. The rest is stored as a
// whole, and the hub sends the current `host_status` of every host that is new
// to this stream. An unknown stream id answers 404 stream_not_found, a
// subscription over a limit or with a malformed container id 400 bad_request
// with the hub's message (it names the limit).
func (dm *dmRequest) liveSubscriptions() {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodPut) {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	var req dmSubscriptionRequest
	if !dm.decode(&req) {
		return
	}
	client, found := live.Client(req.StreamID)
	if !found {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusNotFound, dmCodeStreamNotFound, "There is no open stream with this id", nil)
		return
	}
	sub := dockerwatch.Subscription{Hosts: req.Hosts, Stats: req.Stats, HostStats: req.HostStats}
	rejected := []dmRejectedHost{}
	if dmFewHosts(sub) {
		ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmRegistryTimeout)
		sub, rejected = dm.dropUnusableHosts(ctx, sub)
		cancel()
	}
	accepted, err := client.Set(sub)
	switch {
	case err == nil:
		dmWriteOK(dm.w, http.StatusOK, dmFields{"accepted": accepted, "rejected": rejected})
	case errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrInvalidSubscription):
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, err.Error(), nil)
	case errors.Is(err, dockerwatch.ErrClientClosed):
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusNotFound, dmCodeStreamNotFound, "There is no open stream with this id", nil)
	default:
		dm.liveFailure(err, "")
	}
}

// dmFewHosts reports whether a subscription can still be within the hub's host
// limits: more than three lists' worth of distinct hosts cannot, and the hub then
// refuses it as a whole, so the registry is not asked about each of them.
func dmFewHosts(sub dockerwatch.Subscription) bool {
	return len(dmSubscribedHosts(sub)) <= 3*dockerwatch.MaxSubscribedHosts
}

// dmSubscribedHosts lists the distinct host ids a subscription names, sorted.
func dmSubscribedHosts(sub dockerwatch.Subscription) []string {
	hosts := slices.Concat(sub.Hosts, sub.HostStats)
	for host := range sub.Stats {
		hosts = append(hosts, host)
	}
	sort.Strings(hosts)
	return slices.Compact(hosts)
}

// dropUnusableHosts removes the hosts the registry does not know, or cannot look
// up, from every list of the subscription and returns them, sorted by id, with
// the reason.
func (dm *dmRequest) dropUnusableHosts(ctx context.Context, sub dockerwatch.Subscription) (dockerwatch.Subscription, []dmRejectedHost) {
	dropped := map[string]bool{}
	rejected := []dmRejectedHost{}
	for _, host := range dmSubscribedHosts(sub) {
		_, err := dm.registry().Host(ctx, host)
		if err == nil {
			continue
		}
		reason := dmRejectHostNotFound
		if !errors.Is(err, dockerhost.ErrHostNotFound) {
			dm.s.logDockerManager("Docker stream subscription could not look up a host", err)
			reason = dmRejectHostUnavailable
		}
		dropped[host] = true
		rejected = append(rejected, dmRejectedHost{Host: host, Reason: reason})
	}
	if len(dropped) == 0 {
		return sub, rejected
	}
	kept := dockerwatch.Subscription{
		Hosts:     slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(sub.Hosts), func(host string) bool { return dropped[host] }),
		HostStats: slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(sub.HostStats), func(host string) bool { return dropped[host] }),
		Stats:     map[string][]string{},
	}
	for host, ids := range sub.Stats {
		if !dropped[host] {
			kept.Stats[host] = ids
		}
	}
	return kept, rejected
}
```

### Task C3: Log follow for containers, stacks and projects

**Files:**
- Create (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_logs_test.go`
- Create: `internal/server/docker_manager_logs.go`
- Modify: `internal/server/docker_manager_containers.go`
- Modify: `internal/server/docker_manager_stacks.go`

The three follow routes share `streamLogs`: it validates nothing itself (the callers parse `tail` and `since` first), starts the follower with `FollowOptions.Opened` set to `dmLogStream.open`, and turns the follower's callbacks into events. The headers of the event stream go out only in `Opened`; an error that comes earlier (unknown host, container, stack or project, no free slot, an unreachable host) is answered as the usual JSON, so a client can tell them apart by the status. After the headers, a follower that ends cleanly closes the stream with `end {reason: "ended"}`; any other error ends it with `end {reason: "error", code, message}` (the code `dmLiveFailureOf` would have answered); a client that left, or a write that failed, gets nothing more. `out`, `notice`, the 15 s heartbeat comment (its own goroutine) and `end` write under one mutex, and a failed heartbeat write cancels the follow. A stack follows `ProjectSelector{Project: name, WorkingDir: <its folder>}` with the folder from `Service.List` (deviation 4 in the notes); an external project follows `{Project}`, or `{Project, WorkingDir: <folder>, Exclude: true}` when a stack of that name exists, and is 404 `project_not_found` when no container matches (`ProjectSelector.Matches` over the container list). `projectSub` is the new owner of `/hosts/{id}/projects/{project}/{sub}`: `logs` here, everything else (`start`, `stop`, `restart`, an unknown action) is `projectAction`, unchanged. `GET .../containers/{ref}/logs` without `follow` stays the phase 1 JSON.

```go
package server

	"context"

// dmLines is a batch of two log lines.
func dmLines() dockerwatch.LogBatch {
	return dockerwatch.LogBatch{Lines: []dockerwatch.LogEntry{
		{T: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 29, 123456789, time.UTC), S: "out", Text: "hello", Svc: "web", Ctr: "aaaaaaaaaaaa"},
		{T: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 30, 0, time.UTC), S: "err", Text: "boom", Trunc: true},
	}}
}

func TestDockerManagerContainerLogsFollowStreamsLinesNoticesAndEnds(t *testing.T) {
	f := newDMLiveFixture(t)
	f.live.follow = func(_ context.Context, call dmFollowCall, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error {
		call.opt.Opened()
		if err := out(dmLines()); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := notice(dockerwatch.Notice{Code: dockerwatch.NoticeNotFollowed, Message: "no slot", Services: []string{"db"}, Container: "bbbbbbbbbbbb"}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return out(dockerwatch.LogBatch{Lines: []dockerwatch.LogEntry{{T: time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 31, 0, time.UTC), S: "out", Text: "last"}}})
	}

	// The reconnect of the UI: the newest tail together with the time of the newest line.
	stream := f.open(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/containers/web1/logs?follow=1&tail=5000&since=2026-10-28T07:33:29.123456789Z", nil)
	if got := stream.resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"); got != "text/event-stream" {
		t.Fatalf("Content-Type = %q", got)
	}
	lines := stream.nextEvent()
	entries, _ := lines.json(t)["lines"].([]any)
	first, _ := entries[0].(map[string]any)
	second, _ := entries[1].(map[string]any)
	if lines.event != "lines" || len(entries) != 2 || first["t"] != "2026-10-28T07:33:29.123456789Z" || first["s"] != "out" || first["text"] != "hello" ||
		first["trunc"] != false || first["svc"] != "web" || first["ctr"] != "aaaaaaaaaaaa" || second["s"] != "err" || second["trunc"] != true || second["svc"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("lines = %s %s", lines.event, lines.data)
	}
	notice := stream.nextEvent()
	if got := notice.json(t); notice.event != "notice" || got["code"] != "not_followed" || got["message"] != "no slot" || got["container"] != "bbbbbbbbbbbb" || len(got["services"].([]any)) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("notice = %s %s", notice.event, notice.data)
	}
	if last := stream.nextEvent(); last.event != "lines" {
		t.Fatalf("frame = %s %s, want the last lines", last.event, last.data)
	}
	if end := stream.nextEvent(); end.event != "end" || end.json(t)["reason"] != "ended" || end.json(t)["code"] != nil {
		t.Fatalf("end = %s %s, want reason ended", end.event, end.data)
	}
	stream.expectEnd()

	call := f.live.lastCall(t)
	if call.host != "local" || call.ref != "web1" || call.opt.Tail != 5000 || !call.opt.Since.Equal(time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 7, 33, 29, 123456789, time.UTC)) {
		t.Fatalf("follower got %+v, want host local, web1, tail 5000 and the since time", call)
	}

	// Without a tail the container default is 200 and there is no since.
	f.open(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/containers/web1/logs?follow=1", nil).nextEvent()
	if call := f.live.lastCall(t); call.opt.Tail != 200 || !call.opt.Since.IsZero() {
		t.Fatalf("follower got %+v, want the default tail 200", call.opt)
	}
}

		<-ctx.Done()
		returned <- ctx.Err()
		return ctx.Err()
	}
	stream := f.open(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/containers/web1/logs?follow=1", nil)
	if frame := stream.next(); frame.comment != "heartbeat" {

	stream.close()
	select {
	case err := <-returned:
		if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
			t.Fatalf("follower ended with %v, want a cancelled context", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the follower kept running after the client left")
	}
}

	}
	if q := ls.engine.logRequests(); len(q) != 1 || !strings.Contains(q[0], "follow=1") || !strings.Contains(q[0], "tail=5000") || !strings.Contains(q[0], "since=") || !strings.Contains(q[0], "timestamps=1") {
		t.Fatalf("log requests = %v, want follow, tail 5000, since and timestamps", q)
	}

	ls.engine.release() // the container's log ends
	if end := stream.nextEvent(); end.event != "end" || end.json(t)["reason"] != "ended" {
		t.Fatalf("end = %s %s", end.event, end.data)
	}
	stream.expectEnd()

	ls.open(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/containers/ghost/logs?follow=1", nil, nil).expectError(http.StatusNotFound, "container_not_found")
	// With every stream slot of the host taken, a follow is refused as JSON.
	for i := 0; i < dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost; i++ {
		release, err := ls.s.DockerWatch.Acquire("local")
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Acquire %d: %v", i, err)
		}
		t.Cleanup(release)
	}
	ls.open(http.MethodGet, "/hosts/local/containers/web/logs?follow=1", nil, nil).expectError(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too_many_streams")
}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"
	"aurago/internal/dockerstacks"
	"aurago/internal/dockerwatch"
)

// ── Docker Manager log follow ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// The three `logs?follow=1` routes answer a server-sent event stream:
//
//   - "event: lines":  {"lines":[{"t","s","text","trunc","svc","ctr"}, ...]}
//   - "event: notice": {"code","message","services","container"}
//   - "event: end":    {"reason":"ended"} or {"reason":"error","code","message"}
//   - ": heartbeat" comments every dmSSEHeartbeat while nothing happens.
//
// Anything that goes wrong before the stream is up (unknown host, container,
// stack or project, no free stream slot, an unreachable host, a bad query) is an
// ordinary JSON error answer; the headers of the stream go out only when the
// follower reports that it is established (FollowOptions.Opened). A client that
// leaves ends the follow and gets nothing more. docker.readonly allows it.

const (
	dmLogTailContainer = 200 // default `tail` of a container
	dmLogTailProject   = 100 // default `tail` per container of a stack or project
)

// logOptions reads `tail` (0 to 5000, default def) and `since` (RFC 3339) of a
// follow request. A bad value answers 400.
func (dm *dmRequest) logOptions(def int) (dockerwatch.FollowOptions, bool) {
	query := dm.r.URL.Query()
	opt := dockerwatch.FollowOptions{Tail: def}
	if raw := query.Get("tail"); raw != "" {
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(raw)
		if err != nil || n < 0 || n > dockerwatch.MaxLogTail {
			dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, "tail must be a number from 0 to "+strconv.Itoa(dockerwatch.MaxLogTail), nil)
			return opt, false
		}
		opt.Tail = n
	}
	if raw := query.Get("since"); raw != "" {
		since, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, raw)
		if err != nil {
			dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, "since must be an RFC 3339 time, for example 2026-10-28T07:33:29Z", nil)
			return opt, false
		}
		opt.Since = since
	}
	return opt, true
}

// dmFollowFunc starts one follower with the options, the callbacks of the
// stream and the context that ends it.
type dmFollowFunc func(ctx context.Context, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error

// containerLogsFollow serves GET /hosts/{id}/containers/{ref}/logs?follow=1.
func (dm *dmRequest) containerLogsFollow(hostID, ref string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	opt, ok := dm.logOptions(dmLogTailContainer)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmRegistryTimeout)
	_, known := dm.host(ctx, hostID)
	cancel()
	if !known {
		return
	}
	dm.streamLogs(opt, dmCodeContainerNotFound, func(ctx context.Context, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error {
		return live.FollowContainer(ctx, hostID, ref, opt, out, notice)
	})
}

// stackFolder finds a managed stack of the host in the stacks listing (the
// cached folder scan, the containers read live) and returns its folder on the
// host. found is false when the host has no stack of that name.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackFolder(ctx context.Context, svc dmStackService, hostID, name string) (dir string, found bool, err error) {
	listing, err := svc.List(ctx, hostID, false)
	if err != nil {
		return "", false, err
	}
	for _, stack := range listing.Stacks {
		if stack.Name == name {
			return stack.Dir, true, nil
		}
	}
	return "", false, nil
}

// followRequired answers 400 unless the request carries follow=1: stack and
// project logs exist only as a stream.
func (dm *dmRequest) followRequired() bool {
	if dmTruthy(dm.r.URL.Query().Get("follow")) {
		return true
	}
	dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeBadRequest, "logs of a stack or project are a live stream: add follow=1", nil)
	return false
}

// stackLogs serves GET /hosts/{id}/stacks/{name}/logs?follow=1: the merged logs
// of the containers the stack's folder started. A stack without containers is a
// valid stream (nothing is sent until one starts); an unknown stack is 404
// stack_not_found.
func (dm *dmRequest) stackLogs(hostID, name string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) || !dm.followRequired() {
		return
	}
	svc, ok := dm.stackService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	opt, ok := dm.logOptions(dmLogTailProject)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	if err := dockerstacks.ValidateName(name); err != nil {
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	dir, found, err := dm.stackFolder(ctx, svc, hostID, name)
	cancel()
	switch {
	case err != nil:
		dm.stackFailure(err)
		return
	case !found:
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusNotFound, dockerstacks.CodeStackNotFound, "there is no stack "+strconv.Quote(name)+" on this host", nil)
		return
	}
	sel := dockerwatch.ProjectSelector{Project: name, WorkingDir: dir}
	dm.streamLogs(opt, "", func(ctx context.Context, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error {
		return live.FollowProject(ctx, hostID, sel, opt, out, notice)
	})
}

// projectSub serves /hosts/{id}/projects/{project}/{logs|start|stop|restart}.
func (dm *dmRequest) projectSub(hostID, project, sub string) {
	if sub == "logs" {
		dm.projectLogs(hostID, project)
		return
	}
	dm.projectAction(hostID, project, sub)
}

// projectLogs serves GET /hosts/{id}/projects/{project}/logs?follow=1: the merged
// logs of an external compose project. When the host has a stack of the same
// name, only the containers that do not come from that stack's folder belong to
// the project (the same split the stack list makes). A project without any
// container is 404 project_not_found.
func (dm *dmRequest) projectLogs(hostID, project string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) || !dm.followRequired() {
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	opt, ok := dm.logOptions(dmLogTailProject)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmStackReadTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	_, client, ok := dm.engine(ctx, hostID)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	sel := dockerwatch.ProjectSelector{Project: project}
	if dm.stacks != nil {
		dir, found, err := dm.stackFolder(ctx, dm.stacks, hostID, project)
		var coded *dockerstacks.Error
		switch {
		case err == nil && found:
			sel.WorkingDir, sel.Exclude = dir, true
		case err == nil, errors.As(err, &coded):
			// No stack of that name, or a host without the stack helpers (it has no
			// stacks): the whole project is external.
		default:
			dm.stackFailure(err)
			return
		}
	}
	list, err := dockerhost.ListContainers(ctx, client)
	if err != nil {
		dm.engineFailure(err, "")
		return
	}
	members := 0
	for _, container := range list {
		if sel.Matches(container) {
			members++
		}
	}
	if members == 0 {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusNotFound, dmCodeProjectNotFound, "there is no compose project "+strconv.Quote(project)+" with containers on this host", nil)
		return
	}
	cancel()
	dm.streamLogs(opt, "", func(ctx context.Context, opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, out func(dockerwatch.LogBatch) error, notice func(dockerwatch.Notice) error) error {
		return live.FollowProject(ctx, hostID, sel, opt, out, notice)
	})
}

// dmLogStream is the event stream of one follow. Lines, notices and the
// heartbeat are written by different goroutines under one mutex.
type dmLogStream struct {
	dm     *dmRequest
	cancel context.CancelFunc // ends the follow when a write fails

	once   sync.Once
	stop   chan struct{} // ends the heartbeat
	done   chan struct{} // closed when the heartbeat goroutine has returned
	mu     sync.Mutex
	stream *dmEventStream // nil until open
	failed bool           // a write failed: the client is gone or too slow
}

// open sends the headers of the event stream and starts the heartbeat. It is the
// follower's Opened callback and runs once.
func (l *dmLogStream) open() {
	l.once.Do(func() {
		w := l.dm.w
		flusher := w.(http.Flusher) // checked by streamLogs
		header := w.Header()
		header.Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
		header.Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
		header.Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no")
		l.mu.Lock()
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		flusher.Flush()
		l.stream = &dmEventStream{w: w, flusher: flusher, rc: http.NewResponseController(w)}
		l.mu.Unlock()
		go l.heartbeat()
	})
}

func (l *dmLogStream) opened() bool {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return l.stream != nil
}

// heartbeat writes a comment line whenever the stream has been quiet for
// dmSSEHeartbeat, and ends the follow when that write fails.
func (l *dmLogStream) heartbeat() {
	defer close(l.done)
	tick := time.NewTicker(dmSSEHeartbeat)
	defer tick.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-l.stop:
			return
		case <-tick.C:
			if l.write(func(st *dmEventStream) error { return st.comment("heartbeat") }) != nil {
				l.cancel()
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

// write runs one write on the stream under the mutex. After a failed write it
// refuses all further ones.
func (l *dmLogStream) write(fn func(*dmEventStream) error) error {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	if l.stream == nil {
		return errors.New("the log stream is not open")
	}
	if l.failed {
		return errors.New("the log stream is closed")
	}
	if err := fn(l.stream); err != nil {
		l.failed = true
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

func (l *dmLogStream) lines(batch dockerwatch.LogBatch) error {
	return l.write(func(st *dmEventStream) error { return st.send("lines", batch) })
}

func (l *dmLogStream) notice(n dockerwatch.Notice) error {
	return l.write(func(st *dmEventStream) error { return st.send("notice", n) })
}

// dmLogEnd is the data of the closing `end` event.
type dmLogEnd struct {
	Reason  string `json:"reason"` // ended | error
	Code    string `json:"code,omitempty"`
	Message string `json:"message,omitempty"`
}

// finish stops the heartbeat and writes the closing event for the follower's
// result: err nil is a log that ended; an error is reported with the code the
// route would have answered with before the stream was up. A follow that the
// client cancelled, or one whose writes failed, gets nothing.
func (l *dmLogStream) finish(err error, notFoundCode string) {
	close(l.stop)
	<-l.done
	if l.dm.r.Context().Err() != nil {
		return
	}
	end := dmLogEnd{Reason: "ended"}
	if err != nil {
		failure := dmLiveFailureOf(err, notFoundCode)
		end = dmLogEnd{Reason: "error", Code: failure.code, Message: failure.message}
	}
	_ = l.write(func(st *dmEventStream) error { return st.send("end", end) })
}

// streamLogs runs a follower and turns its callbacks into the event stream.
// Errors that precede the stream's start are answered as JSON.
func (dm *dmRequest) streamLogs(opt dockerwatch.FollowOptions, notFoundCode string, run dmFollowFunc) {
	if _, ok := dm.w.(http.Flusher); !ok {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusInternalServerError, dmCodeInternal, "streaming is not supported", nil)
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(dm.r.Context())
	defer cancel()
	ls := &dmLogStream{dm: dm, cancel: cancel, stop: make(chan struct{}), done: make(chan struct{})}
	opt.Opened = ls.open
	err := run(ctx, opt, ls.lines, ls.notice)

	if !ls.opened() {
		if dm.r.Context().Err() != nil {
			return // the client left before the stream was up
		}
		if err != nil {
			dm.liveFailure(err, notFoundCode)
			return
		}
		ls.open() // a follower that ended without ever opening: an empty stream that ended
	}
	ls.finish(err, notFoundCode)
}
```

### Task C4: The terminal route and the read-only scope

**Files:**
- Create (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_terminal_api_test.go`
- Create (test): `internal/server/docker_manager_live_rules_test.go`
- Create: `internal/server/docker_manager_terminal_api.go`

The terminal route runs every check that can refuse the request as plain JSON before the upgrade, in the order of deviation 1 in the notes, so that the desktop app can explain a refused handshake with a plain GET. It uses the inspect document (`dockerhost.InspectContainer`: `state.Running`, `config.labels`) for the running and helper checks (`dmHelperRole`, the phase 2 detection), `protectionAllowed` for the protection rule, and `Hub.Acquire` for the stream slot, which the session holds until it ends. A request without the upgrade headers frees the slot and answers 400 `websocket_required`; it never reaches `newDockerManagerTerminalSession`. `removeAllowed` is split first: the helper check stays in it and the rest becomes `protectionAllowed(ctx, host, client, ref, action)`, which the terminal calls with the action `terminal`. `containerSub` routes `terminal` (until now it answered `invalid_action`). `docker.readonly` refuses the terminal (403 `read_only`, first after the method) and allows the stream, subscriptions, follows and disk usage; `TestDockerManagerLiveReadsStayAllowedInReadOnlyMode` pins the whole scope.

```go
package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerwatch"

	"github.com/gorilla/websocket"
)

// dmTerminalProbe is how a terminal request ended: the HTTP status and the JSON
// answer of a refusal, or a connected WebSocket.
type dmTerminalProbe struct {
	status int
	body   map[string]any
	conn   *websocket.Conn
}

func (ls *dmLiveServer) wsURL(path string) string {
	return "ws" + strings.TrimPrefix(ls.url, "http") + "/api/docker-manager" + path
}

func dmProbeOf(resp *http.Response) dmTerminalProbe {
	raw, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	var body map[string]any
	_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &body)
	return dmTerminalProbe{status: resp.StatusCode, body: body}
}

// handshake asks for the terminal the way the browser does.
func (ls *dmLiveServer) handshake(path string, headers http.Header) dmTerminalProbe {
	ls.t.Helper()
	conn, resp, err := websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(ls.wsURL(path), headers)
	if err == nil {
		ls.t.Cleanup(func() { _ = conn.Close() })
		return dmTerminalProbe{status: resp.StatusCode, conn: conn}
	}
	if resp == nil {
		ls.t.Fatalf("handshake %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	return dmProbeOf(resp)
}

// diagnose asks for the same URL without the upgrade headers, as the desktop app
// does after a refused handshake to read the reason.
func (ls *dmLiveServer) diagnose(path string, headers http.Header) dmTerminalProbe {
	ls.t.Helper()
	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, ls.url+"/api/docker-manager"+path, nil)
	if err != nil {
		ls.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for key, values := range headers {
		req.Header[key] = values
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		ls.t.Fatalf("GET %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	return dmProbeOf(resp)
}

// dmTerminalSlots counts the stream slots that are free on the host.
func dmTerminalSlots(t *testing.T, hub *dockerwatch.Hub, host string) int {
	t.Helper()
	var releases []func()
	for {
		release, err := hub.Acquire(host)
		if err != nil {
			break
		}
		releases = append(releases, release)
	}
	for _, release := range releases {
		release()
	}
	return len(releases)
}

func TestDockerManagerTerminalExplainsEveryRefusalAsJSONBeforeTheUpgrade(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	remote := newDMLiveEngine(t, dmContainersJSON(t,
		dmContainerJSON('w', "web", "sha256:img1", "running", "bridge", map[string]string{"aurago.managed": "ruview"}, nil)))
	nas := ls.addTCPHost("NAS", remote)

	hold := func(t *testing.T) {
		for i := 0; i < dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost; i++ {
			release, err := ls.s.DockerWatch.Acquire("local")
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Acquire %d: %v", i, err)
			}
			t.Cleanup(release)
		}
	}
	protectLocal := func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Cleanup(replaceContainerProtection(containerProtection{Owner: "ruview"}))
	}
	setReadOnly := func(on bool) {
		ls.s.CfgMu.Lock()
		ls.s.Cfg.Docker.ReadOnly = on
		ls.s.CfgMu.Unlock()
	}
	readOnly := func(t *testing.T) {
		setReadOnly(true)
		t.Cleanup(func() { setReadOnly(false) })
	}

	cross := http.Header{"Origin": []string{"http://evil.example"}}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		path    string
		headers http.Header
		setup   func(t *testing.T)
		status  int
		code    string
	}{
		{"read-only", "/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil, readOnly, http.StatusForbidden, "read_only"},
		{"cross-origin", "/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", cross, nil, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden_origin"},
		{"unknown host", "/hosts/nowhere/containers/web/terminal", nil, nil, http.StatusNotFound, "host_not_found"},
		{"unknown container", "/hosts/local/containers/ghost/terminal", nil, nil, http.StatusNotFound, "container_not_found"},
		{"stopped container", "/hosts/local/containers/stopped/terminal", nil, nil, http.StatusConflict, "container_not_running"},
		{"helper container", "/hosts/local/containers/helper/terminal", nil, nil, http.StatusConflict, "helper_container"},
		{"protected local container", "/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil, protectLocal, http.StatusConflict, "container_protected_confirmation_required"},
		{"protected remote container", "/hosts/" + nas + "/containers/web/terminal", nil, nil, http.StatusConflict, "container_protected_confirmation_required"},
		{"no stream slot", "/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil, hold, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too_many_streams"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if tc.setup != nil {
				tc.setup(t)
			}
			for mode, probe := range map[string]func(string, http.Header) dmTerminalProbe{"handshake": ls.handshake, "plain GET": ls.diagnose} {
				got := probe(tc.path, tc.headers)
				if got.status != tc.status || got.body["status"] != "error" || got.body["code"] != tc.code {
					t.Fatalf("%s: answer = %d %v, want %d error %q", mode, got.status, got.body, tc.status, tc.code)
				}
			}
		})
	}
	if t.Failed() {
		return
	}

	// The reason of the protection is named, so the confirmation can say who owns the container.
	if got := ls.diagnose("/hosts/"+nas+"/containers/web/terminal", nil); got.body["owner"] != "ruview" {
		t.Fatalf("remote protection answer = %v, want the owner ruview", got.body)
	}
	if got := ls.diagnose("/hosts/local/containers/helper/terminal", nil); got.body["role"] != "runner" {
		t.Fatalf("helper answer = %v, want the helper role", got.body)
	}
	ls.open(http.MethodPost, "/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil, nil).expectError(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "method_not_allowed")
}

func TestDockerManagerTerminalPlainGETNeverCreatesAnExecOrKeepsASlot(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	got := ls.diagnose("/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil)
	if got.status != http.StatusBadRequest || got.body["code"] != "websocket_required" {
		t.Fatalf("plain GET = %d %v, want 400 websocket_required once every check has passed", got.status, got.body)
	}
	if execs := ls.engine.term.find(http.MethodPost, "/containers/web/exec"); len(execs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a plain GET created %d exec(s)", len(execs))
	}
	if free := dmTerminalSlots(t, ls.s.DockerWatch, "local"); free != dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost {
		t.Fatalf("%d of %d stream slots are free after a plain GET, want all", free, dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost)
	}
}

func TestDockerManagerTerminalServesTheSharedProtocolOnAnyHost(t *testing.T) {
	ls := newDMLiveServer(t, "[]")
	remote := newDMLiveEngine(t, dmContainersJSON(t,
		dmContainerJSON('w', "web", "sha256:img1", "running", "bridge", map[string]string{"aurago.managed": "ruview"}, nil)))
	nas := ls.addTCPHost("NAS", remote)

	roundTrip := func(conn *websocket.Conn) {
		t.Helper()
		readText := func(n int) string {
			var got []byte
			_ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
			for len(got) < n {
				_, payload, err := conn.ReadMessage()
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("read: %v (got %q)", err, got)
				}
				got = append(got, payload...)
			}
			return string(got)
		}
		if got := readText(len("ready$ ")); got != "ready$ " {
			t.Fatalf("prompt = %q", got)
		}
		if err := conn.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage, []byte("pwd\r")); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := readText(4); got != "pwd\r" {
			t.Fatalf("echo = %q", got)
		}
	}

	// The local host: the whole protocol, and the slot is held while the session runs.
	local := ls.handshake("/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil)
	if local.conn == nil || local.status != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
		t.Fatalf("handshake = %+v, want a WebSocket", local)
	}
	roundTrip(local.conn)
	if free := dmTerminalSlots(t, ls.s.DockerWatch, "local"); free != dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost-1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d stream slots free during a session, want %d", free, dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost-1)
	}
	if err := local.conn.WriteMessage(websocket.TextMessage, []byte(`{"type":"resize","cols":90,"rows":20}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	dmTermWaitFor(t, "the resize", func() bool {
		rs := ls.engine.term.find(http.MethodPost, "/exec/exec-1/resize")
		return len(rs) == 2 && rs[1].query == "h=20&w=90"
	})
	if err := local.conn.WriteMessage(websocket.TextMessage, []byte(`{"type":"end"}`)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	dmTermWaitFor(t, "the end helper", func() bool { return len(ls.engine.term.find(http.MethodPost, "/exec/exec-2/start")) == 1 })
	_ = local.conn.Close()
	dmTermWaitFor(t, "the exec stream to close", func() bool { return ls.engine.term.hijack.Load() == 1 })
	dmTermWaitFor(t, "the stream slot to come back", func() bool {
		return dmTerminalSlots(t, ls.s.DockerWatch, "local") == dockerwatch.MaxStreamsPerHost
	})

	// A protected container of a remote host needs the confirmation; with it the exec runs on that host's Engine.
	remoteWS := ls.handshake("/hosts/"+nas+"/containers/web/terminal?confirm=protected", nil)
	if remoteWS.conn == nil {
		t.Fatalf("confirmed handshake = %+v, want a WebSocket", remoteWS)
	}
	roundTrip(remoteWS.conn)
	if n := len(remote.term.find(http.MethodPost, "/containers/web/exec")); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d exec(s) on the remote Engine, want 1", n)
	}

	// The same for a protected container of the local host.
	t.Cleanup(replaceContainerProtection(containerProtection{Owner: "ruview"}))
	if got := ls.handshake("/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal", nil); got.status != http.StatusConflict {
		t.Fatalf("unconfirmed protected handshake = %d, want 409", got.status)
	}
	confirmed := ls.handshake("/hosts/local/containers/web/terminal?confirm=protected", nil)
	if confirmed.conn == nil {
		t.Fatalf("confirmed protected handshake = %+v, want a WebSocket", confirmed)
	}
}
```

**Create `internal/server/docker_manager_terminal_api.go`**

```go
package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"aurago/internal/dockerhost"

	"github.com/gorilla/websocket"
)

// ── Docker Manager terminal route ───────────────────────────────────────────
// GET /hosts/{id}/containers/{ref}/terminal is a WebSocket with the protocol of
// /api/containers/{id}/terminal (binary stdin and stdout, text frames
// {"type":"resize","cols","rows"} and {"type":"end"}) on any registered host.
// Everything that can refuse the request is checked, and answered as ordinary
// JSON, before the upgrade; a browser hides the body of a refused handshake, so
// the desktop app repeats the request without the upgrade headers to read why. For
// that reason a request without them goes through every check up to the stream
// slot too (all of them only read) and is answered 400 websocket_required only
// then; it never creates an exec.

// dmTerminalSetupTimeout bounds the checks before the upgrade (inspect, the
// protection lookup).
const dmTerminalSetupTimeout = 30 * time.Second

// dmTerminalInspect is the part of a projected inspect document the terminal
// route reads (tools.ProjectDockerInspect keeps the Engine's own state object).
type dmTerminalInspect struct {
	State struct {
		Running bool `json:"Running"`
	} `json:"state"`
	Config struct {
		Labels map[string]string `json:"labels"`
	} `json:"config"`
}

// containerTerminal serves the terminal of a container. The order of the
// answers: 405 (not GET), 403 read_only, 403 forbidden_origin, 404 for an unknown
// host or container, 409 container_not_running, 409 helper_container, 409
// container_protected_confirmation_required (the protection rule of
// /api/containers: needs ?confirm=protected; the same rule for a remote host as for
// removing a container), 429 too_many_streams, 400 websocket_required, then the
// exec is created and the connection upgraded.
func (dm *dmRequest) containerTerminal(hostID, ref string) {
	if !dm.allow(http.MethodGet) {
		return
	}
	if dm.readOnly {
		dm.readOnlyRefusal()
		return
	}
	if !sameOriginOrNoOrigin(dm.r) {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusForbidden, dmCodeForbiddenOrigin, "forbidden websocket origin", nil)
		return
	}
	live, ok := dm.liveService()
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := dm.context(dmTerminalSetupTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	host, client, ok := dm.engine(ctx, hostID)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	raw, err := dockerhost.InspectContainer(ctx, client, ref)
	if err != nil {
		dm.engineFailure(err, dmCodeContainerNotFound)
		return
	}
	var info dmTerminalInspect
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &info); err != nil {
		dm.internalFailure("Docker container inspect could not be read", err)
		return
	}
	if !info.State.Running {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusConflict, dmCodeNotRunning, "The container is not running", nil)
		return
	}
	if role := dmHelperRole(info.Config.Labels); role != "" {
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusConflict, dmCodeHelperContainer, "This is one of the Docker Manager's own helper containers; it does not take a terminal", dmFields{"role": role})
		return
	}
	if !dm.protectionAllowed(ctx, host, client, ref, "terminal") {
		return
	}
	release, err := live.Acquire(hostID)
	if err != nil {
		dm.liveFailure(err, "")
		return
	}
	defer release()
	if !websocket.IsWebSocketUpgrade(dm.r) {
		release() // a diagnosing GET holds no slot; release is idempotent
		dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusBadRequest, dmCodeWebSocketRequired, "The terminal needs a WebSocket upgrade", nil)
		return
	}

	session, err := newDockerManagerTerminalSession(dm.r.Context(), client, ref, 120, 30)
	if err != nil {
		if dockerhost.StatusOf(err) == http.StatusConflict {
			dmWriteError(dm.w, http.StatusConflict, dmCodeNotRunning, "The container is not running", nil)
			return
		}
		dm.engineFailure(err, dmCodeContainerNotFound)
		return
	}
	if dm.r.Context().Err() != nil {
		_ = session.Close()
		http.Error(dm.w, "terminal request was canceled", http.StatusRequestTimeout)
		return
	}
	conn, err := containerTerminalUpgrader.Upgrade(dm.w, dm.r, nil)
	if err != nil {
		_ = session.Close() // Upgrade has answered the handshake itself
		return
	}
	serveDockerManagerTerminal(dm.r.Context(), conn, session)
}
```

```go
// removeAllowed applies the confirmation rule of DELETE /api/containers/{id}.
// The local host, and a remote host that is the Engine AuraGo itself uses (its
// address and port equal docker.host, e.g. a tcp socket proxy), run the full
// classification of containerActionAllowed (self, Docker endpoint, shared
// network, owner). Any other remote host has its own Engine and its own
// containers: the owner from names and labels, plus the self check on the
// container's full ID (an Engine reached by another route, such as an SSH or
// tcp host on AuraGo's own machine, can still hold the container AuraGo runs
// in). The Docker Manager's helper containers are checked first, on every
// host. It writes the 409 and returns false when the request stops.
func (dm *dmRequest) removeAllowed(ctx context.Context, host dockerhost.Host, client *dockerutil.Client, ref string) bool {
	if !dm.helperRemoveAllowed(ctx, client, ref) {
		return false
	}
	cfg, _, _ := containerDockerConfig(dm.s)
	if host.ID == dockerhost.LocalHostID || host.ReachesEngineAt(cfg.Host) {
		return containerActionAllowed(dm.s, cfg, ref, "remove", dm.w, dm.r)
	}
```

with

```go
// removeAllowed applies the confirmation rule of DELETE /api/containers/{id}
// (protectionAllowed). The Docker Manager's helper containers are checked first,
// on every host. It writes the 409 and returns false when the request stops.
func (dm *dmRequest) removeAllowed(ctx context.Context, host dockerhost.Host, client *dockerutil.Client, ref string) bool {
	if !dm.helperRemoveAllowed(ctx, client, ref) {
		return false
	}
	return dm.protectionAllowed(ctx, host, client, ref, "remove")
}

// protectionAllowed applies the protected-container rule of /api/containers for
// action (remove, terminal): a protected container needs ?confirm=protected.
// The local host, and a remote host that is the Engine AuraGo itself uses (its
// address and port equal docker.host, e.g. a tcp socket proxy), run the full
// classification of containerActionAllowed (self, Docker endpoint, shared
// network, owner). Any other remote host has its own Engine and its own
// containers: the owner from names and labels, plus the self check on the
// container's full ID (an Engine reached by another route, such as an SSH or
// tcp host on AuraGo's own machine, can still hold the container AuraGo runs
// in). It writes the 409 and returns false when the request stops.
func (dm *dmRequest) protectionAllowed(ctx context.Context, host dockerhost.Host, client *dockerutil.Client, ref, action string) bool {
	cfg, _, _ := containerDockerConfig(dm.s)
	if host.ID == dockerhost.LocalHostID || host.ReachesEngineAt(cfg.Host) {
		return containerActionAllowed(dm.s, cfg, ref, action, dm.w, dm.r)
	}
```

```go
package server

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

// TestDockerManagerStaysOutOfTheDesktopIntegrationRoots pins that the Docker
// Manager is not reachable through /api/desktop/integrations/: its routes (the
// terminal and the live stream included) keep the admin gate of /api/ and never
// become part of the Desktop policy.
func TestDockerManagerStaysOutOfTheDesktopIntegrationRoots(t *testing.T) {
	for _, root := range []string{"docker-manager", "docker_manager", "dockermanager"} {
		if desktopIntegrationRoots[root] {
			t.Fatalf("desktopIntegrationRoots lists %q: the Docker Manager must not be a Desktop integration", root)
		}
	}
	s, _, _ := testDesktopPermissionServer(t)
	adminToken, _, err := s.TokenManager.Create("fixture", []string{desktopScopeAdmin}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h := desktopIntegrationHandler(s, http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		t.Errorf("%s reached the shared routes through the Desktop integrations", r.URL.Path)
	}))
	for _, path := range []string{"stream", "hosts/local/containers/web1/terminal", "hosts/local/df"} {
		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/desktop/integrations/docker-manager/"+path, nil)
		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+adminToken)
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h(rec, req)
		if rec.Code != http.StatusNotFound {
			t.Fatalf("GET /api/desktop/integrations/docker-manager/%s = %d, want 404", path, rec.Code)
		}
	}
}
```
