```markdown
- Verify `go test ./internal/server -run '(?i)(TestDockerManager|TestInitDockerHosts)'` and `go test ./internal/audit -run Manifest` (the `/api/docker-manager/` contract lists `text/event-stream`).
```

with

```markdown
- Live data (phase 3). The handlers use the hub through the narrow `dmLive` and `dmLiveClient` interfaces (`docker_manager_live.go`; `dmWatchHub` adapts `*dockerwatch.Hub`, `dmRequest.live` stays nil when the server has no hub and `liveService` then answers 503 `docker_hosts_unavailable`; handler tests use `dmFakeLive`, the end-to-end tests the real hub on `dmLiveEngine`). `engineFailureOf` is the classification behind `engineFailure` (a rejected reference 400, `notFoundCode` 404, an Engine status `docker_error`, no answer `host_unreachable` with `reason`); `dmLiveFailureOf` adds `ErrTooManyStreams` and `ErrTooManyClients` (429 `too_many_streams`), a closed hub (503) and a forgotten host (404). New codes: `stream_not_found` 404, `too_many_streams` 429, `websocket_required` 400, `container_not_running` 409, `helper_container` 409 (extra `role`), `project_not_found` 404, `forbidden_origin` 403.
- `GET /stream` (`docker_manager_stream.go`) is `text/event-stream`: `hello {stream_id (32 hex), heartbeat_ms, limits {stats_ids 50, hosts 20}}`, then the hub client's messages under their `dockerwatch.Msg*` names (`host_status`, `event`, `resync`, `stats`, `stats_history`, `stats_gone`, `host_stats`, `operation`, `dropped`; the JSON is the message type's), a comment every `dmSSEHeartbeat`, a write deadline of 30 s per write (`dmEventStream`). One goroutine writes; it returns when the request ends, a write fails or the hub closes the client, and always closes the hub client. The 33rd open stream is 429 `too_many_streams`. `operation` is `{host, operation}` with an empty `output`. `PUT /stream/subscriptions` takes `{stream_id, hosts, stats, host_stats}` (1 MiB): an unknown or closed stream is 404 `stream_not_found`; a host the registry does not know, or cannot look up, is dropped from every list and named in `rejected [{host, reason}]` (`host_not_found`, `host_unavailable`) instead of failing the request (the hub checks only the shape of ids and the limits); a limit or a malformed container id is 400 `bad_request` with the hub's message; the answer is `{status, accepted {hosts, stats, host_stats}, rejected}`. The hub sends the current `host_status` of every host that is new to the stream on each accepted PUT, and `stats_history` before the first live `stats` of a container that has a ring. Verify `TestDockerManagerStream*` and `TestDockerManagerSubscription*`.
- Log follow (`docker_manager_logs.go`): `GET …/containers/{ref}/logs?follow=1` (without `follow` the phase 1 JSON, unchanged), `GET …/stacks/{name}/logs?follow=1` and `GET …/projects/{project}/logs?follow=1` (these two exist only as streams: 400 without `follow`). `tail` 0 to 5000 (default 200 for a container, 100 per container for a stack or project; `tail=5000&since=<RFC 3339>` is the reconnect form) and `since` (RFC 3339) are validated first (400 `bad_request`). The stream is `lines {lines:[{t,s,text,trunc,svc?,ctr?}]}`, `notice {code,message,services?,container?}` and a closing `end {reason: ended}` or `{reason: error, code, message}` (the code `dmLiveFailureOf` gives the same failure before the stream is up); a client that leaves ends the follow and gets nothing more. Everything that fails before the follower reports the stream open (`FollowOptions.Opened` sends the headers) is an ordinary JSON answer: 404 `host_not_found`, `container_not_found`, `stack_not_found`, `project_not_found`, 429 `too_many_streams`, 502 `docker_error` or `host_unreachable`. `dmLogStream` writes lines, notices, the heartbeat comment (its own goroutine) and `end` under one mutex; a failed write ends the follow. The stack's folder comes from `Service.List(refresh=false)` (`stackFolder`): a stack follows `ProjectSelector{Project, WorkingDir: folder}`; an external project follows `{Project}`, or `{Project, WorkingDir: folder, Exclude: true}` when a stack of that name exists (a host without stack helpers has no stacks, the project is then whole); a project with no matching container is 404 `project_not_found`. Verify `TestDockerManagerContainerLogs*`, `TestDockerManagerLogsFollow*`, `TestDockerManagerStackLogs*` and `TestDockerManagerProjectLogs*`.
- `GET /hosts/{id}/df[?refresh=1]` answers `{status, df {images, containers, volumes, build_cache {count, active, size, reclaimable}, total}, fetched_at, cached}` from the hub's 5-minute cache (`refresh` re-reads when it is older than 60 s), within 60 s. `TestDockerManagerDiskUsage*`.
- `GET /hosts/{id}/containers/{ref}/terminal` (`docker_manager_terminal_api.go`) is a WebSocket with the protocol of `/api/containers/{id}/terminal`. A browser hides the body of a refused handshake, so the desktop app repeats the request as a plain GET to read the reason; therefore every refusal is plain JSON, and a request without the upgrade headers goes through every check up to the stream slot and is answered 400 `websocket_required` only then, never creating an exec and keeping no slot. Order: 405 (not GET), 403 `read_only`, 403 `forbidden_origin`, 404 `host_not_found`, 404 `container_not_found` (inspect), 409 `container_not_running`, 409 `helper_container` (`dmHelperRole` of the inspected labels), 409 `container_protected_confirmation_required` (`protectionAllowed`: the local host and a host that is `docker.host` use `containerActionAllowed`, any other host the owner and self rules of removal; `?confirm=protected` confirms), 429 `too_many_streams` (`Hub.Acquire`), 400 `websocket_required`, then `newDockerManagerTerminalSession` (409 `container_not_running`, 404 `container_not_found`, 502 classified), upgrade, `serveDockerManagerTerminal`; the slot is held while the session runs. Verify `TestDockerManagerTerminal*`.
- Verify `go test ./internal/server -run '(?i)(TestDockerManager|TestInitDockerHosts|TestBridgeDockerOperations)'` and `go test ./internal/audit -run Manifest` (the `/api/docker-manager/` contract lists `text/event-stream` and `websocket`); `TestDockerManagerStaysOutOfTheDesktopIntegrationRoots` pins that the Docker Manager is no Desktop integration root.
```

## Part D: the desktop app (`ui/`): live data, logs and terminal

Part D is the UI of Docker Manager phase 3 (Live): the stream client, sparklines and host gauges, the follow panels for logs and terminals in the container drawer and in the stack pane, a pane for external compose projects, live list updates, the new palette commands, the strings in all 16 locales, the Node and browser tests and the DOX guide. It replaces the one-shot log view of phase 1.

**Prerequisites.** Phase 2 is merged (`a80113379`). Parts A to C are **not** needed to build or test this part: the UI codes against the contract's routes and JSON, the Node tests use a fake API and a fake `EventSource` with fake timers, and the browser tests serve their own fake `/api/docker-manager/` (a hand-written `/stream` SSE, hand-written follow SSE streams and a terminal that echoes over a real WebSocket, `github.com/gorilla/websocket`, already in `go.mod`). `node_modules` must exist (it holds `rollup` for `npm run build:ui`); **never run `npm install` or `npm ci`** for this part. Headless Chrome is needed for the browser tests (`AURAGO_RUN_BROWSER_SMOKE=1`); on this Windows box run them with the sandbox off (`reference_chrome_launch_from_agent`; the repo-built test binary starts Chrome only from the Go build temp folder). Commands below are PowerShell from the repository root.

**How the code was verified.** Every task was applied, in order, to a scratch worktree of `a80113379` as one commit per task, and each of the 9 commits was checked in its own state: the Node test (`node scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`), `go test ./ui -run "TestDockerManager|TestDesktopDynamicI18nPrefixKeysExistInAllLanguages"`, `go vet ./ui` and `gofmt -l` of the touched Go files. `npm run build:ui` and `npm run check:ui` were run for the loader edit (D7: the generated `main.bundle.js` does not contain the loader, so nothing is regenerated) and at the end. From Task D8 on the four Docker Manager browser tests pass in headless Chrome (`TestDesktopDockerManagerBrowser` 18 s, `...EditorFallbackBrowser` 2 s, `...LiveBrowser` 4 s, `...FollowBrowser` 7 s); the whole `./ui` package fails only on the two known failures (`TestDashboardCardsFollowSectionPlacementAndAnatomy`, `TestFrontend_StaticI18nKeysExistInEnglishBundle` for the two `help.chromecast.*` keys). The expected outputs in the tasks are the real outputs of those runs; the failing runs are real too (each task's tests on top of the previous commit). The app was also driven in headless Chrome and screenshotted in a dark theme (Standard dark) and a light one (Fruity light): containers with sparklines and rail gauges, container logs, container terminal, stack overview with sparklines, stack logs with service chips and a notice, the external project pane, the paused-updates banner. That review changed three things, which are folded into the tasks they belong to: a young series fills the sparkline instead of hugging its right edge (D1), the paused banner uses the info glyph (D6), the two wrappers of the drawer take no part in the layout (D7). After a cross-check against the real Part C routes nine corrections were folded into the tasks they belong to (a watchdog for a silent stream in D2, the reason `host_not_found` in D3, merged `not_followed` notices, a final 4xx diagnosis and service names in the notices in D4, the confirmed protected diagnosis and short ids in D5, short ids of the service rows, the cause of an ended stream and three more error sentences in D6). **Not run:** nothing in this part talked to a real server, a real Engine or a real terminal; the fakes follow `CONTRACT.md`. The points a cross-check against Parts A to C has to confirm are listed under "What the UI expects from the backend".

**Conventions.** Files in a Windows working tree have CRLF line endings; the Edit tool matches the old texts regardless. None of the code contains a backslash followed by `u`, so the Write and Edit tools do not alter it. Helper scripts go to `disposable\` (never staged); every commit adds exact paths. The strings come in one rows file per task (`[key, en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pt, pl, sv, da, no, cs, el, hi, ja, zh]`) merged by a script that checks the text count and the `{{placeholders}}` of every row (and, in D6, removes four keys). All 16 locales get real translations; **Greek, Hindi, Japanese and Chinese were written without a native reviewer**, like the strings of phases 1 and 2 (have a native speaker look at `el`, `hi`, `ja`, `zh` before a release). The German strings use the formal "Sie" like the existing ones.

**Order and what runs when.** D1 and D2 add pure modules with their Node tests. D3 extends the store (live stream, safety poll, reloads, disk usage, external project, diagnosis) and removes its one-shot log loader. D4 and D5 add the log and terminal panels. D6 changes the builders and adds the panes module. D7 wires the loader and the stylesheet. D8 swaps the composition root and brings the browser tests. D9 is the DOX guide. **The app is not runnable between D3 and D8** (the old root still calls the removed `store.loadLogs` and the old string drawer); the Node tests and the Go guards are the check in between, and each task states exactly what they print.

### Deviations from the contract

1. **One more module, `docker-manager-panes.js` (`DockerManagerPanes`).** The contract lists four new modules. The glue that mounts the log and terminal panels in the container drawer, the stack pane and the project pane, fills the load cells in place and collects the visible containers does not belong into the root (which would pass 1100 lines) nor into the panels. It loads after `terminal` and before `palette`: `model, stack-model, charts, store, live, views, stacks, editor, ops, logs, terminal, panes, palette, dialogs, newstack, docker-manager.js`, after the two xterm scripts and `xterm.css` (no WebGL renderer).
2. **A refused handshake or stream is explained by a plain GET.** A browser hides the HTTP answer of a refused WebSocket handshake and of a failed `EventSource` request. After a failure the panel asks `store.diagnose(path)`, which repeats the same URL as a plain `GET` (8 s timeout) and reads the JSON error. For the terminal this carries the whole protected-confirm flow (`409 container_protected_confirmation_required` opens the confirmation and connects again with `?confirm=protected`); for the follow routes any 4xx answer and the codes `docker_disabled`, `docker_hosts_unavailable` and `stacks_unavailable` end the retries; a 5xx answer, a timeout and a network failure are tried again. The diagnosis of a confirmed protected container carries `?confirm=protected`. **Part C must answer the terminal route's checks (origin, `read_only`, `helper_container`, `container_not_running`, protection) before the `400 websocket_required` test**, as the existing `/api/containers` terminal does for its non-upgrade check, otherwise the UI can only say "could not be opened". A `429 too_many_streams` or `502` on the terminal that comes after the upgrade check is not visible to the UI either (generic message).
3. **Reconnect of a log follow:** `tail=5000&since=<RFC 3339 time of the newest line>`. The contract names `since` but not what `tail` means with it; a `tail=0` would lose the lines of the gap. The UI drops lines older than `since` and exact repeats of lines at `since` (same container, service, time and text), so the server may apply `since` inclusively.
4. **Stats subscriptions send 12-character ids** (the first 12 characters of the container list's `id`), never names.
5. **The 60 s safety poll is a staleness rule on the 5 s tick:** a host whose stream status is `live` is skipped by the tick until its data is 57.5 s old; every other host (connecting, paused, unreachable, stream down) is polled on every tick as before. The 300 ms "debounce" of the reloads is a coalescing window (the first container event of a host starts it, later events join it), so a container in a restart loop cannot starve the update. Image, volume and network events do not reload anything (no view needs them before phase 4).
6. **External project rows open a pane** (tabs Overview and Logs; start, stop, restart as before) instead of filtering the Containers section; the old effect is a button "Show in Containers" in the pane.
7. **Read-only** means `!store.canMutate()`: the desktop's read-only mode and `docker.readonly` both hide the terminal (message instead) and the palette's Terminal commands; logs and stats work in both.
8. **`Ctrl+]` also matches `event.code === 'BracketRight'`** (layouts where `]` needs AltGr). Closing a panel, or picking another container, sends the text frame `{"type":"end"}` before the WebSocket closes, so the shell does not stay behind in the container.
9. **The phase 1 one-shot log view is gone from the UI:** `store.loadLogs`, `state.detail.logs`, `Store.LOG_TAILS`, `views.logsPanel` and the strings `logs_reload`, `logs_loading`, `logs_failed`, `logs_empty` are removed; `GET .../logs` without `follow` stays on the server for other callers. `views.drawer(snap, row)` returns `{top, body, live}` instead of one string. The Containers table has a sixth column (CPU / Memory) and its column widths changed.
10. **The watchdog for a silent stream asks before it declares the stream dead.** EventSource hides the comment-line heartbeats, so a stream that only carries heartbeats (nothing subscribed, nothing happening) never delivers a message; closing it after 45 s would make every idle stream flap between "live" and "paused". After three heartbeats (at least 45 s) without a message the client sends its wish again with `PUT /stream/subscriptions`: an answer keeps the stream, a `404 stream_not_found`, any other error or no answer within 10 s closes it and the backoff reopens it. A dead connection is thereby found by the server's own bookkeeping (it drops a client whose heartbeat write fails). Reading the window as `max(45 s, 3 x heartbeat_ms)` follows the `hello`.
11. **Diagnosis answers:** any 4xx answer of the plain GET ends the retries of a log follow (a 5xx answer, a timeout and a network failure are tried again); the diagnosis of a confirmed protected container carries `?confirm=protected`; the server's `not_followed` notices (one per failed container, one for the services the budget left out) are one line with every service once; `attached` and `detached` name the first service, else the container id.

### What the UI expects from the backend (Parts A to C)

| Call or message | What the UI does with it |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /stream` (SSE) | `hello {stream_id, limits}` starts the subscription; `host_status {host, state, reason, t}` (`live`, `paused`, `unreachable`, `connecting`; a stream with no message for three heartbeats, at least 45 s, is asked with a repeated `PUT` before it counts as dead); `event` (only `type: "container"` reloads the host, `project` selects the open stack); `resync {host, reason}`; `stats {host, id, point}`, `stats_history {host, id, points}` (replaces the ring), `stats_gone`; `host_stats`; `operation {host, operation}` (through `trackOperation`); `dropped` (reconnect). A stats point with `cpu: -1` is a gap in the sparkline and a dash in the text; `0` is a value. Statuses: `paused` and `unreachable` poll every 5 s again, `unreachable` shows no extra banner when the host has its own. |
| `PUT /stream/subscriptions` | Body `{stream_id, hosts, stats, host_stats}`; only sent when the wish changed (250 ms debounce), and again after every `hello`. `404 stream_not_found` reconnects; any other failure is retried 3 times after 3 s. `rejected` entries are kept (`store.liveRejected()`). |
| `GET /hosts/{h}/df[?refresh=1]` | `{df: {images, containers, volumes, build_cache, total}, fetched_at, cached}`; read on selecting a single host, again after 5 minutes, and by the refresh button (`refresh=1`); 65 s browser timeout. |
| `GET .../containers/{ref}/logs?follow=1&tail=N[&since=T]`, `.../stacks/{name}/logs?...`, `.../projects/{project}/logs?...` | `lines {lines:[{t,s,text,trunc,svc,ctr}]}`, `notice {code,message,services,container}` (`not_followed`, merged into one line with every service once, whether the server sends one per container or one for the budget; `attached` and `detached`, named by the first service or else the container; `truncated_history`), `end {reason: ended\|error, code, message}`. After `end` with `host_unreachable`, `timeout`, `docker_error`, `internal_error` or `network` the panel follows again by itself (backoff 1 s to 15 s, five tries); every other `end` waits for the Reconnect button. A dropped connection resumes with `since`. |
| `GET .../containers/{ref}/terminal[?confirm=protected]` | WebSocket, binary frames in both directions, text frames `{"type":"resize","cols","rows"}` and `{"type":"end"}` from the browser. `ref` is the container's `full_id`. |

What a cross-check of Parts A to C has to confirm: (a) the hub sends the current `host_status` of every host right after a subscription is accepted (without it a host stays `connecting` and is polled every 5 s, which degrades gracefully) and `stats_history` before the first `stats` of a container with a ring; (b) the terminal route checks before the upgrade check (Deviation 2); (c) `since` is applied inclusively or exclusively, either way works; (d) `end:error` carries a `code` from the error table; (e) a project or stack follow reports the services it could not follow in one `notice not_followed` (replaces the previous one in the UI); (f) the subscription accepts container ids of 12 to 64 hex characters (the browser fixture uses readable fake ids because the phase 1 and 2 fixture always did; the UI does not validate them).

### Open questions

1. Does the hub answer `PUT /stream/subscriptions` for a host the user lost access to with `rejected` or with a 400? The UI shows nothing for rejected hosts (they stay `connecting` and are polled).
2. Should a `429 too_many_streams` on the terminal route come before the upgrade check, so that the UI can name it? It would need the slot to be taken before the upgrade; today the UI says "may have no free connection".
3. The image, volume and network events are ignored until phase 4 needs them.
4. The Node test script grew from 1349 to 2237 lines (charts, live client, store, logs model, views, panes). Splitting it into one script per area (they share one fixture and fake api) is a follow-up.
5. NVDA and keyboard-only passes of the terminal and the log panel (`role="log"`, `aria-live="off"`, no announcement per line) are open for the acceptance on the real server.

### Task D1: Charts: sparklines, gauges, bytes and percent (pure)

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-charts.js`

`docker-manager-charts.js` returns SVG and HTML strings for the live numbers and knows no colour: the shapes carry classes and `data-level` attributes that the stylesheet (D7) paints from tokens. `sparkline(points, {width, height, max, window, label})` draws a polyline and an area for runs of known values (null, NaN and the server's -1 are gaps; 0 is a value), right-aligned in a window of slots; `gauge(value, max, {label, unit, text})` is a labelled meter (`ok`, `warn` from 75 %, `bad` from 90 %, `plain` without a ceiling, `none` for an unknown value) whose bar is an SVG, so no inline style is needed; `loadCell(points)` is the two-line cell of a container (CPU and memory: the latest value as text next to a sparkline). The window of `loadCell` is as wide as the points seen so far (at least 10 slots, at most 60): a screenshot review showed that a fixed 60-slot window leaves a young series as a few ticks at the right edge. `bytes`, `percent`, `series` and `rate` (bytes per second between the last two points of a cumulative counter) are the helpers.

```js
/* Docker Manager charts: pure functions that return SVG or HTML strings for the live numbers (sparklines, gauges, byte and
   percent text). A classic script (window.DockerManagerCharts) with no DOM work at load, so that
   scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs can run it in a Node vm. Nothing here knows a colour: the shapes carry classes and
   data-level attributes and docker-manager's stylesheet paints them from theme tokens. Unknown values (-1 from the
   server, NaN, null) are gaps in a sparkline and an en dash in text. */
(function () {
    'use strict';

    const UNITS = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB'];
    const DASH = '–';
    const known = value => typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0;
    // null, undefined and blank strings are unknown, not zero (Number(null) is 0).
    const num = value => (typeof value === 'number' ? value : typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() !== '' ? Number(value) : NaN);
    const round = value => Math.round(value * 100) / 100;
    const attr = value => String(value == null ? '' : value).replace(/[&<>"']/g, ch => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&#39;' }[ch]));
    const fixed = (value, digits, lang) => {
        try { return value.toLocaleString(lang || undefined, { minimumFractionDigits: digits, maximumFractionDigits: digits }); } catch (error) { return value.toFixed(digits); }
    };

    // 1536 -> "1.5 KB"; 2147483648 -> "2.0 GB"; unknown or negative -> en dash. Two significant digits from 10 upwards.
    function bytes(n, lang) {
        let value = num(n);
        if (!known(value)) return DASH;
        let unit = 0;
        while (value >= 1024 && unit < UNITS.length - 1) { value /= 1024; unit += 1; }
        return (unit === 0 ? String(Math.round(value)) : fixed(value, value >= 10 ? 0 : 1, lang)) + ' ' + UNITS[unit];
    }

    // 0.03 -> "0%"; 3.2 -> "3.2%"; 42.4 -> "42%"; unknown (-1 from the server) -> en dash.
    function percent(n, lang) {
        const value = num(n);
        if (!known(value)) return DASH;
        if (value < 0.05) return '0%';
        return (value < 10 ? fixed(value, 1, lang) : fixed(Math.round(value), 0, lang)) + '%';
    }

    // One number per sample of a StatsPoint series ("cpu", "mem", ...); anything that is not a known number becomes null.
    const series = (points, key) => (Array.isArray(points) ? points : []).map(point => (point && known(point[key]) ? point[key] : null));

    // Bytes per second of a cumulative counter ("net_rx") between the last two points; 0 after a counter reset, null without two points.
    function rate(points, key) {
        const list = Array.isArray(points) ? points : [];
        if (list.length < 2) return null;
        const a = list[list.length - 2], b = list[list.length - 1];
        const seconds = (Number(b && b.t) - Number(a && a.t)) / 1000;
        if (!(seconds > 0) || !known(a[key]) || !known(b[key])) return null;
        return b[key] >= a[key] ? (b[key] - a[key]) / seconds : 0;
    }

    // An inline SVG polyline of `points` (numbers; null or negative = gap), right-aligned in a window of `window` slots (default:
    // as many as there are points) and scaled to `max` (default: the highest value). With a `label` the SVG is an image for
    // assistive technology; without it, it is decorative.
    function sparkline(points, o) {
        const opt = o || {}, width = Number(opt.width) || 80, height = Number(opt.height) || 20, margin = 1.5;
        const values = (Array.isArray(points) ? points : []).map(value => (known(value) ? value : null));
        const slots = Math.max(Number(opt.window) || values.length, values.length, 2), offset = slots - values.length;
        const present = values.filter(value => value !== null);
        let max = Number(opt.max);
        if (!(max > 0)) max = present.length ? Math.max.apply(null, present) : 0;
        if (!(max > 0)) max = 1;
        const x = index => round(margin + (offset + index) * (width - 2 * margin) / (slots - 1));
        const y = value => round(height - margin - Math.min(value, max) / max * (height - 2 * margin));
        const runs = [];
        let run = [];
        values.forEach((value, index) => {
            if (value === null) { if (run.length) runs.push(run); run = []; } else run.push([x(index), y(value)]);
        });
        if (run.length) runs.push(run);
        const base = round(height - margin);
        let line = '', area = '';
        for (const part of runs) {
            line += 'M' + part.map(point => point[0] + ' ' + point[1]).join('L') + (part.length === 1 ? 'L' + part[0][0] + ' ' + part[0][1] : '');
            if (part.length > 1) area += 'M' + part[0][0] + ' ' + base + 'L' + part.map(point => point[0] + ' ' + point[1]).join('L') + 'L' + part[part.length - 1][0] + ' ' + base + 'Z';
        }
        const label = String(opt.label || '');
        const head = '<svg class="dm-spark' + (runs.length ? '' : ' is-empty') + '" viewBox="0 0 ' + width + ' ' + height + '" width="' + width + '" height="' + height + '" preserveAspectRatio="none" focusable="false"'
            + (label ? ' role="img" aria-label="' + attr(label) + '"' : ' aria-hidden="true"') + '>';
        if (!runs.length) return head + '<path class="dm-spark-base" d="M' + margin + ' ' + base + 'H' + (width - margin) + '"/></svg>';
        return head + (area ? '<path class="dm-spark-area" d="' + area + '"/>' : '') + '<path class="dm-spark-line" d="' + line + '"/></svg>';
    }

    // A labelled meter. `o.unit` is "percent" (value 0..100) or "bytes"; `o.text` replaces the generated value text. Without a
    // positive `max` (the Docker disk gauge: Docker's own usage has no ceiling) there is no bar, only label and value.
    // data-level is ok, warn (75 %), bad (90 %), plain (no ceiling) or none (unknown value).
    function gauge(value, max, o) {
        const opt = o || {}, label = String(opt.label || ''), lang = opt.lang;
        const v = known(num(value)) ? num(value) : NaN, m = Number(max), ceiling = m > 0 && Number.isFinite(m);
        const ratio = Number.isFinite(v) && ceiling ? Math.min(1, v / m) : 0;
        const level = !Number.isFinite(v) ? 'none' : !ceiling ? 'plain' : ratio >= 0.9 ? 'bad' : ratio >= 0.75 ? 'warn' : 'ok';
        let text = opt.text != null ? String(opt.text) : '';
        if (!text) {
            if (!Number.isFinite(v)) text = DASH;
            else if (opt.unit === 'percent') text = percent(v, lang);
            else if (opt.unit === 'bytes') text = bytes(v, lang) + (ceiling ? ' / ' + bytes(m, lang) : '');
            else text = fixed(v, 0, lang);
        }
        const head = '<div class="dm-gauge-head"><span class="dm-gauge-label">' + attr(label) + '</span><span class="dm-gauge-value">' + attr(text) + '</span></div>';
        const bar = ceiling && Number.isFinite(v)
            ? '<svg class="dm-gauge-bar" viewBox="0 0 100 4" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><rect class="dm-gauge-track" width="100" height="4"/><rect class="dm-gauge-fill" width="' + round(ratio * 100) + '" height="4"/></svg>'
            : '';
        const a11y = bar
            ? ' role="meter" aria-label="' + attr(label) + '" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="' + round(m) + '" aria-valuenow="' + round(v) + '" aria-valuetext="' + attr(text) + '"'
            : ' role="group" aria-label="' + attr(label + ': ' + text) + '"';
        return '<div class="dm-gauge" data-level="' + level + '"' + a11y + '>' + head + bar + '</div>';
    }

    // The two lines of a container's load cell (CPU, memory) for a StatsPoint series: the latest value as text next to a sparkline.
    // The CPU line scales to at least 10 %, so an idle container shows a flat line instead of noise. The window is as wide as the points
    // seen so far, at least 10 slots and at most 60 (the ring), so a young series fills the sparkline instead of hugging its right edge.
    // '' without points.
    function loadCell(points, o) {
        const opt = o || {}, list = Array.isArray(points) ? points : [];
        const last = list[list.length - 1];
        if (!last) return '';
        const cpu = series(list, 'cpu'), mem = series(list, 'mem');
        const cpuMax = Math.max(10, Math.max.apply(null, cpu.filter(value => value !== null).concat([0])));
        const line = (text, spark) => '<span class="dm-load-line"><span class="dm-load-val">' + attr(text) + '</span>' + spark + '</span>';
        const slots = opt.window || Math.min(60, Math.max(list.length, 10));
        return line(percent(last.cpu, opt.lang), sparkline(cpu, { width: 56, height: 16, max: cpuMax, window: slots }))
            + line(bytes(last.mem, opt.lang), sparkline(mem, { width: 56, height: 16, window: slots }));
    }

    window.DockerManagerCharts = { bytes, percent, series, rate, sparkline, gauge, loadCell };
})();
```

### Task D2: The live stream client (fake EventSource, fake timers)

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-live.js`

`DockerManagerLive.create({api, eventSource, now, setTimeout, clearTimeout, base, onConnection, onStatus, onEvent, onResync, onOperation, onStats, onHostStats, onSubscribed})` owns one `EventSource` on `/api/docker-manager/stream`. `hello` names the stream; `setWant({hosts, stats, hostStats})` normalises the wish (container ids cut to 12 characters, at most 50 per host and 20 hosts or the limits of `hello`) and sends it with `PUT /stream/subscriptions` 250 ms after the last change, at once after a `hello`, never when nothing changed and never an empty first wish. A broken stream is closed by the client (the browser's own retry would repeat the request without backoff) and reopened after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s; `hello` resets the delay and resubscribes. It keeps the last `host_status` of every host, a ring of 60 `StatsPoint`s per wanted container (older or repeated points are ignored, `stats_history` replaces the ring, `stats_gone` frees it) and the latest host stats. A `404 stream_not_found` and a `dropped` message reconnect; another subscription failure is retried three times. A watchdog (three heartbeats of the `hello`, at least 45 s, restarted by every message) covers a stream that goes silent: EventSource shows no comment lines, so a stream that only carries heartbeats looks the same as a dead one, and declaring it dead would make every idle stream flap. When the window runs out the client therefore sends its wish again; an answer keeps the stream, a `404`, any other error or no answer within 10 s closes it and the usual backoff reopens it. The EventSource, the api function, the clock and the timers are injected, so the Node test drives everything with fakes.

```js
// ---- live stream client: fake EventSource, fake api, fake timers ---------------------------------------------------------
function fakeTimers() {
    let clock = 0, seq = 0;
    const jobs = new Map();
    return {
        setTimeout: (fn, ms) => { const id = ++seq; jobs.set(id, { fn, at: clock + ms }); return id; },
        clearTimeout: id => { jobs.delete(id); },
        // Runs every timer due within `ms`, in order; a timer may arm the next one inside the window.
        advance(ms) {
            const end = clock + ms;
            for (;;) {
                const next = [...jobs].filter(([, job]) => job.at <= end).sort((a, b) => a[1].at - b[1].at)[0];
                if (!next) break;
                clock = next[1].at;
                jobs.delete(next[0]);
                next[1].fn();
            }
            clock = end;
        },
        now: () => clock,
        pending: () => jobs.size
    };
}
class FakeSource {
    constructor(url, list) { this.url = url; this.handlers = {}; this.closed = false; list.push(this); }
    addEventListener(type, fn) { (this.handlers[type] = this.handlers[type] || []).push(fn); }
    close() { this.closed = true; }
    emit(type, data) { for (const fn of this.handlers[type] || []) fn({ data: typeof data === 'string' ? data : JSON.stringify(data) }); }
    fail() { this.onerror?.(new Error('boom')); }
}
function liveHarness(extra = {}) {
    const timers = fakeTimers(), sources = [], puts = [], log = [];
    let putResult = () => ({ status: 'ok', accepted: { hosts: 1, stats: 0, host_stats: 0 }, rejected: [] });
    const api = async (url, init) => {
        puts.push({ url, method: init.method, body: JSON.parse(init.body) });
        return putResult(init);
    };
    const live = window.DockerManagerLive.create({
        api, eventSource: url => new FakeSource(url, sources), now: timers.now, setTimeout: timers.setTimeout, clearTimeout: timers.clearTimeout,
        onConnection: (up, info) => log.push(['connection', up, !!(info && info.resumed)]), onStatus: (host, status) => log.push(['status', host, status.state]),
        onEvent: ev => log.push(['event', ev.action]), onResync: ev => log.push(['resync', ev.host, ev.reason]), onOperation: (host, op) => log.push(['operation', host, op.id]),
        onStats: (host, id, ring) => log.push(['stats', host, id, ring.length]), onHostStats: (host, data) => log.push(['host_stats', host, data.cpu]),
        ...extra
    });
    return { live, timers, sources, puts, log, setPut: fn => { putResult = fn; } };
}
const hello = (source, id = 's'.repeat(32)) => source.emit('hello', { stream_id: id, heartbeat_ms: 15000, limits: { stats_ids: 50, hosts: 20 } });
const point = (t, cpu = 1, mem = 100) => ({ t, cpu, mem, mem_limit: 1000, net_rx: 0, net_tx: 0, blk_r: 0, blk_w: 0, pids: 1 });
```

```js
/* Docker Manager live stream: the client of GET /api/docker-manager/stream. One EventSource per app window. The first message
   (hello) names the stream; what the window wants to hear about (hosts for events and status, containers for 3 s stats, hosts
   for the rail gauges) goes to PUT /stream/subscriptions, debounced by 250 ms and sent again after every reconnect, because a
   new stream starts with an empty subscription. A broken stream is closed by this module (the browser's own retry would repeat
   the request without backoff) and opened again after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s. It keeps the last status of every host, a ring of
   60 StatsPoints per container and the latest host stats, and hands every message to the callbacks. A stream that stays silent for
   three heartbeats (at least 45 s; EventSource shows no comment lines, so a stream that only carries heartbeats looks the same) is
   not given up at once: the client sends its wish again, and only a server that no longer knows the stream, an error or no answer
   within 10 s counts as a dead connection. A classic script
   (window.DockerManagerLive) with no DOM work at load; the EventSource, the api function, the clock and the timers are injected so
   that scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs can drive it with fakes. */
(function () {
    'use strict';

    const BASE = '/api/docker-manager';
    const DEBOUNCE_MS = 250;
    const BACKOFF_MS = [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 30000];
    const RETRY_PUT_MS = 3000;
    const MAX_PUT_RETRIES = 3;
    const RING = 60;
    const DEFAULT_LIMITS = { stats_ids: 50, hosts: 20 };
    const WATCH_MIN_MS = 45000;
    const WATCH_FACTOR = 3;
    const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;

    const array = value => (Array.isArray(value) ? value : []);
    const text = value => (value == null ? '' : String(value));
    const unique = list => [...new Set(list)];
    const parse = data => { try { const value = JSON.parse(data); return value && typeof value === 'object' ? value : null; } catch (error) { return null; } };

    function create(options) {
        const o = options || {};
        const model = window.DockerManagerModel;
        const base = o.base || BASE;
        const api = o.api;
        const openSource = o.eventSource;
        const setT = typeof o.setTimeout === 'function' ? o.setTimeout : (fn, ms) => setTimeout(fn, ms);
        const clearT = typeof o.clearTimeout === 'function' ? o.clearTimeout : id => clearTimeout(id);
        const now = typeof o.now === 'function' ? o.now : () => Date.now();
        const call = (name, ...args) => {
            if (typeof o[name] !== 'function') return;
            try { o[name](...args); } catch (error) { console.error('Docker Manager live:', error); }
        };

        let source = null, streamId = '', connected = false, failed = false, stopped = true, failures = 0, generation = 0, putRetries = 0;
        let retryTimer = 0, putTimer = 0, watchTimer = 0, watchMs = WATCH_MIN_MS, sending = false, dirty = false, limits = Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_LIMITS);
        let want = { hosts: [], stats: {}, host_stats: [] }, wantSig = '', sentSig = '', rejected = [], accepted = null;
        const statuses = new Map(), rings = new Map(), hostStats = new Map();

        const ringKey = (host, id) => host + '/' + id;
        const wantsId = (host, id) => array(want.stats[host]).includes(id);

        // ---- what the window wants -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

        // input = {hosts: [id], stats: {host: [container id]}, hostStats: [id]}. Container ids are cut to 12 characters (the
        // server's short id), lists keep their order up to the limits of the stream, and the signature sorts them so that the
        // same wish in another order sends nothing.
        function normalize(input) {
            const i = input || {};
            const hosts = unique(array(i.hosts).map(text).filter(Boolean)).slice(0, limits.hosts);
            const stats = {};
            for (const host of Object.keys(i.stats || {})) {
                const ids = unique(array(i.stats[host]).map(id => text(id).slice(0, 12)).filter(Boolean)).slice(0, limits.stats_ids);
                if (ids.length) stats[host] = ids;
            }
            return { hosts, stats, host_stats: unique(array(i.hostStats || i.host_stats).map(text).filter(Boolean)).slice(0, limits.hosts) };
        }
        const signature = value => JSON.stringify({
            h: value.hosts.slice().sort(), s: Object.keys(value.stats).sort().map(host => [host, value.stats[host].slice().sort()]), g: value.host_stats.slice().sort()
        });
        const isEmpty = value => !value.hosts.length && !Object.keys(value.stats).length && !value.host_stats.length;

        function setWant(input) {
            const next = normalize(input), sig = signature(next);
            if (sig === wantSig) return;
            want = next;
            wantSig = sig;
            putRetries = 0;
            for (const key of [...rings.keys()]) {
                const at = key.lastIndexOf('/');
                if (!wantsId(key.slice(0, at), key.slice(at + 1))) rings.delete(key);
            }
            if (connected) schedulePut(DEBOUNCE_MS);
        }

        function schedulePut(delay) {
            clearT(putTimer);
            putTimer = setT(() => { putTimer = 0; void put(); }, delay);
        }

        async function put() {
            if (stopped || !connected || !streamId || wantSig === sentSig) return;
            if (sending) { dirty = true; return; }
            if (isEmpty(want) && sentSig === '') { sentSig = wantSig; return; }
            sending = true;
            dirty = false;
            const mine = generation, sig = wantSig, body = Object.assign({ stream_id: streamId }, want);
            try {
                const answer = await api(base + '/stream/subscriptions', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(body) });
                if (mine !== generation) return;
                sentSig = sig;
                putRetries = 0;
                rejected = array(answer && answer.rejected);
                accepted = (answer && answer.accepted) || null;
                call('onSubscribed', { accepted, rejected });
            } catch (error) {
                if (mine !== generation) return;
                const info = model.normalizeError(error);
                if (info.code === 'stream_not_found') failure();
                else if (info.code !== 'aborted' && putRetries < MAX_PUT_RETRIES) { putRetries += 1; dirty = true; }
            } finally {
                if (mine === generation) {
                    sending = false;
                    if (dirty && !stopped && connected) schedulePut(putRetries ? RETRY_PUT_MS : 0);
                }
            }
        }

        // ---- connection ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

        // Every message (not the comment heartbeats, which EventSource hides) starts the window again. When it runs out the client
        // asks the server whether it still has the stream, by sending the wish again: an answer keeps the stream, a 404, any other
        // error or no answer within 10 s means the connection is dead.
        function armWatchdog() {
            clearT(watchTimer);
            watchTimer = 0;
            if (stopped || !connected) return;
            watchTimer = setT(() => { watchTimer = 0; void probe(); }, watchMs);
        }
        async function probe() {
            if (stopped || !connected || !streamId) return;
            const mine = generation, controller = typeof AbortController === 'function' ? new AbortController() : null;
            const timeout = setT(() => { if (controller) controller.abort(); }, PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS);
            try {
                await api(base + '/stream/subscriptions', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ stream_id: streamId }, want)), signal: controller ? controller.signal : undefined });
                if (mine === generation) armWatchdog();
            } catch (error) {
                if (mine === generation) failure();
            } finally { clearT(timeout); }
        }

        function closeSource() {
            if (!source) return;
            const old = source;
            source = null;
            try { old.close(); } catch (error) { /* already closed */ }
        }

        // The stream broke or the server dropped us: forget the stream, tell the callbacks and try again after the next delay.
        function failure() {
            const was = connected;
            closeSource();
            generation += 1;
            sending = false;
            dirty = false;
            clearT(putTimer);
            putTimer = 0;
            clearT(watchTimer);
            watchTimer = 0;
            connected = false;
            failed = true;
            streamId = '';
            sentSig = '';
            statuses.clear();
            if (stopped) return;
            const delay = BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(failures, BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)];
            failures += 1;
            clearT(retryTimer);
            retryTimer = setT(() => { retryTimer = 0; connect(); }, delay);
            if (was || failures === 1) call('onConnection', false, { failed: true });
        }

        function connect() {
            if (stopped || source) return;
            if (typeof openSource !== 'function') return;
            let next;
            try { next = openSource(base + '/stream'); } catch (error) { failure(); return; }
            source = next;
            const on = (type, handler) => next.addEventListener(type, event => {
                if (source !== next || stopped) return;
                const data = parse(event && event.data);
                if (data) { armWatchdog(); handler(data); }
            });
            on('hello', data => {
                streamId = text(data.stream_id);
                limits = Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_LIMITS, data.limits || {});
                const resumed = failed;
                watchMs = Math.max(WATCH_MIN_MS, WATCH_FACTOR * (Number(data.heartbeat_ms) || 0));
                connected = true;
                failed = false;
                failures = 0;
                sentSig = '';
                rejected = [];
                accepted = null;
                armWatchdog();
                call('onConnection', true, { resumed });
                // The limits may be lower than assumed: sign the wish again against them.
                const again = normalize(want);
                want = again;
                wantSig = signature(again);
                if (!isEmpty(want)) void put();
            });
            on('host_status', data => {
                const host = text(data.host);
                if (!host) return;
                const status = { state: text(data.state), reason: text(data.reason), t: Number(data.t) || now() };
                statuses.set(host, status);
                call('onStatus', host, status);
            });
            on('event', data => call('onEvent', data));
            on('resync', data => call('onResync', data));
            on('operation', data => { if (data.operation) call('onOperation', text(data.host), data.operation); });
            on('stats', data => {
                const host = text(data.host), id = text(data.id), point = data.point;
                if (!point || !wantsId(host, id)) return;
                const key = ringKey(host, id);
                const ring = rings.get(key) || [];
                const last = ring[ring.length - 1];
                if (last && Number(point.t) <= Number(last.t)) return;
                ring.push(point);
                if (ring.length > RING) ring.splice(0, ring.length - RING);
                rings.set(key, ring);
                call('onStats', host, id, ring);
            });
            on('stats_history', data => {
                const host = text(data.host), id = text(data.id);
                if (!wantsId(host, id)) return;
                const ring = array(data.points).filter(point => point && typeof point === 'object').slice(-RING);
                rings.set(ringKey(host, id), ring);
                call('onStats', host, id, ring);
            });
            on('stats_gone', data => {
                const host = text(data.host), id = text(data.id);
                rings.delete(ringKey(host, id));
                call('onStats', host, id, []);
            });
            on('host_stats', data => {
                const host = text(data.host);
                if (!host) return;
                hostStats.set(host, data);
                call('onHostStats', host, data);
            });
            // The server closes a client whose buffer filled; the stream ends, and the reconnect resubscribes.
            on('dropped', () => failure());
            next.onerror = () => { if (source === next) failure(); };
        }

        function start() {
            if (!stopped) return;
            stopped = false;
            failures = 0;
            connect();
        }
        function stop() {
            if (stopped) return;
            stopped = true;
            clearT(retryTimer);
            clearT(putTimer);
            clearT(watchTimer);
            retryTimer = putTimer = watchTimer = 0;
            closeSource();
            generation += 1;
            sending = false;
            dirty = false;
            connected = false;
            failed = false;
            streamId = '';
            sentSig = '';
            statuses.clear();
            hostStats.clear();
            rings.clear();
        }

        return {
            start, stop, setWant,
            connected: () => connected, failed: () => failed, streamId: () => streamId, limits: () => Object.assign({}, limits),
            status: host => statuses.get(host) || null, ring: (host, id) => rings.get(ringKey(host, id)) || [], hostStats: host => hostStats.get(host) || null,
            rejected: () => rejected.slice(), accepted: () => accepted, want: () => normalize(want)
        };
    }

    window.DockerManagerLive = { create, BACKOFF_MS, DEBOUNCE_MS, RING };
})();
```

### Task D3: The store follows the stream: safety poll, reloads, disk usage, external project, diagnosis

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-model.js`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-stack-model.js`
- Modify: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-store.js`
- Modify: `ui/lang/desktop/{cs,da,de,el,en,es,fr,hi,it,ja,nl,no,pl,pt,sv,zh}.json`

The store creates the live client when the window becomes visible and stops it when it is hidden (`setVisible`). `liveStatus(host)` is `live`, `paused`, `connecting` or `off`; `pollOnce` skips a `live` host until its data is 57.5 s old (the 5 s tick with a 60 s safety poll) and polls every other host on every tick. A container `event` or a `resync` of a host in scope is coalesced (300 ms) into one reload of its containers, of its stacks in the Stacks section and of the open stack when the event names its project or a resync says anything may have changed. `operation` messages go through `trackOperation`. `setLiveStats({host: [ids]})` is how the app says which containers are on screen; the store adds the hosts in scope and, under a single host, that host for the gauges. Stats and host stats reach `onStats` and `onHostStats` listeners and **never** `emit()`. `loadDf(host, {refresh})` reads `GET /hosts/{h}/df` (state `df[host]`), `diagnose(path)` repeats a failed stream URL as a plain GET (8 s) and returns the JSON error, `openProject/closeProject/setProjectTab` keep the pane of an external compose project (mutually exclusive with the stack pane). The one-shot log loader (`loadLogs`, `detail.logs`, `LOG_TAILS`) is removed: the Logs tab is a follow panel from D4 on. The stack model gains the tabs `logs` and `terminal` (and `PROJECT_TABS`), the palette gets Logs commands for stacks and containers and Terminal commands for running containers that are no helpers (only with the new optional data fields, so the phase 2 palette is unchanged), and the model gets `terminalState(container)` and the host reason `host_not_found` (a host deleted while it was watched; its sentence is the third string of this task).

```js
    assert.equal(n('GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/stacks/shop') - stackBase, 1);
    sources[0].emit('resync', { host: 'local', reason: 'reconnect' });
    timers.advance(400);
    await tick(); await tick();
    assert.equal(n('GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/stacks/shop') - stackBase, 2, 'a resync reloads the open stack too');
    store.closeStack();

    // operation messages join the drawer and are followed through their own stream
    sources[0].emit('operation', { host: 'local', operation: opFixture({ state: 'running' }) });
    eq([store.state.ops.length, store.state.ops[0].op.state, sources.filter(s => s.url.endsWith('/operations/op_a1/stream')).length], [1, 'running', 1]);

    // stats and host stats reach their own listeners and never repaint the app
    let repaints = 0;
    store.subscribe(() => { repaints += 1; });
    const seen = [];
    const off1 = store.onStats((host, id, points) => seen.push(['stats', host, id, points.length]));
    const off2 = store.onHostStats((host, data) => seen.push(['host', host, data.cpu]));
    store.setLiveStats({ local: ['abcdef012345ffff'], elsewhere: ['zzz'] });
    timers.advance(300);
    await tick();
    eq(api.calls.filter(call => call.method === 'PUT').pop().body.stats, { local: ['abcdef012345'] }, 'only containers of hosts in scope are subscribed, cut to the short id');
    repaints = 0;
    sources[0].emit('stats', { host: 'local', id: 'abcdef012345', point: point(1, 4) });
    sources[0].emit('host_stats', { host: 'local', t: 1, cpu: 7, ncpu: 2, mem_used: 1, mem_total: 2, running: 1, sampled: 1, partial: false });
    eq(seen, [['stats', 'local', 'abcdef012345', 1], ['host', 'local', 7]]);
    assert.equal(repaints, 0, 'stats do not repaint the app');
    eq([store.liveRing('local', 'abcdef012345').length, store.liveHostStats('local').cpu], [1, 7]);
    off1(); off2();
    sources[0].emit('stats', { host: 'local', id: 'abcdef012345', point: point(2, 5) });
    assert.equal(seen.length, 2, 'a removed listener hears nothing');

    // gauges are asked for under a single host
    store.setScope('local');
    timers.advance(300);
    await tick();
    eq(api.calls.filter(call => call.method === 'PUT').pop().body.host_stats, ['local']);
    store.setScope('all');
    await tick(); await tick();

    // paused host: the 5 s poll is back and the status says so
    sources[0].emit('host_status', { host: 'local', state: 'paused', reason: '', t: 9 });
    assert.equal(store.liveStatus('local'), 'paused');
    const pausedBase = n(C);
    store.pollOnce();
    await tick(); await tick();
    assert.equal(n(C) - pausedBase, 1, 'a paused host is polled on every tick again');
    sources[0].emit('host_status', { host: 'local', state: 'live', reason: '', t: 10 });

    // the stream breaks: every host is paused, and the reconnect reads everything once
    sources[0].fail();
    eq([store.state.live.failed, store.liveStatus('local'), store.liveStatus('h_nas')], [true, 'paused', 'paused']);
    const downBase = n(C);
    timers.advance(1001);
    assert.equal(sources.filter(s => s.url === B + '/stream').length, 2);
    hello(sources[sources.length - 1], 'r'.repeat(32));
    await tick(); await tick();
    eq([store.state.live.failed, store.state.live.connected, n(C) - downBase >= 1], [false, true, true], 'the reconnect reloads what may have changed meanwhile');

    // hiding the window ends the stream
    store.setVisible(false);
    assert.equal(sources[sources.length - 1].closed, true);
    eq([store.liveStatus('local'), store.state.live.connected], ['off', false]);
    store.dispose();
}

// ---- store: disk usage, external project, terminal diagnosis --------------------------------------------------------------
{
    let mode = 'ok';
    const df = { images: { count: 3, active: 2, size: 1000, reclaimable: 100 }, containers: { count: 2, active: 1, size: 10, reclaimable: 0 }, volumes: { count: 1, active: 1, size: 500, reclaimable: 0 }, build_cache: { count: 0, active: 0, size: 0, reclaimable: 0 }, total: 1510 };
    const api = fakeApi({
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts']: { hosts: [hostA, hostB] },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/containers']: { containers: [] }, ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/h_nas/containers']: { containers: [] },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/stacks']: listingBody([]), ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/h_nas/stacks']: listingBody([]), ['GET ' + B + '/operations']: { operations: [] },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/df']: () => { if (mode === 'fail') throw httpError(502, { code: 'host_unreachable', reason: 'timeout', message: 'slow' }); return { status: 'ok', df, fetched_at: '2026-10-28T10:00:00Z', cached: mode === 'cached' }; },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/containers/ruview/terminal']: () => { throw httpError(409, { code: 'container_protected_confirmation_required', owner: 'ruview', message: 'confirm' }); },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/containers/ro/terminal']: () => { throw httpError(403, { code: 'read_only', message: 'read only' }); },
        ['GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/containers/odd/terminal']: {}
    });
    const store = Store.create({ api, scope: 'local', section: 'containers', live: false });
    await store.refresh();
    const D = 'GET ' + B + '/hosts/local/df';
    eq([api.count(D), store.state.df.local.status, store.state.df.local.df.total, store.state.df.local.cached], [1, 'ok', 1510, false], 'a single host scope reads its disk usage once');
    await store.refresh();
    assert.equal(api.count(D), 1, 'a fresh reading is not read again');
    mode = 'cached';
    await store.loadDf('local', { refresh: true });
    eq([api.calls.filter(call => call.key === D).pop().url, store.state.df.local.cached], [B + '/hosts/local/df?refresh=1', true], 'the gauge refresh asks the server to read again');
    mode = 'fail';
    await store.loadDf('local', { refresh: true });
    eq([store.state.df.local.status, store.state.df.local.df.total, store.state.df.local.error.code, store.state.df.local.busy], ['ok', 1510, 'host_unreachable', false], 'a failed reading keeps the last numbers and records the error');
    store.setScope('all');
    const allBase = api.count(D);
    await store.refresh();
    assert.equal(api.count(D), allBase, 'all hosts have no gauge and read no disk usage');
    store.dispose();

    // the external project pane and the stack pane exclude each other; tabs are checked
    const store2 = Store.create({ api, live: false, scope: 'all' });
    await store2.refresh();
    store2.openProject('local', 'legacy', 'logs');
    eq([store2.state.project.key, store2.state.project.tab], ['x:local/legacy', 'logs']);
    store2.setProjectTab('compose');
    assert.equal(store2.state.project.tab, 'logs', 'an unknown tab is ignored');
    store2.openStack('local', 'shop', 'overview');
    eq([store2.state.project, store2.state.stack.key], [null, 'local/shop'], 'opening a stack closes the project pane');
    store2.openProject('local', 'legacy');
    eq([store2.state.stack, store2.state.project.tab], [null, 'overview'], 'opening a project closes the stack pane');
    store2.closeProject();
    assert.equal(store2.state.project, null);
    store2.dispose();

    // a refused terminal handshake is explained by a plain GET
    const store3 = Store.create({ api, live: false });
    const protectedInfo = await store3.diagnoseTerminal('local', 'ruview');
    eq([protectedInfo.code, protectedInfo.data.owner], ['container_protected_confirmation_required', 'ruview']);
    const readonlyInfo = await store3.diagnoseTerminal('local', 'ro');
    eq([readonlyInfo.code, store3.state.dockerReadonly], ['read_only', true], 'a read_only answer switches the app to read-only');
    assert.equal(await store3.diagnoseTerminal('local', 'odd'), null, 'an answer without an error is no diagnosis');
    store3.dispose();
}
```

Create `disposable\dm3-i18n\merge-docker-manager-live-i18n.mjs` (never committed; the later tasks use it again):

```js
// One-off helper, never committed: appends docker_manager.* keys to the sixteen ui/lang/desktop/<lang>.json files and removes keys
// that no code asks for any more.
// Usage: node merge-docker-manager-live-i18n.mjs <repo-root> <rows-a.mjs> [<rows-b.mjs> ...]
// A rows module exports ROWS (every row is [key, en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pt, pl, sv, da, no, cs, el, hi, ja, zh]) and optionally
// REMOVE (a list of keys). A row with another number of texts, a text whose {{placeholders}} differ from the English one, a key that
// exists already, a key listed twice or a key to remove that does not exist stops the script before anything is written.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const LANGS = ['en', 'de', 'es', 'fr', 'it', 'nl', 'pt', 'pl', 'sv', 'da', 'no', 'cs', 'el', 'hi', 'ja', 'zh'];
const [root, ...sources] = process.argv.slice(2);
const placeholders = text => [...String(text).matchAll(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g)].map(match => match[1]).sort().join(',');

const rows = [], remove = [];
for (const source of sources) {
    const module = await import(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(source)).href);
    rows.push(...(module.ROWS || []));
    remove.push(...(module.REMOVE || []));
}

const problems = [], seen = new Set();
const dir = path.join(root, 'ui', 'lang', 'desktop');
const existing = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, 'en.json'), 'utf8'));
for (const row of rows) {
    const [key, ...texts] = row;
    if (texts.length !== LANGS.length) { problems.push(key + ': ' + texts.length + ' texts, want ' + LANGS.length); continue; }
    if (seen.has(key)) problems.push(key + ': listed twice');
    seen.add(key);
    if (key in existing && !remove.includes(key)) problems.push(key + ': exists already');
    texts.forEach((text, index) => {
        if (!String(text).trim()) problems.push(key + ' [' + LANGS[index] + ']: empty');
        if (placeholders(text) !== placeholders(texts[0])) problems.push(key + ' [' + LANGS[index] + ']: placeholders differ from English');
    });
}
for (const key of remove) if (!(key in existing)) problems.push(key + ': cannot remove, not in en.json');
if (problems.length) { console.error(problems.join('\n')); process.exit(1); }

LANGS.forEach((lang, index) => {
    const file = path.join(dir, lang + '.json');
    const raw = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
    const eol = raw.includes('\r\n') ? '\r\n' : '\n';
    let lines = raw.split(/\r?\n/);
    if (remove.length) {
        const drop = new Set(remove.map(key => '  ' + JSON.stringify(key) + ':'));
        lines = lines.filter(line => ![...drop].some(prefix => line.startsWith(prefix)));
        // the last entry of the object must not end with a comma
        for (let i = lines.length - 1; i > 0; i -= 1) {
            if (lines[i].trim() === '}') { if (lines[i - 1].endsWith(',')) lines[i - 1] = lines[i - 1].slice(0, -1); break; }
        }
    }
    let body = lines.join(eol).replace(/\s+$/, '');
    if (!body.endsWith('}')) throw new Error(file + ' does not end with }');
    if (rows.length) {
        const add = rows.map(([key, ...texts]) => '  ' + JSON.stringify(key) + ': ' + JSON.stringify(texts[index]));
        body = body.slice(0, -1).replace(/\s+$/, '') + ',' + eol + add.join(',' + eol) + eol + '}';
    }
    const out = body + eol;
    JSON.parse(out);
    fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
});
console.log('appended ' + rows.length + ' keys, removed ' + remove.length + ', in ' + LANGS.length + ' files');
```

### Task D4: The log follow panel

**Files:**

- Modify (test): `scripts/test-docker-manager-ui.mjs`
- Modify (test): `ui/i18n_lint_test.go`
- Create: `ui/js/desktop/apps/docker-manager-logs.js`
- Modify: `ui/lang/desktop/{cs,da,de,el,en,es,fr,hi,it,ja,nl,no,pl,pt,sv,zh}.json`

`docker-manager-logs.js` has a pure part and the panel. `createModel` is a ring of 5000 lines with a filter by text and by service, the follow flag with the count of lines that arrived while it was off, the stderr flag, ANSI codes removed and a carriage-return progress bar reduced to its last state, `lastTime()` for `since` and a duplicate filter (`beginResume`) for what a reconnect repeats. `mergeNotice(list, notice)` keeps at most four notices and folds every `not_followed` notice (the server sends one per container whose history or follow failed and one for the services the stream budget left out) into one entry with every service once, and `noticeName` names the first service, else the container, for `attached` and `detached` (the message of the server is the hover detail of a line); `isFinalDiagnosis(info)` ends the retries after a failed request for any 4xx answer and for `docker_disabled`, `docker_hosts_unavailable` and `stacks_unavailable`, while a 5xx answer, a timeout and a network failure are tried again. `followUrl(target, {tail, since})` builds the three SSE URLs (container: 200 lines by default, stack and project: 100 per container; a reconnect asks for `tail=5000&since=...`). `create(deps).open(el, target, options)` builds the panel: one `EventSource` that follows only while the panel is active, lines appended in animation frames as DOM nodes (`textContent`, never HTML), follow/pause by scroll position with a "New lines: n" button, filter, service chips (stacks and projects), timestamps and wrap as `data-` switches, copy of the visible lines, clear, notices, the end message, a Reconnect button, backoff reconnect for a broken connection, and the plain-GET diagnosis for a request that failed before it opened. The panel is exercised by the browser tests of D8; the Node test covers the model and the URLs.
